author: aiteann
title: Shane Finan Furze Pavilion performance (2026)
content:
Artist Shane Finan performs a ritual at the (

Furze Pavilion

) (2026). In the project, Finan was exploring some of the folk histories and traditions surrounding the use of furze (gorse) in Ireland from the 16th to the 20th Century.


For the performance Shane sang the folk song

Cad é sin don té sin

 (

What is it to that person

), first written down in 1812. He created a dornóg, which is a rope glove made from grass rope to protect the hand while harvesting furze (gorse). He then walks and cuts some furze using the dornóg and a billhook. Reusing the glove, he undoes the rope and ties it to the cut furze; and brings it back with an untangled rope tied to the cut plant. The performance finishes with the gate outside the pavilion being sealed by the cut furze.


The video was recorded by Serhii Shapoval for Mermaid Arts Centre Bray. The project was supported by the Arts Council through the Wicklow Arts Office Strategic Projects Award.

title: Digitalzwang auf jobcenter.digital bringt erhebliche Probleme für Bürgergeld-Bezieher
content:
„

Viele Bezieher von Bürgergeld nutzen das Portal jobcenter.digital um einfacher und schneller mit ihrem Jobcenter zu kommunizieren und um vorab über Einladungen, Bescheide usw. informiert zu sein, ohne auf deren postalische Zusendung zu verzichten, da die Postzustellung erfahrungsgemäß nicht immer zuverlässig und pünktlich ist. Wer jobcenter.digital nutzen will, muss jedoch seit dem 18.11.2024 erklären, dass er auf die postalische Zustellung von sämtlichen Schriftstücken verzichtet. Ohne diese generelle Verzichtserklärung ist es nicht mehr möglich jobcenter.digital zu nutzen

…“

Beitrag von Ottokar vom 14.03.2025 auf gegen-hartz.de


 mit Informationen zur Rechtslage und praktischen Problemen und dazu:


Analoge Zugangswege zu Jobcentern sollen erhalten bleiben


„

Die Bundesregierung spricht sich dafür aus, analoge Zugangswege zu den Leistungen der Grundsicherung für Arbeitsuchende dauerhaft zu erhalten. Leistungsberechtigten dürften keine rechtlichen Nachteile entstehen, wenn sie nicht die digitalen Angebote nutzen. Dies geht aus der Antwort der Bundesregierung (

Drucksache 21/7276

 


) auf eine Kleine Anfrage der Fraktion Die Linke (

Drucksache 21/6621


) hervor. Zugleich räumt die Bundesregierung ein, dass es bei der Registrierung und Authentifizierung im Online-Portal der Bundesagentur für Arbeit (BA) wiederholt zu Schwierigkeiten gekommen ist. Insbesondere die nach einem Sicherheitsvorfall eingeführte verpflichtende Mehr-Faktor-Authentifizierung habe für zusätzliche Herausforderungen gesorgt. Um den Zugang zu erleichtern, hat die Bundesagentur für Arbeit nach eigenen Angaben den technischen Support ausgebaut und mit der „BA-Secure-App“ eine weitere Möglichkeit zur Anmeldung geschaffen

.“  Aus dem

Thomé Newsletter 28/2026 vom 23.08.2026


, siehe dazu auch:


Basta Erwerbsloseninitiative: „

Warum wir davon abraten ausschließlich digital mit dem #Jobcenter zu kommunizieren:


Der für uns zentrale Punkt, warum wir den digitalen Kontakt mit dem Jobcenter ablehen ist, daß die #Digitalisierung aller Lebensbereiche Menschen und menschliches Handeln überfüssig machen soll.


Dagegen haben wir etwas. Dazu kommen noch einige praktische Probleme mit der digitalen Plattform der #Jobcenter: Die Benutzung von „Jobcenter digital“ setzt oft neue Endgeräte (Computer, Handys oder Laptops) voraus. Die sind teuer und können sich viele von uns nicht leisten. Und nehme ich teil an der digitaler Kommunikation mit dem #Jobcenter, dann muss ich mich bereit erklären, nur noch digital mit der Behörde zu kommunizieren. Das Ding ist weder mehrsprachig, noch barrierefrei. Eine Verschlüsselung klappt nicht, gibt es nicht. Das Hochladen von Unterlagen haut oft nicht hin,


Die ganze Geschichte ist störanfällig. Der Stand des Antragsverfahren kann nicht vernünftig nachvollzogen werden und Unterlagen verschwinden trotzdem weiterhin, nur habe ich dann keine*n Zeug*in. Deshalb empfehlen wir euch weiter per Papier zu kommunizieren

.“

author: Joe Todd
title: Whatever Happened to the ‘Enough Is Enough’ Campaign?
content:
On Wednesday 7 September 2022, Glasgow’s Old Fruitmarket was packed out. Hundreds of people had queued around the block for the city’s biggest leftwing rally in years.


Mark Thomas, a local homelessness worker, remembered being excited.


“It was absolutely massive… It was something new,” he told Novara Media. “[The crowd] was a real mix. Young people who I’d never seen before.”


That September was the end of the UK’s

hot strike summer

. Inflation was skyrocketing, wages were collapsing and energy bills were set to triple. Hundreds of thousands had gone on strike: rail, mail, telecoms and port workers and more. Mick Lynch, the straight-talking former leader of the National Union of Rail, Maritime and Transport Workers (RMT), had spent the summer

going viral

, making the case for striking workers and skewering journalists on live TV.


Amid this crisis, a new campaign was born:

Enough Is Enough

.


Launched in August, Enough Is Enough promised to “turn anger” at the cost of living crisis “into action”. It was, by any measure, an overnight sensation.

150,000 people

 signed up on the first day alone;

450,000

 by a fortnight later. Tens of thousands attended rallies nationwide, wanting to hear how to join a political movement to “win back dignity for working class people”.


But just a few months later, Enough Is Enough went pretty much silent. No more rallies. No more speeches. Just the odd post from a Twitter account. The most dynamic new campaign on the UK left had disappeared – and no-one seemed to know why.


“It feels like a missed opportunity,” said Thomas. “I felt annoyed. What was the point? Was it just a mailing list?”


Four years on, Novara Media spoke to nine co-founders, coordinating group members, organisers and key stakeholders – some of whom chose not to be named to protect their professional relationships – to find out what happened. Their recollections paint a picture of overwhelm, strategic contradiction and a desire for total control. Enough Is Enough didn’t collapse by accident: it was undone by the very organisations that created it.

 


‘We had a platform to create solidarity.’


Wind back to February 2022, and the pressure on the government was building. Prime minister Boris Johnson was flailing in the aftermath of ‘partygate’. Keir Starmer, leader of the opposition, was busy purging the Labour left. There was a political vacuum – and the cost of living crisis was only intensifying.


Chris Webb, then head of communications at the Communication Workers Union (CWU), told Novara Media it was clear working people “were pissed off” and something needed to be done.


That spring, in London pubs and Manchester curry houses, a small group of people hatched a plan. Led by an initial coordinating group made up of Webb, Chloe Koffman (another former staffer at the CWU), Ronan Burtenshaw and Marcus Barnett (then both editors of the socialist magazine Tribune), a meeting was held in London with representatives from Unite and the GMB, as well as Labour councillors, the staffers of leftwing Labour MPs, and Acorn, the community union.


The group shared a sense of urgency about the need to address the cost of living crisis, as well as a desire to reboot Labour party politics. They also didn’t want to become “just another lefty cultural campaign,” according to another co-founder, who chose not to be named.


“The People’s Assembly [another campaign group] was putting on yellow jacket demonstrations in Liverpool that were attracting 25 people,” they told Novara Media.

Don’t Pay

, a campaign that signed up

more than 100,000 people

 to stop paying energy bills and was described by energy firm E.ON as an

“existential threat”

 to the sector was, they argued, also “going nowhere”.


The coordinating group soon agreed on some core demands for the campaign: a real pay rise, a cut in energy bills, an end to food poverty, decent homes for all, and a tax on the rich. What they didn’t have, however, was a collective vision for what the campaign would actually be.


According to one co-founder, Burtenshaw wanted “big names and big tweets” to build a media network, while representatives from trade unions wanted a “rally front” and a “massive defence force” for striking workers (Burtenshaw didn’t respond to requests for an interview). The Zionist gang that murdered Bernadotte, Lehi, was active from 1940 to 1948. In May 1948, most of the gang’s active members were inducted into the IDF and Lehi itself was formally dissolved. author: Black Freighter
title: Our Dogmatism and Theirs
content:
A Response to Kazi Tanvir Hossein’s ‘Bolshevik Confusion and the Theoretical Bankruptcy of Anarchists’; his article critiques the International Confederation of Labour on the basis of their solidarity work with a garment worker's union affiliated with the Communist Party of Bangladesh

Kazi Tanvir Hossein’s article ‘Bolshevik Confusion and the Theoretical Bankruptcy of Anarchists’ takes issue with a solidarity campaign conducted by the International Confederation of Labour with the Garments Workers’ Trade Union Centre (GWTUC) of Bangladesh over five years ago. His primary concern is GWTUC’s affiliation with the Communist Party of Bangladesh (CPB), arguing that “for anarchists to support or assist any Marxist-Leninist group essentially means directly opposing the core ideals and free thought of anarchism.” A critique of authoritarian socialism is necessary, but it shouldn’t lead us to create new certainties of our own. Anarchism is not a fixed doctrine; it is a living movement of the working class. In rejecting authoritarian socialism, we cannot withdraw from the struggle of workers who finds themselves (at least for now) within imperfect organisations.

To give some context of the situation, the ICL was approached in August 2020 with a call for solidarity with workers at Dragon Sweaters, a firm in Dhaka under the organisational reach of GWTUC. The ICL is a federation of anarcho-syndicalist and revolutionary syndicalist unions – a definition relevant to this discussion as it makes clear that the ICL is not an exclusively anarchist organisation. In its 2018 statutes, it lists solidarity as one of its core principles, “understood as mutual aid among all working people towards each other.”

The letter received by the ICL arrived in the context of Covid-19 lockdowns, detailing a decision by Dragon’s owners to terminate the majority of workers on their sites without outstanding employment entitlements (severance pay etc). The letter therefore appealed to the ICL to campaign on behalf of those workers against brands partnered with Dragon, including Primark, Zara and New Yorker. In announcing their campaign, the ICL also noted that the workers at Dragon were supported by Auraj, a Bangladeshi anarchist network.

After a brief but intense multinational effort, the ICL announced in December 2020 that the campaign was a success. The exact circumstances aren’t relevant to this discussion, but in January 2021 GWTUC General-Secretary Joly Talukder addressed a letter to the ICL and other supporting unions stating that international efforts “pushed the movement to the victory”. This success led to further collaboration between the ICL and GWTUC, including efforts to raise the Bangladeshi minimum wage for garment workers in 2023.

Hossein argues that the ICL’s decision to campaign and raise funds for GWTUC presents “a profound theoretical contradiction”, given the latter’s affiliation with the CPB:

“On one hand, Leninist parties believe in bureaucratic central leadership and the politics of state capture, while on the other hand, anarcho-syndicalist international networks fight for the establishment of a stateless, decentralized, and independent workers' federation. This contradiction is not merely theoretical; it severely damages the labor movement in practical terms as well.”

According to him, Leninism’s ideological dogmatism is among the “primary obstacles to human free intellect” . To free itself of all constraints, he writes that “kindling the flame of doubt is … the sole tool for liberating thought from any dogmatist and materialist shroud.” The problem with this line of reasoning is that anarchism is not just an abstract philosophical system, but a practical ethic of freedom based in material struggle.

Perhaps the most substantial question that Hossein raises is the level of organisational overlap between GWTUC and the CPB. Talukder and much of the union leadership also hold senior positions within the CPB, raising the legitimate question about whether solidarity with GWTUC strengthens the influence of the CPB. This possibility is not in itself sufficient grounds to condemn the ICL’s campaign, however. While GWTUC’s bargaining power has increased, there is no evidence to suggest that solidarity funds were misappropriated by the CPB’s political apparatus. The question Hossain should be asking is not whether GWTUC is affiliated with the CPB but whether the ICL’s solidarity is strengthening worker’s struggle or the party …

author: Joseph Lee
title: Living with drought has taught pastoralists lessons the world needs
content:
Cattle are a central part of the identity of Andrew Msami’s Maasai community in northeast Tanzania. Herd size determines social position, and many people keep all their wealth in livestock, not banks. But in recent years, Msami and others have been forced to sell the animals and buy goats, which can handle drought better but are less financially and culturally valuable. Msami says adapting to a shifting climate has been a part of Maasai life for generations, but recent conditions represent an existential threat.


“We have to adapt because it’s like desertification is attacking our identity,” Msami told Grist. “If you lose your identity, it means you have lost everything.”


The Maasai are pastoralists, a term that describes the roughly 500 million people around the world who tend herds of livestock like cattle, goats, and sheep. They often move with the animals as they seek grass and water. Because they live and work in places with arid conditions and extreme temperatures, they are particularly vulnerable to climate change. 


Around the world, drought and land degradation threaten rangelands, which make up roughly half of the planet’s landmass, and the pastoralists from Tanzania and Sudan to Nepal and Mongolia that rely on them. Desertification is occurring at 30 to 35 times the historical average, threatening even the most resilient communities. That’s on top of an influx of invasive species, extractive industries, tourists, and other threats. 


To address these overlapping crises, Msami and hundreds of other pastoralists are in Mongolia this week for the

United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification

, or UNCCD. They are calling for stronger protections for Indigenous pastoral traditions, greater access to funding and resources to combat the crisis, and official recognition that generations of experience living on increasingly marginal lands offers lessons for adapting to a hotter, drier world.


“We want to give the world a message that it’s not only the land that you will have to really look at,” said Msami, who is the program lead for the Pastoralists Indigenous Non-Governmental Organizations Forum, or

PINGOs Forum

, which is a network representing over 50 pastoralist organizations in Tanzania. “But you look at the people in that land, and maybe their lives should not be disturbed or sacrificed for the development of the world.” 


That message must first overcome a global environmental movement that has not always prioritized rangelands and the peoples who steward them. 


In 1992, world leaders gathered at the historic

United Nations Earth Summit

 in Brazil, where they identified three great environmental challenges: climate change, biodiversity loss, and desertification. Global conferences were established for each, creating a forum where the world would develop plans to tackle them. In the decades since, trillions of dollars have flowed toward the first two, while desertification has largely been relegated to a problem for the developing world to address.


“But now the history is catching them because when you look at Spain, France, even Sweden, all those countries, they have a bigger drought ever since the last two years,” said Hindou Oumarou Ibrahim, who is Mbororo from Chad and the first chair of the Indigenous peoples caucus at UNCCD. “So it is becoming a developed countries issue, and now they start paying more attention, but still it does not get the same attention on the level of political will or finance.”


Although this is the 17th meeting of the convention, Ibrahim described this year’s event as “unique, historic, and particular.” That is because it is the first with a formal caucus specifically for Indigenous peoples, something not found at the climate and biodiversity conferences. Because of that, Ibrahim and others consider this gathering a unique opportunity for Indigenous pastoralists to advocate for their rights and advance their goals on the international stage. 


Read Next


Indigenous cultural practices are a climate solution, report finds


Joseph Lee


The gathering also comes during the

United Nations’ International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists

, which Ibrahim said has had a positive impact on raising awareness of the challenges communities like his face and the contributions they are making to climate resilience.


Despite those signs of progress, attendees in Mongolia said that the Indigenous caucus has faced resistance. In the first week of the conference …

author: ROAPE
title: The murder of Professor Jason Arday
content:
On Sunday 16 August I joined the vigil for Professor Arday in London’s Trafalgar Square in the summer’s heat, packed tight with thousands of protestors marking their respect, holding bunches of flowers aloft, and placards reading, ‘Rest in Power Professor Jason Arday.’ Heads bowed, hundreds around me in tears – the words of his students unbearable, our anger craving a response. 


Professor Arday is dead. Murdered. Yet again another Black person has been killed – pilloried in a public execution orchestrated by a profoundly racist press, and organised fascists.


The vigil spoke to the structural racism that shaped Professor Arday’s life and death. I was struck by British MP Diane Abbott’s comments on the Black experience in the UK and the racism encountered daily. This daily experience is engrained in British institutions, the press and political life.


His family commented about the outpouring of grief and fury, describing their emotions: ‘The public cruelty Jason was subjected to was too much for any man to bear. The outpouring of love, support, and grief since his death means so much to us. Although it is bittersweet now, kindness is needed in life, not just in death.’


Bittersweet indeed – the kindness, support and grief were essential but too late. 


Professor Jason Arday – the Black professor of sociology at Cambridge University – was hounded to his death by a racist campaign to unseat him from his position. In the 22 days leading to his suicide, there were 249 articles in major newspapers in the UK, continual coverage on TV, radio and blogs. This had followed a repeated effort to undermine Arday since he became a professor at the university in 2023.


The noise from this pogrom – accusing him of plagiarism, lies, bombast, academic fakery – was overwhelming. Many people who should have known better joined the chorus. The UK’s mainstream liberal paper, 

The Guardian,

 

launched an investigation into Arday’s scholarship

. I encountered family members who joined in the chorus – denouncing Arday, ridiculing his claims, and his work.


On 5 August, Arday resigned from his post; the following week, on 14 August, he committed suicide. A man described by his students as ‘gentle’, ‘caring’, ‘compassionate’ and ‘inspiring’ was systematically broken – destroyed in a campaign which led directly to his suicide. 


Arday was murdered. 


This was the objective – Arday’s suicide was the logical outcome. Leading the recent crusade was the racist scholar, Nathan Cofnas, who published on his Substack the blog, ‘

DEI Fraud and Cover-Up at Cambridge

’, on 21 July 2026.  A vile man who targeted and conducted his own investigation into Arday’s work  – charging him with plagiarism, which confirmed Cofnas’ thesis that Black people are inferior, unworthy of senior academic positions. 


Cofnas is a symptom of our times. A marginal, bigoted voice that once would have remained largely undetected in the swamp is now amplified by a mainstream, racist agenda. In the global North, these voices have reached fever pitch – finding traction in a political climate that has seen right-wing governments elected, and racist policies normalised in daily political speech. 


To say these developments are worrying is a grotesque understatement – these are clarion signs of our current and deepening crisis, and the irredeemable racism of our political and economic system. This cannot be absorbed and understood simply as a British thing. We see the same tightening of the screw in the personal attacks on International Criminal Court judges and the normalisation of genocide.


There are three observations that I want to make in this piece. Firstly, I want to look at two political parallels –  one that prompted the global mass movement, Black Lives Matter, a few years ago, and the second when antisemitism was denounced by the French author Émile Zola at the end of the 19

th

 century. Finally, I want to say a few things about plagiarism and academia. 


On 25 May 2020 in Minneapolis, George Floyd was stopped by the police, then wrestled to the ground by police officer Derek Chauvin – clips of his slow death over nine minutes were beamed across the planet. Chauvin was later convicted of murder. George Floyd was choked to death by Chauvin, who pinned Floyd to the ground, as he died – filmed by the incredibly brave 17-year-old Darnella Frazie – he was heard saying,‘Mama, mama, mama’, ‘Momma, I love you,’ and ‘Momma! I’m through.’

author: webadmin
title: Leveret Hunting Underway Across The Country
content:
The recent conviction of packs such as the Stowe School Beagles, the Pipewell Foot Beagles and the Dorset & Somerset Bassets have highlighted the ongoing issue of illegal hare hunting.


But far from being deterred by their paltry fines, these and other packs will shortly be beginning their programme of illegal leveret hunting.


Low key: beaglers head out into the killing fields.


What Is Leveret Hunting?


As with fox hunting, beagles must be trained to hunt and kill their quarry. Leverets – young hares – present an easy target for the new and inexperienced hounds. The pack of beagles are taken to open fields and encouraged to search for hares and leverets. Unlike in main season hunting, the hunters do not want a long chase. They will even turn escaping leverets back towards the hounds to ensure a quick kill.


Leveret hunting usually takes place in September and early October but can start as soon as crops are cleared. The hunters meet early in the morning – from 6am onwards – because that is when the scent is best for new, inexperienced hounds and because the countryside is very quiet.


The Sandhurst & Aldershot Beagles keep a low profile.


“The Hare Hunters Equivalent of Cub Hunting”


Fox hunters have tried to rebrand their cub hunting as ’autumn’ hunting. However, beaglers recognise that hunting young hares is so horrendous that they simply deny it exists. A brief look at their literature – from the days when they were a little more open and honest – reveals otherwise:


“…young hounds should be allowed to get away on a well-grown leveret rather than an old, experienced hare.” –

‘Early Hunting Lessons’ chapter in ‘Beagling’ by J.C. Jeremy Hobson.


“…hounds are taken out in the early morning or late afternoon. This is for the hare hunters equivalent of cub hunting; some masters, in fact, call the period “leveret hunting.” –

‘Hunts and Countries’ chapter in ‘Beaglers’ by Jack Ivester Lloyd


“In order to get young hounds trained to hunt they start hunting in the very early morning or evening once the harvest is clear usually in August or September. They are accompanied only by invitation of the Master for this beagling equivalent of the foxhunter’s cub-hunting.” –

An Introduction To Beagling by Iain Clarke.


Typical leveret hunt meet: note hound trailer to the left.


What does it look like?


Obviously, a pack of small beagle hounds in the middle of a field is a give-away. There will be few people present as only the most trusted supporters are invited to attend these secret hunts. Don’t expect the hunters to be in uniform – they don’t usually wear this until the main season.


Stowe School Beaglers congratulate each other after tearing a hare to pieces.


What should I do if I see a suspected leveret hunt?


If it is safe to do so, filming the hunters will often be enough to stop them in their tracks. Try to film key individuals and their vehicles. Please then pass this information to the Hunt Saboteurs Association tip-off line on:

07443 148426

.


Hunting leverets with dogs is illegal so, if you believe a crime is in progress, call the police straight away.

Leveret Hunting Underway Across The Country

Hunt Saboteurs Association

title: Προσφυγικά Λ. Αλεξάνδρας: Η Ευρωπαϊκή Επιτροπή απαντά στις απειλές της Περιφέρειας Αττικής
content:
Σύνδεσμος δημοσίευσης:

Προσφυγικά Λ. Αλεξάνδρας: Η Ευρωπαϊκή Επιτροπή απαντά στις απειλές της Περιφέρειας Αττικής


ΔΕΛΤΙΟ ΤΥΠΟΥ 23/08/2026


ΠΡΟΣΦΥΓΙΚΑ Λ. ΑΛΕΞΑΝΔΡΑΣ: Η ΕΥΡΩΠΑΪΚΗ ΕΠΙΤΡΟΠΗ ΕΠΙΒΕΒΑΙΩΝΕΙ ΤΗΝ ΠΡΟΣΤΑΣΙΑ ΤΩΝ ΘΕΜΕΛΙΩΔΩΝ ΔΙΚΑΙΩΜΑΤΩΝ ΤΩΝ ΚΑΤΟΙΚΩΝ ΤΗΣ ΚΟΙΝΟΤΗΤΑΣ ΚΑΤΕΙΛΗΜΜΕΝΩΝ ΠΡΟΣΦΥΓΙΚΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΤΟ ΜΠΛΟΚΟ ΣΤΙΣ ΕΚΚΕΝΩΣΕΙΣ


Σε συνέχεια της γραπτής ερώτησης που κατατέθηκε στις 12 Ιουνίου 2026 και υπογράφηκε από 32 ευρωβουλευτές από διάφορες κοινοβουλευτικές ομάδες, η Ευρωπαϊκή Επιτροπή, μέσω του Εκτελεστικού Αντιπροέδρου Raffaele Fitto, εξέδωσε απάντηση που αποτελεί ένα καθοριστικό πολιτικό και νομικό εργαλείο για την υπεράσπιση της Κοινότητας των Προσφυγικών.


Η απάντηση της Επιτροπής κατοχυρώνει τα εξής θεμελιώδη σημεία:


Μπλόκο στα πλάνα εκκένωσης και στη χρηματοδότησή τους:

 Η αρχική έγκριση της Ευρωπαϊκής Επιτροπής για την ενδιάμεση επανεξέταση του προγράμματος Αττική 2021-2027, η οποία περιλαμβάνει την «Προώθηση της πρόσβασης σε οικονομικά προσιτή και βιώσιμη στέγαση», αποτελεί εξαιρετικά πρώιμο στάδιο της διαδικασίας και έπονται στάδια εξειδίκευσης των συμπεριλαμβανόμενων έργων, μέχρι την τελική έγκριση οποιασδήποτε χρηματοδότησης. Η απάντηση αναφέρει ρητά ότι σε κάθε στάδιο θα πρέπει να τηρούνται αυστηρά από τα κράτη μέλη οι υποχρεώσεις που πηγάζουν από το ενωσιακό δίκαιο και τον Χάρτη Θεμελιωδών Δικαιωμάτων της Ε.Ε. Επομένως, οποιαδήποτε κρατική παρέμβαση για την βίαιη εκδίωξη των κατοίκων συνιστά παραβίαση των προβλεπόμενων όρων της Ε.Ε., εκθέτοντας για ακόμη μια φόρα την ελληνική κυβέρνηση με ό,τι αυτό συνεπάγεται, αλλά και την Περιφέρεια Αττικής, η οποία θα χάσει αυτομάτως και οριστικά οποιουδήποτε εγκριθέντες ευρωπαϊκούς πόρους.


Υποχρέωση διαβούλευσης με την Κοινότητα των Προσφυγικών:

 Η Επιτροπή ξεκαθαρίζει ότι υπάρχει νομική υποχρέωση προηγούμενης διαβούλευσης με όσους διαμένουν στο συγκρότημα («

διαβούλευση με τα θιγόμενα μέρη

»). Ως εκ τούτου, η Περιφέρεια Αττικής παρανόμησε και παραβίασε το ενωσιακό δίκαιο από την στιγμή που δεν έχει προβεί σε καμία συνομιλία με την Κοινότητα των Προσφυγικών και τους 400 και πλέον κατοίκους, των οποίων την παρουσία αγνοούσε… επιδεικτικά μέχρι πρόσφατα, με τις νόμιμες συνέπειες που αυτό συνεπάγεται ως προς την μελλοντική έγκριση οποιασδήποτε ευρωπαϊκής χρηματοδότησης. Σε κάθε περίπτωση, η Περιφέρεια οφείλει, έστω και καθυστερημένα, να υλοποιήσει την πρόταση του Ψηφίσματος της 24ης Ιουνίου του Δήμου Αθηναίων και να καθίσει στο τραπέζι του διαλόγου με την Κοινότητα των Προσφυγικών, που αποτελεί τον αναγνωρισμένο φυσικό συνομιλητή.


Το θεμελιώδες δικαίωμα στη στέγαση προστατεύει απόλυτα τους κατοίκους της Κοινότητας:

 Η Επιτροπή τονίζει «

την ανάγκη ανάπτυξης μέτρων μετριασμού και μηχανισμών συνεργασίας για τη μείωση των κινδύνων έξωσης και αστεγίας

». Εξάλλου, υπογραμμίζει ότι η έξωση χωρίς την προηγούμενη παροχή μιας συγκεκριμένης, εξειδικευμένης, αυτόνομης και αξιοπρεπούς εναλλακτικής λύσης αντίκειται στο ευρωπαϊκό και διεθνές δίκαιο. Παράλληλα, υπενθυμίζει ότι η Ευρωπαϊκή Σύμβαση Δικαιωμάτων του Ανθρώπου και ο Ευρωπαϊκός Κοινωνικός Χάρτης επιβάλλουν τη μέγιστη νομική προστασία για όσους κινδυνεύουν με έξωση, διασφαλίζοντας απόλυτα την αναζήτηση λύσεων.


Αυτή η τοποθέτηση ορίζει με τον πλέον κατηγορηματικό τρόπο ότι οποιαδήποτε βίαιη ή αναγκαστική παρέμβαση δεν περιλαμβάνει επίσημο διάλογο με τους κατοίκους και δεν τους εγγυάται μια αξιοπρεπή εναλλακτική λύση συνιστά παραβίαση του ευρωπαϊκού δικαίου.


Επιτροπή για την Ανάδειξη και Υπεράσπιση της Κοινότητας των Προσφυγικών και της Συλλογικής τους Μνήμης

title: The 1926 general strike: an anarchist communist critique: ACG Online Public Meeting
content:
Wednesday, September 9th   7 pm – 8:30 pm


A talk and discussion on the history, significance and lessons of the British general strike of 1926 to mark its 100th anniversary


For contemporary anarchists, the General Strike remains highly relevant. It demonstrates that workers possess the capacity to disrupt capitalist society on a massive scale. It also demonstrates that such disruption alone does not guarantee victory. Organisation, political clarity, and democratic control are essential. Movements that rely upon leaders committed to compromise will ultimately be constrained by those leaders’ priorities.


From an anarchist communist perspective, the central lesson of 1926 is that working class power must be organised independently and consciously. At a rank and file level, trade unions can play a role in defending immediate interests, but they cannot be treated as vehicles for the defence of the interests of the working class, of social revolution. Revolutionary transformation requires organisations rooted in the working class yet committed to broader emancipatory goals. It requires structures of direct democracy capable of replacing hierarchical institutions. Most importantly, it requires revolutionary militants prepared to coordinate efforts across workplaces and communities while remaining accountable to those they seek to organise alongside.


For anarchist communists, the defeat of 1926 was not evidence that revolutionary change is impossible. Rather, it was evidence that revolutionary potential must be matched by revolutionary organisation. Without that combination, even the most impressive demonstrations of working-class power can be contained, redirected, and ultimately defeated.

title: İsveç’te seçim öncesi on binler iklim için sokakta
content:
İsveç’in başkenti Stockholm, genel seçimlere üç hafta kala kitlesel bir iklim eylemine sahne oldu.


23 Ağustos Pazar günü Vasaparken’de bir araya gelen göstericiler, hükümetten sera gazı emisyonlarını hızla azaltmasını ve fosil yakıtlardan çıkış için daha güçlü politikalar uygulamasını istedi.


Eyleme ilişkin ilk katılım sayısı 10 bin olarak aktarılırken, organizatörler daha sonra katılımın 50 bini aştığını açıkladı.


280 örgüt aynı yürüyüşte


“İklim için Birlikte” çağrısıyla düzenlenen yürüyüşün organizatörleri arasında İsveç Doğa Koruma Derneği (Naturskyddsföreningen), Rebel Moms, Rebel Dads ve Researchers’ Desk yer aldı.


Yaklaşık 280 örgütün desteklediği eylemde çevre ve insan hakları örgütleri, sendikalar, gençlik ve spor örgütleri, araştırmacılar, kırsal örgütler, dini topluluklar ile kültür-sanat çevreleri bir araya geldi.


Organizatörler, eyleme destek veren örgüt sayısının İsveç’teki iklim gösterileri açısından rekor olduğunu belirtti.


Yürüyüşe iklim aktivisti Greta Thunberg de katıldı. Thunberg, İsveç’teki siyasi partilerin hiçbirinin iklim krizinin gerektirdiği ölçekte politika ortaya koymadığını söyledi. Mevcut politikaların sürmesi halinde iklim krizinin sonuçlarının daha da ağırlaşacağı uyarısında bulundu.


Stockholm, 23 Aug 2026

Thousands marched for stronger climate action ahead of the Swedish election.

Organisers reported up to 50 000 people. Climate ranks high among voters’ concerns.

Meanwhile Nordic governments keep pouring billions into foreign wars and weapons factories.…

pic.twitter.com/LT4fh7EAp2


— Erik Andreasen (@underreason1985)

August 24, 2026


İklim seçmenin öncelikli gündemlerinden


Eylem, İsveç’te 13 Eylül’de yapılacak parlamento seçimlerinden üç hafta önce gerçekleşti.


Kamu yayıncısı SVT için Verian tarafından yapılan araştırmaya göre seçmenlerin yüzde 37’si iklimi seçimde öncelikli gördüğü başlıklar arasında sayıyor. İklim; sağlık, eğitim, suç ve yaşlı bakımının ardından seçmenlerin en fazla önem verdiği konular arasında bulunuyor.


İsveç Doğa Koruma Derneği Başkanı Beatrice Rindevall da Avrupa’da bu yaz yaşanan aşırı sıcaklara dikkat çekerek, emisyonları bugünden azaltacak politikaların hayata geçirilmesini istedi.


Fotoğraf: Jana Eriksson/Greenpeace


Hükümetin iklim politikaları eleştiriliyor


Göstericilerin eleştirilerinin odağında Başbakan Ulf Kristersson liderliğindeki hükümetin iklim politikaları vardı.


Aşırı sağcı İsveç Demokratlarının desteğiyle 2022’de göreve gelen hükümet, akaryakıt vergilerini düşürdü ve yakıt tedarikçilerinin düşük karbonlu yakıt kullanmasına ilişkin yükümlülükleri azalttı.


İsveç İklim Politikası Konseyi de Mart 2026’da yayımladığı değerlendirmede hükümetin iklim politikasını “yetersiz” buldu.Bağımsız uzmanlardan oluşan Konsey’e göre İsveç, mevcut politikalarla 2030 ve 2040 ulusal iklim hedeflerine ve 2030 için Avrupa Birliği kapsamındaki yükümlülüklerine ulaşma yolunda değil. Konsey ayrıca mevcut hükümet döneminde karbondioksit emisyonlarının 1990’lardan bu yana ilk kez genel olarak “yanlış yönde” ilerlediğini belirtti.


Hedef 2045’te net sıfır


İsveç’in iklim yasası ve parlamento tarafından kabul edilen iklim çerçevesi, ülkenin 2045’e kadar net sıfır sera gazı emisyonuna ulaşmasını öngörüyor.


İç ulaşımdan kaynaklanan emisyonların ise 2030’a kadar 2010 seviyesine kıyasla en az yüzde 70 azaltılması hedefleniyor.


İklim Politikası Konseyi, seçimlerden sonra kurulacak hükümetin bu hedeflere ulaşabilmesi için görev döneminin başında “somut ve güçlü” kararlar alması gerektiğini belirtiyor.


Kristersson hükümeti ise fosil yakıtlardan çıkışın ülkenin rekabet gücü ve şirketler üzerindeki etkileri gözetilerek aşamalı biçimde gerçekleştirilmesini savunuyor. Hükümet, nisan ayında ulaşımın elektrifikasyonunu hızlandırmak amacıyla elektrikli araç teşviklerini genişleteceğini de açıklamıştı.

title: Li Stenbolê bernameya bîranînê ji bo gerîlayên PKKê yên ku can dane pêk hat
content:
Piştî nav û nasnavên gerîlayên PKKyê yên di dîrokên cuda û li deverên cuda can dane aşkere bûn, li Amed, Mêrdîn, Wan û Stenbolê bernameyên bîranînê hatin li dar xistin.


Bi pêşengtiya MEBYA-DERa Amedê de ji bo gerilayên PKKê yên ku di dîrokên cuda de can dane, li li navçeyên Baxcilar û Sancaktepeyê yên Stenbolê bernameya bîranînê hat li dar xistin. Malbatê gerilayan, Dayikên Aştiyê, Hevserokên DBPê, endam û rêveberên partiyên siyasî, nûnerên saziyên civakî û gelek welatî tevlî bernameyê bûn.


Li gorî nûçeya Ajansa Welat di salona bîranînê de li ser maseyan fotografên gerîlayan, Abdulla Ocalan û gul hatin danîn. 


Li salonê pankartên “Em şehîden rûmetê bi bîr tînin”, “Şehîdên me rûmeta me ne”, “Têkoşîna wan rêya me ronî dike” û “Şehîd Namirin” hatin daliqandin.


Di bernameyê de di destpêkê de dayika endamê PKKê Ferrah Guneş û bavê Necmettîn Tarin axivîn.


Piştre Hevserokê Giştî yê DBPê Keskîn Bayindir axivî. Keskîn Bayindir destnîşan kir ku her yek cangoriyan destanek nivîsandiye û wiha got: 


“Bila tu kes xwe tenê nebihîse. Bi milyonan gelê me îro gel hev in. Wekî malbatan jî got şehîd şehîdên Kurdistanê ne. Em li ku bin ev têkoşîna ku bi serokatiya Rêber Apo dimeşe me anîn gel hev. Her şehîd kevirek danîn ser hev û kelehek avakirin. Em şehîdên xwe dispêrin axê lê em dibêjin aştî, dayikên şehîdan dibêjin aştî. Spartina axê ne dawîbûn e, destpêkek e. Em ê ala wan li erdê nexin.”

author: Unknown
title: Ephéméride des luttes : 24 août
content:
Dans l'éphéméride des luttes du 24 août, la torpeur de l'été est propice à des découvertes d'importance, qui viennent s'ajouter à la liste des bâtons qui ont fait faire des progrès aux luttes sociales : les frites et la dynamite.


1853 :

 Selon nos informations, les premières frites sont préparées ce jour-là.


1927 :

 A Chicago, dans le cadre de la campagne de soutien aux anarchistes Italiens Sacco et Vanzetti, qui risquent la condamnation à mort aux Etats-Unis, une bombe fait sauter trois magasins et deux habitations, faisant plus de 250.000 dollars de dégâts.


1944 :

 A Paris, les anarchistes espagnols participent à la libération de la ville, et De Gaulle les 'remerciera' les années suivantes en interdisant la presse antifranquiste et en mettant en prison des militants anarcho-syndicalistes.


1954 :

 Aux États-Unis, le Président Eisenhower signe le Communist Control Act, interdisant le Parti Communiste dans le pays.


1967 :

 A New York, Abbie Hoffman et Jerry Rubin lancent des billets de banque au NY Sotkc Exchange, provoquant une émeute.


1970 :

 Dans le Wisconsin, le New Year's Gang fait sauter un institut de recherche de l'armée dans l'université.


1994 :

 A Montevideo en Uruguay, des manifestations ont lieu devant l'hôpital Filtro pour protester contre l'extradition de trois Basques accusés d'appartenir à ETA. La police tire à balles réelles, faisant un mort et plus d'une trentaine de blessé-e-s.


2017 :

 A Chorges dans les Hautes-Alpes, un véhicule de RTE

est incendié

 contre l'installation d'une ligne à Très Haute Tension dans le coin.


Voir

l'éphéméride anarchiste

 du 24 août pour quelques petites choses en plus.

title: «Канскому подростку» Никите Уварову добавили статью
content:
В отношении Никиты Уварова «выявлен» новый эпизод «преступной деятельности», сообщил Следственный Комитет по Красноярскому краю и Республике Хакасия.

Уваров — фигурант знаменитого «дела Канских подростков». В 2020 году задержанным в Канске (Красноярский край) несовершеннолетним за расклейку анархистских листовок предъявили абсурдное обвинение в террористической деятельности. На тот момент 15-летний Уваров отсидел по этому делу пять лет.

Сейчас ему 21, и он до сих пор за решеткой: сразу после отбытия срока его арестовали по новому абсурдному обвинению, участие в деятельности не существующей, но запрещенной в России экстремистской организации «Арестантский Уклад Един» (АУЕ).

Ранее Уваров обвиняли лишь в участии (ч.2 282.2 УК), а теперь и в вовлечении в деятельность АУЕ (ч. 1.1 ст. 282.2 УК). Нового суда Уваров ждет в СИЗО.

Адрес для писем: 660075, РФ, г. Красноярск, ул. Республики, 72, СИЗО-1, Уваров Никита Андреевич 2005 г. р. Возможна отправка писем через сервисы «Ф-письмо», «Зонателеком» и PrisonMail.Online (для зарубежных карт).

title: L’accanimento continua: Giorgio di nuovo in carcere
content:
Nella serata di venerdì, senza alcuna avvisaglia, Giorgio è stato prelevato dai Carabinieri di Susa dalla sua dimora sopra la Credenza a Bussoleno e tradotto nel carcere delle Vallette.

A determinare il ritorno in casa circondariale è stata la revoca della misura alternativa concessagli dal Tribunale di Sorveglianza, a seguito di non ben specificate violazioni delle prescrizioni imposte.

Nel mese di marzo, dopo aver già passato parecchi mesi sottoposto alle misure stabilite dal Tribunale di Sorveglianza, guarda caso il giorno stesso della sua liberazione, Giorgio era stato nuovamente posto agli arresti domiciliari per scontare un’altra pena che avrebbe concluso in autunno. Una nuova pagina della vicenda giudiziaria che lo riguarda e che da anni accompagna la sua storia all’interno del Movimento No Tav. Continueremo, dunque, a fare sentire a Giorgio e all* compagn* tedesch* a cui è stato confermato il carcere, la nostra vicinanza e solidarietà, in Valsusa come in città, nelle piazze come nei sentieri, consapevoli che la sua storia. che è la nostra storia di tanti e tante altre No Tav, è parte di un percorso collettivo che certo non si interromperà con le porte di un carcere.


Giorgio libero subito!

author: LCM-Redaktion
title: The kids are all red? – Interview mit Rote Jugend Deutschland
content:
Rote Jugend ist mittlerweile allen in der radikalen Linken ein Begriff.


Für Außenstehende


praktisch


aus dem Boden geschossen undschnell


gewachsen ist die Rote Jugend


mehr als ein Internetphänomen, sondern als junge, kommunistisch orientierteBewegung


auch auf der Straße, auf Konferenzen, Veranstaltungen, Aktionen und Camps präsent.


Das Außenbild polarisiert mit kommunistischerÄsthetik, Kampfsport, Instagram-Reels mit Graffiti und Bengalos und marxistisch-leninistischerTheorie.


Die Organisation Rote Jugend Deutschland (RJD) hat sich während des Rollens der neuen roten Welle im Januar 2026 offiziell gegründet und gehört aktuell wahrscheinlich zu den am meisten Zulauf kriegenden Strömungen in der deutschen Linken. Wir wollten RJD besser kennenlernen und haben einen ihrer Aktivisten zu ihren Inhalten, Aktivitäten, Plänen und Kritiken befragt. Das Interview ist für RJD das erste dieser Art.


Wie ist Rote Jugend Deutschland entstanden? Wann habt ihr euch gegründet und warum habt ihr die Struktur aufgebaut?


Das ist eine gute Frage, aber nicht so einfach zu beantworten, weil wir nicht zu einem Zeitpunkt entschieden haben, dass es jetzt eine Rote Jugend Bewegung in Deutschland bräuchte und die dann aufgebaut haben. Sondern den Begriff „Rote Jugend“, „Rote Jugend Bewegung“ oder „Rote Jugend Deutschland“ benutzen wir auf drei verschiedene Art und Weisen. Erstmal benutzen wir den Begriff Rote Jugend stellvertretend für eine gewisse politische Sequenz, d.h. eine objektive Bewegung innerhalb der politischen Kräfte in der radikalen Linken. Wir sehen rückblickend, dass ungefähr ab 2008 mit dem G8-Gipfel der Marxismus-Leninismus wieder Einzug in die radikale Linke gefunden hat. Darüber schreibt z.B. J. Moufawad-Paul in „Die kommunistische Notwendigkeit“, dass grob zu dem Zeitpunkt wieder eine Form von primitivem Verständnis von Marxismus Einzug in die radikale Linke in den imperialistischen Zentren gehalten hat. Wir datieren rückblickend deshalb die Entstehung von dem, was wir Rote Jugendbewegung nennen, auf ungefähr diesen Zeitpunkt. Damals entstanden ungeplant und unbewusst die ersten Kollektive, die wir als Teil unserer Bewegung, als Teil unserer Geschichte, als Rote Jugend betrachten würden. Natürlich gibt es Organisationen und Gruppen, die schon älter waren. Aber ab diesem Punkt wurde auch als Korrekturbewegung angefangen, Elemente des Marxismus wieder mit der proletarischen und populären Jugendkultur zu verbinden und es hat ein neuer revolutionärer Aufbruch stattgefunden. Wir sagen deshalb retrospektiv, dass da die Rote Jugendbewegung entstanden ist. Das wusste damals nur noch keiner.

Wir haben aber gemerkt, dass man immer wieder Genoss:innen aus anderen Kollektiven, aus anderen Städten trifft, mit denen man dieselbe politische DNA teilt, auch wenn es natürlich auch Unterschiede gab. Aber das sind Kinder derselben Wut, das ist ähnlich, das ist mehr als nur eine zufällige Erscheinung, sondern es gab dieses Phänomen: Kollektive von jungen Genoss:innen bilden sich, verbinden den Marxismus mit revolutionärer Jugendkultur, haben inhaltliche Gemeinsamkeiten und bilden Zirkel und Kollektive, die aber damals oft noch lokal begrenzt waren und höchstens regionale Kooperationen hatten. Diese Rote Jugendbewegung, die es in der BRD seit den 2010er Jahren gibt, ist eine tatsächlich stattfindende Bewegung. Das ist nichts, was wir uns ausgedacht haben, sondern es ist passiert. Man will nicht sagen natürlich, aber organisch im Klassenkampf aus der Gesellschaft der BRD entstehen solche Kollektive.

Die gehen aber auch genauso schnell wieder kaputt. Die sind dann getragen von 1, 2 Chefinnen und Chefs und fallen diese weg, bricht das Kollektiv mehr oder weniger zusammen. Wir haben dann, nachdem wir länger schon gespürt und beobachtet hatten, wie verschiedene Genoss:innen in verschiedenen Projekten, verschiedenen Jugendgruppen, auch z.B. vom ehemaligen Jugendwiderstand, eine ähnliche Praxis und ähnliche Vorstellungen hatten, gesagt, dass diese Bewegung mehr werden muss, als die Summe seiner Teile. Und das haben wir Ende 2020 in manchen Städten dann theoretisiert. Es gibt gute historische Beispiele, wie aus Jugendorganisationen/-bewegungen auch fortgeschrittenere politische Formierungen entstehen können. Wir haben uns auf der Grundlage dann aufgemacht, diese rote Jugendbewegung zu vereinigen. Dafür war ein erster Schritt erst mal klarzumachen: Es gibt eine rote Jugend in Deutschland und du bist Teil davon. Wir haben einen …

author: Mansoor Qaisar
title: The First Middle East Alliance That Doesn’t Need Washington’s Permission
content:
Sometime this past week, an Iranian parliamentary official told a Lebanese television channel that Tehran had received an invitation to join the Mecca Accord. No signature, no letterhead, no confirmation from Riyadh, Ankara, or Islamabad — and Iran’s own foreign ministry has responded with the kind of calculated ambiguity that neither confirms nor kills a story. In the same week, Iran’s foreign ministry announced that Field Marshal Asim Munir will travel to Tehran on Monday, August 24, for high-level talks framed around bilateral cooperation and “regional peace and security.”


It is tempting, and wrong, to fuse those two stories into “Munir flew to Tehran to deliver the Mecca invitation.” He didn’t — the visit’s confirmed purpose sits inside Pakistan’s separate role as the last working conduit in a stalled US-Iran negotiation, not inside accord diplomacy. But the fact that both stories are landing in the same week, through the same government, carried by the same general, is itself the story worth taking seriously.


What actually happened, and what didn’t


The Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, signed August 7 by Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan, was built to be deliberately vague about its target. All three founders have repeated that the pact names no enemy and stays open to new members. Egypt has been floated as a candidate almost since the ink dried, and Syria’s foreign minister said during an August 20 Islamabad visit that Damascus was weighing whether to join or cooperate with it. Iran’s initial public reaction ranged from cautious welcome to open mockery from hardline clerics.


That range of reactions is exactly why Munir’s visit matters more than the unconfirmed invitation itself. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi travelled to Tehran on August 12 specifically to brief President Masoud Pezeshkian on the Mecca agreement’s contents, carrying a message directly from Munir and the prime minister. Pakistan is the only accord founder Iran has kept talking to consistently through a shooting war, a collapsed US negotiation, and a defence pact its own hardliners initially treated as provocation.


The question the accord can’t dodge: Palestine


Here is what most coverage of the Mecca Accord treats as background and what should actually be the center of any expansion scenario: this pact did not emerge in a vacuum. Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan made little secret of wanting to build a Muslim alliance partly in reaction to what he and others in the region describe as Israel’s war in Gaza, and the founding summit’s choice of Mecca over Riyadh — accompanied by images of the three leaders praying together — was a deliberate signal about the moral register the accord wanted to claim. 


That test gets harder, not easier, as membership grows. A wider accord, and especially an Iran-inclusive one, would functionally become the first Muslim-majority security architecture in decades explicitly capable of imposing costs on Israel over Gaza and the West Bank, rather than merely issuing statements about them. Emirati and Israeli intelligence services were reportedly caught off guard by the original pact and remain unsettled by it — the fear in Abu Dhabi and Tel Aviv is not really about Pakistan’s nuclear status, it is about a bloc gaining the collective standing to actually extract a price for continued action in Gaza. If a critical mass of Muslim states sits inside one framework, Israel loses the ability to manage the Palestinian file through bilateral relationships alone, and normalization tracks with any Gulf state still outside the bloc become far harder to sell domestically. 


How far does “Muslim-majority” actually stretch?


There is a version of this scenario more dramatic than Iran alone, and it’s worth naming precisely because it’s the one most casual commentary reaches for without examining it: not just Iran, but a genuine majority of the Muslim world — Indonesia and Malaysia from Southeast Asia, Azerbaijan and the Central Asian states, Nigeria and Algeria and Morocco from Africa, most of the Gulf beyond Saudi Arabia — folding into one framework. That version isn’t a defense pact anymore. It’s the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation with an actual enforcement mechanism, something the OIC has talked about and never built in nearly six decades of existence.


The scale would be real. It would mean a bloc spanning the world’s largest Muslim population (Indonesia), two of its most capable defense industries (Türkiye …

author: Krishna Kumar
title: 500,000 children are born with congenital heart disease in Africa. Where are the hospitals to treat them?
content:
When Tendai Moyo’s daughter, Rudorwashe Grace, was born in a Zimbabwean hospital, she struggled to breathe, her lips turned blue, and feeding exhausted her. Recognising instantly that her baby was seriously unwell, Tendai repeatedly sought medical help, but her concerns were ignored. Because her daughter’s illness was invisible and she appeared to others like a healthy baby, her symptoms were even dismissed as witchcraft.


Tendai Moyo


It took six months of fighting for Rudorwashe Grace to be diagnosed with tricuspid atresia and cardiomegaly, a severe congenital heart defect. By then, valuable time had been lost. For babies with the most serious heart defects, those months can be the difference between life and death.


But even after diagnosis, Tendai couldn’t find the care her baby needed. At the time, Zimbabwe had only one paediatric cardiologist for a population of 15 million, practising privately in Harare, about 400 kilometres away. With no hope that surgery could take place locally, Tendai’s only chance was to raise around US$20,000 to send her daughter to India for treatment.


Tragically, her daughter died at just 10 months old. Her death was not inevitable. It was the result of systemic delays, missed opportunities by governments and policymakers and a health system that was not equipped to respond to congenital heart disease.


What went wrong?


Tendai’s story is sadly far from unique. Congenital heart disease (CHD) is one of the most common birth defects in the world, affecting up to one in every 50 newborns. Across Africa, this means

500,000 babies are born each year

 with damaged hearts. Some will have small defects that can be monitored, but at least a third will need critical treatment in their first year of life. Without it,

up to 85% of children with the severest form of CHD will die

.


For thousands of African children effective treatment is a matter of life and death. Despite this, across much of Africa, the systems needed to diagnose and treat CHD are dangerously out of reach for most families.


Outlined in the World Heart Federation’s yearly

World Heart Report

, as

many as 90% of children

 in some regions of Africa, such as Somalia, Djibouti, Niger and Chad, live in “paediatric heart health deserts” – areas with no timely access to safe diagnosis or care for congenital heart disease. The very few paediatric cardiac surgery centres in Africa are often concentrated in capital cities, where the costs of travel and accommodation alone can render surgery unfeasible.


As the report illustrates, congenital heart disease often falls between categories, prompting planning and policy misalignments on a global scale. It is present at birth, but not always included in maternal and newborn health programmes. It is a heart condition, but often missing from cardiovascular disease plans, which are typically designed around adults and place emphasis on lifestyle factors and hypertension, rather than conditions present from birth. It requires surgery, but a very specialised surgery that may not be included in national surgical strategies.


Even when safe, affordable and timely surgery can take place, a decent quality of life can only be assured by lifelong follow-up care. In today’s global healthcare lottery, the result is that many children fall through the cracks.


Creating pathways


Despite the prevalence of these “heart-health deserts”, encouragingly, there are models from low- and middle-income regions that can be adapted. Kerala, in India, is widely lauded for its efforts to approach congenital heart disease as a population health challenge, rather than with a case-by-case treatment model. When Kerala channelled funding and resources into this approach, the state developed a “Continuum of Care” for CHD to not only encapsulate recognition, diagnosis and referral, but with provisions for transport, integrated collaboration with the private sector for surgical treatment and follow-up care.


The results of this shift in approach during the programme’s first six years

speak for themselves

: 22876 children with suspected CHD were registered; 767 newborns and 2612 infants (30 days-1 year) underwent a therapeutic procedure that typically involved open-heart surgery. Most newborns with CHD were identified through prenatal or neonatal screening. During this period the infant mortality of the state of Kerala declined from 12/1000 to 6/1000.


Top-down vs. bottom-up


Despite systemic failings at a …

author: Mohamed Alagra, Mashair Idris, Hassan Alnaser
title: Sudan Nashra: Burhan offers temporary immunity for internal dialogue participants | AU Peace, Security Council in Khartoum | Khartoum, Riyadh establish bilateral coordination council | Second-largest single group RSF defection arrive in Northern State
content:
Subscribe to our Lens on Sudan newsletter

here

.


In an Armed Forces Day speech on August 14, Transitional Sovereignty Council Chair Abdel Fattah al-Burhan offered temporary immunity to participants in the intra-Sudanese dialogue his government is now rushing to launch, including a suspension of criminal proceedings against those facing charges while they take part.


The move is largely aimed at clearing the legal obstacle facing leaders of the opposition Sumud coalition, the civilian coalition led by former Prime Minister Abdalla Hamdok that was formed on the back of a factional split in the the Civil Front for Democracy, a previous anti-war civilian front. The charges stem from that earlier coalition over what the military saw as proximity to the Rapid Support Forces.


But the legal cases are only one obstacle. Civilian forces want the dialogue to follow a halt in fighting, input on how its preparatory arrangements are made and to know whether whatever comes out of the process will bind state institutions. The military is showing no sign of halting its campaign, while Burhan’s central role in building the dialogue and his apparent ambitions for it do little to settle questions about its independence.


Moreover, Khartoum cannot entirely escape the regional and international tracks it is trying to outpace. An African Union diplomat told Mada Masr that any internal dialogue would ultimately need to connect with those tracks and gain acceptance from them. 


Khartoum may have seen an opening for some African cover. Just hours after Burhan’s speech, a delegation from the African Union’s Peace and Security Council arrived in Port Sudan before travelling to Khartoum for its first field visit to the capital since the outbreak of the war.


Sudan has been trying to repair its relationship with the AU since 2021, when the bloc suspended its membership after the military and Rapid Support Forces jointly ousted the civilian wing of the government. Now, with state institutions back in Khartoum, a civilian government appointed last year and a domestic dialogue being hurried toward a September launch, authorities are looking for the AU’s renewed attention to translate into a role in the political process and the restoration of Sudan’s membership.


But the visit is not quite the diplomatic endorsement Khartoum might want. Another AU diplomat told Mada Masr that the union is still assessing, speaking to multiple sides and gathering information. There is a lot the bloc needs to know, the diplomat said, and the AU is not prepared to give any political process a “blank check.”


Monday was a busy day for what a Sudanese political source described as Khartoum’s effort to “rearrange its foreign relations during the war and beyond.”


In Ankara, military Chief-of-Staff Yasser al-Atta held talks with his Turkish counterpart Selcuk Bayraktaroglu and Defense Minister Yasar Guler. Sudanese military sources said contacts between the two establishments have become more regular. 


The sources said Monday’s talks focused on the military’s needs at the current stage and the support it wants from Turkey after the war, from training and reconnaissance to rebuilding the armed forces’ capabilities and institutions.


Turkey’s existing defense relationship with Sudan and its experience in areas where the military needs help make it one of the easier partnerships for Khartoum to deepen, one of the military sources said.


On the same day, Burhan was in Riyadh signing the largest agreement in the history of Sudanese-Saudi relations, establishing a bilateral coordination council. A Sudanese diplomatic source said the council is intended to move the relationship “from managing scattered files to a single political and institutional mechanism.”


The new mechanism is also intended to give the political relationship a more direct economic dimension, according to a former Sudanese diplomat. Political discussions with Riyadh can now be linked to projects in agriculture, energy, mining, infrastructure and trade. 


On the battlefield, both the military and the RSF are trying to take back territory following a series of gains by both sides in recent weeks. In Blue Nile, the military has stepped up air and artillery strikes on the RSF’s newly captured positions in Geisan and Kurmuk, while in North Kordofan, the RSF has launched drone attacks on towns recently captured by the military.

title: Recentering African Feminist Epistemologies: A Community of Practice to Prevent and Respond to Sexual Violence
content:
Over the past year, Liberation Alliance Africa has sustained the

Building Knowledge Bridges Community of Practice on Recentering African Indigenous Epistemologies to Prevent and Respond to Sexual Violence

. This Community of Practice is a collective of African feminist scholars, practitioners, organisers, artists, and movement builders committed to the dreaming and making of a world free from sexual violence through knowledge bridges.


Sexual violence continues to impact communities across the African continent, and class, ethnicity and religion play a critical role in making civilians in conflict-affected countries particularly more vulnerable. It disproportionately affects women and girls, and ethnic, gender and racialized minorities. Sexual violence is compounded by conflict, displacement, poverty, and gender inequality. It remains significantly under-reported due to stigma and under-prosecuted? Due to weak and corrupt justice systems. Sexual violence includes rape and sexual assault, sexual coercion and exploitation, including trafficking for sexual exploitation and conflict-related sexual violence such as using rape as a weapon of war. It affects people of any gender and age. 


Our starting premise is simple: sexual violence on the continent cannot be understood, let alone addressed, through frameworks that treat colonialism as history rather than a structural force that continues to shape theory, practice, and response to sexual violence. 


Coloniality was

coined

by Peruvian philosopher and sociologist Aníbal Quijano, and it describes the long-lasting pattern of power produced by colonial rule and shape

s

 how we approach epistemological frameworks through which violence is understood.

Epistemology deals with questions concerning the nature, scope, and sources of knowledge.

 A meaningful analysis of sexual violence must begin by seeking to decolonise knowledge and epistemic structures. This analysis requires us to interrogate the assumptions that underpin dominant theories, question whose expertise is legitimised, and create space for African feminist epistemologies to shape how violence is understood, prevented, and responded to. 


We felt an urgent need to organise as scholars and practitioners to generate new frameworks grounded in our histories, political realities, and lived experiences. Our analyses are rooted in our confrontation of the neo-colonial state, the global imperialist, extractive and patriarchal systems that shape our everyday existence. We arrive as feminists in service of a liberatory project, convinced that knowledge-making is itself a site of feminist struggle. 


As the CoP came together through both intentional convening and organic growth, we began organising our work around three enquiries that we believe are critical to envisioning a decolonial feminist approach to preventing and responding to sexual violence in Africa. 


The first enquiry,

Whose Knowledge? An Audit of the Current Knowledge Systems within Sexual Violence Prevention and Response in Africa

 examines the dominant literature, asks whose voices have shaped the field, whose knowledge has been marginalised, and what becomes possible when African feminist scholarship is placed at the centre of analysis. 


The second enquiry,

 The Coloniality of Sexual Violence: Gender, Power, Sovereignty, and the Neo-Colonial State,

 advances interventions on sexual violence that explicitly interrogate the role and impact of hetero-patriarchal colonial racial-capitalism, alongside the complicity of neo-colonial states, in producing and sustaining conditions of gendered violence. 


The third enquiry,

Truth-telling and Epistemic Sovereignty in the Prevention and Response Continuum

, centres on indigenous and endogenous knowledge systems as essential practice-based frameworks for reimagining prevention, response, healing, accountability, and collective safety.


The Imperative of Recentering African Epistemologies


At Liberation Alliance Africa, we believe African women and gender-expansive people’s knowledge-making and world-building are crucial to de-westernising normative assumptions and dominant approaches. African women and gender-expansive scholars must nurture new ways of knowing and being- knowledge that doesn’t just challenge dominant views, but creates a rich foundation for how we understand reality and tackle life’s critical questions.


For a long time, African women and gender minorities were treated as …

author: Simon Ramapuputla
title: Marikana’s wounds still bleed 14 years after police massacre
content:
Fourteen years after police opened fire on striking mineworkers at Marikana, the massacre is remembered not only for the 34 men who were killed, but for their absence in the lives of their families.


For some, the memory is of a father who never came home. For others, it is the loss of a breadwinner, a brother or a son. And for those who were children when the killings happened, it is the experience of growing up with memories that have become increasingly distant, while the questions about justice remain.


At a commemoration marking 14 years since the massacre, the families, activists and academics reflected on what Marikana means more than a decade later – and on its place in South Africa’s longer history of protest, police violence and struggles for dignity.


For the Socio-Economic Rights Institute of South Africa (Seri), which has represented the families since 2012, the central question remains accountability. Seri secured payments for 35 of the 37 families whose loved ones were killed by police. Two families have received no compensation.


Seri’s executive director, Nomzamo Zondo said the compensation process itself reflected a deeper problem in how the state understood the loss suffered by the families. “Part of that is a narrative that what the state is interested in compensating is the income that the miners would have earned. They do not want to account for the husbands, brothers, sons and fathers that they took away from the families,” she said.


For Zondo, compensation alone cannot address the significance of Marikana. The state also needs to acknowledge that the massacre should never have happened, she argued: “That’s what a public holiday on the 16

th

 of August would mean. It would say: we are saying never, never again.”


She said this was particularly important given the continued use of force by police in managing protests. “We’ve seen that police continue to manage protests through the use of violence. They have continuously refused to accept that their role is to facilitate protests as a constitutional right.”


Zondo also pointed to the failure to implement recommendations made by the panel of experts on public order policing and the management of protests. The panel completed its work in 2018, but its recommendations remain largely unimplemented.


Squalid living conditions in the informal settlement, Nkaneng, in the shadow of Marikana platinum mine, a source of immense wealth for the owners in 2012, Lonmin. Archive photo by The Benchmarks Foundation


Another major concern, she said, was the failure of the National Prosecuting Authority to bring those responsible for the 16 August killings to court. “Every year, of course, when the anniversary comes, there is an explanation that work is being done,” Zondo said. “But now we are like one year short from 15 years since the massacre. We are just 12 years since the Commission finalised its report and recommended that the NPA must investigate and charge whoever is responsible.”


The question, she said, was whether there was “really an intention to hold anyone accountable for the deaths of the 16

th

 of August”.


For the families, however, the consequences of Marikana are not measured only by the progress of criminal investigations or compensation claims. They are lived in the absence of loved ones.


‘I still have that memory’


NowilI Nungu was 15 when her father, Jackson Lehopa, was killed at Marikana. Today, at 29, she remembers him through the ordinary moments of their life together: travelling to school on a bicycle, buying him a Coke and watching him repair the bicycle whenever it broke.


“I have so many memories with my dad,” Nungu said. She was the only girl among six children and had been living with her father in Rustenburg while her mother moved back to the Eastern Cape.


By the time of the massacre, Nungu had moved to the Eastern Cape with her mother. The family did not have electricity and relied on the radio for news. Her father normally called every day after returning from the koppie to tell them he was safe. But that day, he did not call.


Crosses erected at the koppie as a symbol of lives lost on 16 August 2012. Archive photo by Muzi Mzoyi


Sebolai Liau lost his father, the late Janefeke Raphael Liau, at Marikana. For him, the question of justice remains unresolved. “I think regarding the Marikana massacre, there is no justice. I don’t think it will ever be served, but for now it has not been, and there are no signs …
