author: AWSM
title: A Community in the Cracks of Capitalism
content:
A piece of Christchurch that the property market abandoned after the earthquakes has become home to people abandoned by the property market. The old Bexley neighbourhood was largely cleared after liquefaction made conventional residential development impossible. Houses disappeared, streets remained and the land sat waiting for whatever official purpose would eventually be found for it. Into that gap came people who needed somewhere to live. They arrived in cars, vans, buses and tents. Some were working. Some were retired. Some had children. They did what people have always done when the institutions around them fail, they improvised. A community grew. Earlier this year about 40 people were living around Wetlands Grove; reports now put the number at more than 100. Christchurch City Council has told them they must leave by 28 February 2027 because the area is intended for wetland development. There is an obvious temptation to treat this as a story about homelessness, council planning or the difficulties of finding somewhere suitable for a group of people living in vehicles. It is all of those things, but underneath them sits a much simpler question. What is land for? The answer given by our economic system is that land belongs to whoever has legal title to it, and its legitimate use is determined by owners, planners and institutions. The people actually living on it remain secondary. They may sleep there, look after one another there and make the place usable through their own effort, but none of that gives them any meaningful claim to it. Their relationship to the place exists only for as long as the legal owner tolerates it. That distinction between ownership and use lies close to the heart of the anarchist criticism of private property.

The people living at Wetlands Grove have already demonstrated something that governments spend enormous amounts of money trying unsuccessfully to manufacture through policy documents – people can organise social life themselves. Earlier reporting described an informal community growing around buses, vans and cars, with neighbours helping one another through winter and a communal tent being established as shared space. One man who had been sleeping in a small tent was helped into an old car when the cold became severe. Council rubbish collection and portable toilets made conditions more bearable, but the social organisation of the place came largely from the people living there. Moko, one of the informal figures in the community, was working full-time on an on-call road crew. Others were pensioners. Ngawai Timu described abandoning a $470-a-week rental because she felt she was spending her life paying somebody else’s mortgage. Polly Stewart was surviving on the pension in a bus. Families were living there too, including a woman with several children living from a bus. These details matter because homelessness is constantly spoken about as though it were primarily a pathology of homeless people. Addiction, mental illness, poor budgeting, antisocial behaviour and bad choices are summoned as explanations because those explanations leave the social order intact. They allow us to imagine that housed people possess some quality that homeless people lack. Wetlands Grove makes that story harder to sustain. When people with jobs cannot obtain housing, when pensioners decide rent leaves too little for ordinary life, and when families find themselves competing with dozens of others for a private rental, the problem is no longer plausibly located inside the individual. There are certainly people living rough who struggle with addiction or serious psychological distress. There are also people who get up and go to work from a tent. A housing system that cannot reliably house either has failed at the most elementary level.

New Zealand has become remarkably skilled at describing this failure without challenging the institution producing it. We talk about housing supply, affordability pressures and housing need. We devise eligibility categories and waiting lists. We construct administrative pathways through emergency housing, transitional housing, community housing and social housing. Every stage acquires its own assessments and rules. The language becomes more sophisticated while people remain without homes. At the 2023 Census, Statistics New Zealand estimated that at least 112,496 people were experiencing severe housing deprivation, around 2.3 percent of the usually resident population. The …

author: Kelly Cvetkova
title: Why One Nation is attacking women
content:
Pauline Hanson has spat in the faces of the millions of Australian women who have experienced family violence by describing the crime as a “two-way street”. Returning to a tired victim-blaming rhetoric that women just “shouldn’t put up with it”, she’s trying to turn the clock back on attitudes to women experiencing violence and the real difficulties they face getting support. 

Hanson has featured on right-wing podcasts asserting that women are treating the family courts and child support payments as a “cash cow”, a system that needs to be “reined in”. These comments not only fly in the face of reality but are also an attack on some of the poorest and most vulnerable people in Australia. The 2025 Household, Income and Labour Dynamics survey found that 34.7 percent of children in single parent households live in poverty. Eight out of every ten of these households are headed by women. Domestic abuse is the main reason women become homeless in Australia, women and children making up nine out of the ten people attempting to access specialist housing services. 

Hanson’s outbursts are not the result of ignorance. One Nation’s increased attacks against the rights of women, whether on the issues of domestic abuse, abortion rights or parental leave, are part of the intensification of its far-right agenda, and an attempt to integrate a broader range of social issues into it. Women, according to this logic, are just another interest group that gets “special treatment” thanks to wokeism and whose endless demands are a drain on business and wealth creation. In her now infamous speech at the National Press Club, Hanson made this clear, stating “if women take time off [to have children] and they are not paid their wages because they’re not working, fair enough ... Why should business pay? They’re not at work”.

This parallels her attacks on organisations like the National Indigenous Australians Agency, which she argues should be abolished to save taxpayers from “wasteful Indigenous grants”. She likewise attacks LGBTI people, specifically the “transgender insurgency”, that has “penetrated almost every regulatory authority”. Who is on the other side of this equation?  Apparently, as Hanson told parliament in 2023, “the most oppressed and neglected minority in Australia”, is—wait for it—“men”. 

The positioning around women’s rights is also intended to garner One Nation stronger support with a wider and more hardcore base of potential members and campaigners, most recently on the issue of abortion.

While the party has always maintained sexist talking points about the family courts and the evils of feminism, it has not previously actively campaigned against abortion rights. Hanson has been testing the waters on this issue lately though, indicating that she thinks Australia needs to “have a conversation” about abortion and flagging that she thinks abortion rights should be restricted after twenty weeks. She’s rubbed shoulders with the likes of infamous anti-abortion activist and influencer Joanna Howe. When Malcolm Roberts was questioned at a Brisbane Christian conference about whether the party would move to a policy of banning abortion altogether, the One Nation senator said that it was “becoming [his] goal” to do so.

Barnaby Joyce has been the most explicit in why the change of approach has come now. Speaking to a Sydney crowd of anti-abortion demonstrators, he stated, “What I see before me here is about 1,500 people who can hand out how to vote cards”. One Nation has a clear desire to recruit those sections of the right who are motivated by this issue. And why not—they are an already organised layer of activists who can be relatively easily deployed to campaign, especially if One Nation seems able to deliver and potentially reverse their flagging fortunes. 

Abortion has, in practice, been a settled issue in Australian politics for decades. Nearly three in every four people support legal abortion in some or all cases. But the right know both that there is a motivated minority available to them, and are confident that an aggressive campaign can swing more people behind the cause—especially when Labor is too cowardly to fight on the issue, as it was during the Voice referendum, for example. And the reality is that attitudes to abortion are already going backwards. A

Guardian

author: Tom Bramble
title: US imperialism and the war in Iran
content:
It is now six months since the US and Israel launched their war on Iran. The bloody offensive was meant to demonstrate US military might. It has revealed US weaknesses instead. This could not have come at a worse time for the US, which is facing a rising China, an intractable stand-off with Russia in Ukraine and increasing discontent within the ranks of its allies.

The attack on Iran was only the latest instalment of a decades-long campaign by the US and Israel to weaken, if not bring down, the Islamic Republic. The enmity has its roots in the challenge Iran represented to US imperialism in the Middle East following its 1979 revolution. That hostility has endured. As the US stumbled through defeats in Afghanistan and Iraq in the 2000s, Iran built a network of allies it called the “axis of resistance”. These included Hezbollah in Lebanon, Hamas in Palestine, loyal militias in Iraq and the Houthi rebel movement in Yemen, as well as a strong relationship with Syrian dictator Bashar al-Assad.

The escalation of Israel’s wars in the region following the 7 October 2023 Hamas attack inflicted serious damage on Iran’s regional alliance. Israel’s targeted assassinations of leaders and bombing raids, along with genocide, invasion and land grabs in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria rocked Iran’s allies. The fall of al-Assad in December 2024 took another piece out of Iran’s regional bloc. Repeated mass demonstrations and strikes in Iran itself further undermined the Tehran regime.

Israel determined that now was the time to finish off the regime. The Trump administration, despite ruling class reservations, agreed that a renewed war would weaken Iran. It also wanted to use what it expected would be a swift victory to impress upon Russia and China that the US was still top dog in the Middle East and to remind its allies of its role as the region’s security guarantor. US success in deposing Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and installing in his place puppet Delcy Rodriguez in January filled them with confidence.

The US and Israel have succeeded in one regard. According to the US administration, they have wiped out Iran’s navy and air force along with missile and defence systems. The economic cost to Iran in destroyed infrastructure and damage to the oil industry stands in the tens of billions of dollars. 

But in most other respects the US and Israel have failed. The US attack will not stop Iran’s progress to nuclear power; in fact, it will only make it more likely. Despite the killing of many top Iranian leaders, the regime has survived and dug in. There is no Delcy Rodriguez figure waiting to take over in Tehran. The war and intensified repression have driven the protest movement off the streets.

The US has failed to take control of Iranian oil. Quite the opposite. Iran has demonstrated its ability to weaponise the Strait of Hormuz, choking the world’s oil trade. It is unlikely now to cede this power. The Gulf states, which opposed the US-Israeli attack, are now facing the consequences. Oil prices have fluctuated but are now climbing once again, presenting fresh threats to the world economy.

The US and Israel may wield enormous firepower, but the war, coming on top of arms deliveries to Ukraine, is draining US missile and interceptor drone capacity. It is also drawing assets away from other potential theatres; the redeployment of the USS

 George Washington

 to the Middle East means the US no longer has an aircraft carrier in the Asia-Pacific for the first time since 1944.

The US may have built a substantial domestic oil industry in the last couple of decades, but its strategic oil reserves are now down to less than 300 million barrels, close to the minimum needed before storage facilities start to degrade.

The cost of the war is climbing. Taking into account not just the direct military outlays but also economic disruption, veteran care and lost stockpiles of missiles, the war is costing the US hundreds of billions of dollars, possibly approaching $1 trillion over time, contributing to the country’s spiralling national debt.

The attack on Iran was never popular among a US public wary of a repeat of the disasters in Afghanistan and Iraq. Six months on, with victory nowhere in sight and gasoline and heating oil prices rising, public support has dropped further. Opponents of the war now outnumber supporters by 20 percentage points. New York Times

author: Ben Radford
title: Socialist Alliance candidates to contest Lutruwita council elections
content:
Candidates for Lutruwita Socialist Alliance (LSA) are running in three local government areas in the Lutruwita/Tasmania council elections over September to October.

Snowgum Ries is running in the Huon Valley, Matt Haubrick in Glenorchy and Sam Campbell in Hobart.

They have decided on five “core planks”, three of which they share — affordable housing, more public transport and democracy — and two community-specific planks, formulated from conversations with their communities.

While the electoral system frames all candidates as individuals rather than parties, Campbell told Green Left: “Everyone knows who belongs to what because branding, or at least colour schemes, make it pretty clear.

Campbell said his campaign is focused on making Hobart a “people-focused CBD”, including with fair rates. “It’s about prioritising human connection. This can, in part, be achieved by increasing walkability, expanding free third spaces and cultivating social spontaneity.

“I’m campaigning for streets to be recuperated from cars for the people. We could then re-green them with local native plants, while adding accessible seating, more shade and spaces for pop-up culture, like youth art, social enterprise stalls and community theatre. This is already being done multiple times a year already, so let’s just make it permanent.”

Campbell said a fairer rate system would be based on the use of, and relationship to, the local community. “For example, a residential super-landlord with multiple Short Stay Accommodations (SSAs are like Airbnbs) should pay more, not only for operating grey-hotels, but to compensate for the social costs to the surrounding community.

“Another example could be a commercial premises that lies empty for 90 or more sequential days; the landlord should pay more for not lowering rents or allowing its use for a social benefit, such as a free pop-up art space.

“Pensioners, who may own their homes, but are still struggling with the cost of living should also only have to pay lower rates. Those who can pay more, such as self-funded retirees and those with financial trusts, should pay more.”

Campbell is keen on council promoting “more mixed-use passive-haus developments”, where “a percentage must be guaranteed public homes. With differential rates, it would go a significant way towards improving affordability locally.

“Questions over planning, insurance, licenses and the cost of materials are not insurmountable. For example, council could give automatic approval for developments that meet, or exceed, pre-defined criteria, such as the use of materials like hempcrete, or structures of mass-timber like dowel-laminated (reclaimed, ethical) timber.”

Lester Ries, known as “Snowgum”, has lived and worked in the Huon Valley for their entire life. “That means I’ve seen the harsh conditions that people face and I’ve seen the optimistic grit that comes from it,” they told GL.

“People in the Huon Valley are being hit with housing unaffordability, a lack of infrastructure and healthcare facilities and severe food insecurity. This leads to a dwindling sense of community, which disproportionately affects young people and minority groups.

“Capitalism puts profits ahead of people’s needs and is the root cause of these crises.

“LSA supports setting up ‘People’s voice councils’, where decisions would then inform council policy and community land trusts, which would allow more people access to land.

“We also support a large-scale, non-commercial food security network, which could reliably supply people with the essentials.

“We are also campaigning for greater council transparency and accountability, including by council publishing its accounts and minutes and recording meetings.”

Snowgum, who is 19 years old, said young people are “disproportionately affected by cuts to services and the lack of affordable housing”. While many are sceptical about young councillors, they said young people who are passionate about listening to everyday people’s voices would make the best representatives.

“Councils are supposed to be where people’s voices are heard,” Snowgum said. “Becoming a councillor is also a good way to build support for socialist ideas and solutions to improve people’s everyday lives.”

Haubrick told GL he is campaigning to make the Glenorchy Pool community owned and operated. Given the housing shortages, he said empty homes need to be filled and public transport needs to be improved with better lighting and accessibility.

author: Lance Selfa
title: The hue and cry about the Democratic Socialists
content:
CHICAGO—To US political pundits, a spectre is haunting the Democratic Party. That is, of course, the spectre of “socialism” as embodied in Democratic primary victories for progressives, some of them affiliated with the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA).

The balance sheet for the “socialist” wave won’t be known until the November mid-term elections. But there is a good chance that DSA members could add Los Angeles and Washington, DC, to New York on the roster of US cities with “democratic socialist” mayors. Democratic primary victories in New York, Philadelphia and Denver could add three to four more DSA members to Congress. And DSA-adjacent progressives like Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed could boost liberal Democrats in the next US Congress. 

Also, Florida state Representative Angie Nixon recently defeated a “resistance” celebrity, former Lieutenant Colonel Alexander Vindman, to become the state’s Democratic nominee for the federal Senate. Nixon reported joining the DSA a few weeks before the election. She won despite being outspent sixteen to one.

All of this has caused Democratic establishment figures and long-time DC players like the American Israel Political Action Committee to sound the alarm. Dinosaurs like Bill Clinton adviser James Carville have threatened to leave the party if it doesn’t do something to stop the progressive tide.

A “centrist” Democratic donor group

 composed primarily of investment bankers has announced its intention to spend millions to conduct what amounts to a McCarthyite smear campaign against the DSA and the candidates it supports.

Everyone on the left should oppose these right-wing efforts to smear the DSA, just as we should

oppose government snooping and criminalisation of the left,

 labour unions and liberal non-government organisations.

But the disdain that highly engaged Democratic “base” voters are showing towards the party leaders isn’t ideological, apart from a shift among Democratic voters against automatic support for Israel. What’s really driving the support for progressives is the same thing that is driving support for candidates who (rhetorically at least) say they want to “fight” Trump. That’s the assessment among a significant section of Democratic voters that their “leaders” aren’t up to the task of opposing Trump’s destruction of everything they support.

That so many of those leaders have been in Congress for decades opens the door for younger politicians making the running on a “generational transition” appeal. This is also a non-ideological way of running for “change” in the Democratic Party. In fact, billionaire Democrat donor Stephen Mandel is

devoting his resources

 to promote a new generation of “moderates” and “centrists” against the progressives.

Whether the progressives and “fighters” have a strategy to defeat Trumpism is a topic for another article. In the current anti-incumbent climate, with Trump’s unpopularity trending towards that of Richard Nixon and Jimmy Carter, aspiring Democratic politicians have a low bar to clear to win support. Georgia Senator Jon Ossoff, a moderate

who voted


for the anti-immigrant

 Laken Riley Act, has excited liberals with his

well-curated trolling of Trump

 despite his conventional policy stances. 

The main Democratic watchword during this election season has been “affordability”. That’s hardly a brilliant stroke given that inflation is eroding people’s living standards and polls show that the cost of living is the chief voter concern. But it wasn’t until Zohran Mamdani—campaigning on making New York affordable again—won the 2025 mayor’s race that the Democratic political class took note.

That fact should be a tell on just how threatening to the Democrats the socialist wave is. As

Jacobin

 and

Nation

 publisher

Bhaskar Sunkara, responding to anti-left pundit Jonathan Chait, explained

: 

“[W]e lead with affordability, with rent and health care and the demands that look most winnable. Of course we do. If you cannot assemble enough political power to bring down rents or win universal health care, you are certainly not going to socialise the economy.”

In reality, what the democratic socialists are promoting isn’t “socialism” understood as workers’ control of society. It’s barely even social democracy as practised in Scandinavia for a century. It’s much more akin to the reformed capitalism of Franklin Delano Roosevelt’s 1930s New Deal or Lyndon Johnson’s 1960s Great Society.

title: Όχι στην πειθαρχική δίωξη 2.500 εκπαιδευτικών ενάντια στην αξιολόγηση!
content:
Να επιστρέψει άμεσα η συν. Χρύσα Χοτζόγλου στο σχολείο της! Κανείς/μία εκπαιδευτικός σε δυνητική αργία!


Οι συνδικαλιστικές διώξεις δε θα περάσουν!


 

Πάνω από 2.500 είναι οι πειθαρχικές διώξεις εκπαιδευτικών για τη συμμετοχή τους σε αποφάσεις των σωματείων και των ομοσπονδιών ενάντια στην αντιεκπαιδευτική πολιτική της κυβέρνησης και του ΥΠΑΙΘΑ.


Από αυτές τις 2.500 διωκόμενων, η πλειοψηφία τους είναι νεοδιόριστοι συνάδελφοι που συμμετέχουν στην απεργία αποχή από την Αξιολόγηση, όπως έχει αποτυπωθεί από τις αποφάσεις όλων των σωματείων (ΔΟΕ, ΣΕΠΕ, ΑΔΕΔΥ, ΟΛΜΕ, ΕΛΜΕ). Διώκονται με σκοπό την τρομοκράτησή τους για να καμφθεί ο αγώνας ενάντια στην αξιολόγηση, ο αγώνας για την υπεράσπιση του δωρεάν δημόσιου χαρακτήρα του σχολείου.


Ήδη έχουν αρχίσει οι εκδικάσεις των πειθαρχικών αυτών και έχουμε πλήθος αποφάσεων που όλες απαλλάσσουν τις/τους συναδέλφισσες/ους!


Την ίδια στιγμή έχουν περάσει ήδη 17 μήνες μετά τη θέση της Χρύσας Χοτζόγλου σε αργία για συνδικαλιστική δράση -και με αντίστοιχο ερώτημα διώκεται και ο νεοδιόριστος συνάδελφος Χαρτζουλάκης Δημήτρης-, παρά την ΟΜΟΦΩΝΗ απόφαση του πειθαρχικού συμβουλίου ενάντια στην αργία, κάτι που  αγνοήθηκε επιδεικτικά από τον τότε υπουργό παιδείας. Και ενώ έχει γίνει το 2

ο

 Πειθαρχικό, η συναδέλφισσα παραμένει εκτός σχολείου, το υπουργείο ροκανίζει τον χρόνο, σχετικά με τα χρονικά περιθώρια που προβλέπονται για την έκδοση της υπουργικής απόφασης («

εύλογο χρονικό διάστημα

»), κρατώντας σε ομηρία τη συναδέλφισσα.

Μάλιστα, αμέσως μετά το κλείσιμο των σχολείων δόθηκαν και στους δύο οι γνωμοδοτήσεις του Πειθαρχικού Συμβουλίου που εισηγούνται στην Υπουργό ενάντια στην αργία. Απαιτούμε να γυρίσει τώρα η Χρύσα Χοτζόγλου στο σχολείο και να μην επιβληθεί καμιά αργία για τον συνάδελφο Δ. Χαρτζουλάκη.


Η πολιτική των πειθαρχικών διώξεων δεν είναι ούτε τυχαία ούτε συγκυριακή

: Γιατί στην εκπαίδευση εξελίσσεται μια επιχείρηση σαρώματος δικαιωμάτων και κατακτήσεων τόσο των εργασιακών όσο και των δικαιωμάτων των μαθητών στο σχολείο. Αλλά και συνολικά στην κοινωνία επιχειρείται να επιβληθεί ένας σύγχρονος εργασιακός μεσαίωνας (13ώρες εργασίας, μισθοί που δεν φτάνουν ούτε για ζήτω κ.λπ.), ενώ ότι υπήρχε ως κατάκτηση ανατρέπεται! Γιατί τα σύννεφα του πολέμου που πυκνώνουν επιβάλλουν ακόμα μεγαλύτερη τρομοκρατία και καταστολή. Να μην ακούγεται καμιά φωνή πραγματικής αντίστασης στην κυρίαρχη πολιτική. Σε αυτή την κατεύθυνση ψηφίστηκε και το προηγούμενο καλοκαίρι και ο νέος νόμος για τα Πειθαρχικά που φέρνει αυστηρότερες ποινές, χτυπά το δικαίωμα στην συνδικαλιστική δράση, ανοίγει τον δρόμο για απολύσεις στο δημόσιο.


Για αυτό αποτελεί κεντρικό ζήτημα για τους εκπαιδευτικούς.

 Γιατί δε μπορούν να διεκδικηθούν καλύτεροι μισθοί, περισσότερα εργασιακά δικαιώματα, να υπερασπιστούμε την δωρεάν δημόσια παιδεία αν επικρατήσει σιγή νεκροταφείου.


Είναι γεγονός ότι η κυβέρνηση χρησιμοποιεί την τρομοκρατία και την καταστολή γιατί αδυνατεί να πείσει για την πολιτική της. Γιατί η πλειοψηφία των εκπαιδευτικών δεν πείθεται για τον ρόλο που τους ετοιμάζει να παίξουν στο δημόσιο σχολείο.


Δηλώνουμε την πλήρη και αμέριστη στήριξή μας στους/στις διωκόμενους/ες συνάδελφους/ισσες. Απαιτούμε να σταματήσουν τώρα όλες οι διώξεις, να γυρίσει η Χρύσα στο σχολείο της και να παρθούν πίσω όλες οι απαράδεκτες ποινές, όπου έχουν επιβληθεί.


Σε αυτή την κατεύθυνση τα εκπαιδευτικά συνδικάτα ΔΟΕ, ΟΛΜΕ και τα πρωτοβάθμια σωματεία ΣΕΠΕ, ΕΛΜΕ να κάνουν όλες τις απαραίτητες ενέργειες και κινηματικές πρωτοβουλίες προκειμένου να κινηθούν μαζικά και αποφασιστικά οι εκπαιδευτικοί ενάντια σε όλη αυτή τη βιομηχανία διώξεων!


Όπως δυο χρόνια τώρα, μέσα από αποφάσεις (ΔΣ και Γενικών Συνελεύσεων),  στα σωματεία των δύο διωκόμενων –με απειλή/επιβολή δυνητικής αργίας- εκπαιδευτικών, των ΧΧ και ΔΧ,  ΕΛΜΕ Πειραιά και Α’ ΕΛΜΕ Δυτικής Αττικής αντίστοιχα, μαζί με άλλα πρωτοβάθμια σωματεία, συλλογικότητες και επιτροπές αγώνα, δίνεται η κόντρα και στηρίζονται οι συνάδελφοι ενάντια σε αυτή την απαράδεκτη και πρωτοφανή δίωξή τους.


Να γυρίσει στο σχολείο η Χρύσα Χοτζόγλου! Κανείς άλλος συνάδελφος σε δυνητική αργία!


Κάτω τα χέρια από σωματεία-απεργία-αγώνα!


Η τρομοκρατία δε θα περάσει!


Να παρθούν πίσω όλες οι διώξεις!


Δ.Σ. του Ζ΄ Σ.Ε.Π.Ε. Θεσ/νίκης

author: CMI Argentina
title: Reforma laboral y resistencia sindical: estado de situación
content:
La reforma laboral hace 5 meses que está en vigor, pero su implementación está lejos de ser un proceso lineal. Los decretos reglamentarios se suceden, las cautelares judiciales frenan algunos de sus artículos más lesivos y los sindicatos, en las paritarias, encuentran resquicios para blindar convenios y aportes solidarios que la ley pretendía desactivar. En paralelo, los primeros datos oficiales muestran una tendencia que contradice las promesas oficiales: durante los dos primeros meses de vigencia ya se perdieron casi 20 mil puestos de trabajo registrados en el sector privado. ¿Cómo se está tejiendo esta trama de resistencias y retrocesos? El informe del Instituto de Estudios y Formación de la CTAA recorre las distintas dimensiones de una ofensiva que, desde el Estado, busca reconfigurar de raíz las relaciones entre el capital y el trabajo.


Foto: El Ciudadano.


 


Reforma Laboral Informe Julio 2026


Reforma laboral: reglamentación, resistencias e impacto en el mercado laboral a cinco meses de su aprobación

(1)

 


  1. Introducción


La reforma de la legislación laboral ha sido uno de los ejes centrales de la ofensiva del gobierno de La Libertad Avanza contra los derechos de los trabajadores y trabajadoras. Su primer episodio se plasmó en el capítulo laboral del DNU 70/23 dictado en diciembre de 2023. Esta norma, en su dimensión laboral, fue cuestionada en sede judicial por las centrales de trabajadores y fue declarada inconstitucional por la Cámara Nacional de Apelaciones del Trabajo. Por ende, sus disposiciones no se aplican en la actualidad, pero su contenido guió las posteriores iniciativas legislativas del gobierno nacional.


Pocos meses más tarde, el Congreso Nacional aprobó la Ley Bases, que también incluyó un capítulo laboral donde se recogieron parcialmente algunas de las disposiciones del DNU 70/23.


Finalmente en febrero de 2026 se aprobó la ley de reforma laboral 27.802, que por su extensión y profundidad constituye la modificación regresiva de los derechos de los trabajadores y trabajadoras más importante desde los cambios normativos dispuestos de facto por la última dictadura militar en 1976.


En los tres casos los argumentos del gobierno nacional para justificar estas modificaciones fueron los mismos: se trataría de leyes necesarias para facilitar la creación de empleo formal y para avanzar en la registración laboral de millones de trabajadores y trabajadoras que en la actualidad se desempeñan en la informalidad.


Al tratarse de reformas estructurales, sus efectos sólo podrán ser analizados en el mediano y largo plazo. Asimismo, sus objetivos no se reducen a una única dimensión, por lo que también será necesario considerar las distintas dimensiones alcanzadas. En principio, y sin ser exhaustivos, se trata de un proceso que afecta las relaciones individuales entre empleadores y trabajadores, que busca debilitar la acción colectiva de las organizaciones sindicales y que transfiere recursos multimillonarios del trabajo al capital por vía del desfinanciamiento del sistema de seguridad social.


Todas estas dimensiones son, en cierto sentido, una noticia en continuo desarrollo. El gobierno nacional ha comenzado el proceso de reglamentación de la ley de reforma laboral, cuya finalización todavía está lejos de consumarse. En paralelo, las organizaciones sindicales han impulsado distintas acciones de resistencia, ya sea a través de medidas de fuerza, de presentaciones judiciales y de la negociación colectiva. Finalmente, es posible comenzar a monitorear si los objetivos declamados al momento de aprobar estas reformas se han plasmado en la práctica. Este documento sistematiza las principales acciones llevadas adelante entre marzo y julio de 2026, tanto en el plano reglamentario como en el de la resistencia colectiva impulsada por los trabajadores y trabajadoras.


Foto:

Mat ((i))


  2. La reglamentación de la reforma laboral


La ley 27.802 de reforma laboral entró en vigencia el 6 de marzo de 2026. La gran mayoría de sus artículos comenzaron a implementarse de inmediato; sin embargo, muchos de sus capítulos requieren del dictado de normas reglamentarias.


En mayo de 2026 el gobierno nacional dictó el decreto 315/26 que reglamentó el Régimen de Incentivo a la Formalización Laboral (Título XX de la ley). Posteriormente, a comienzos de junio se dictaron tres decretos que avanzaron sobre la mayoría de las dimensiones de la ley de reforma laboral:

author: Unknown
title: Fascists attack Kurdish seasonal workers in Düzce
content:
Kurdish workers from Mardin, who traveled to the Cumayeri and Gümüşova districts of Düzce in search of work to earn a living, said they were subjected to a fascist attack at the place where they were staying.


Footage sent by the workers to Mezopotamya Agency (MA) shows some moments from the incident. The workers expressed growing concern for their safety after the attack and said they were considering leaving the area.


According to the workers, who did not want to give their names for security reasons, the attack took place in the evening while they were sitting in the garden of the house where they were staying. A group approached the house and one of the assailants pulled a knife on them.


The workers described what happened as follows: “It was evening, and we were sitting in the garden of our house. Suddenly, a group came up to our garden. One of them pulled out a knife and began swearing at us. He told us that we had to leave and that they did not want us here. We were frightened and called the police. The police arrived and took the man away. But now we are genuinely afraid that more attacks could follow. That is why we are considering leaving.”

title: Endorse this Response to the Urgent Appeal From the Palestinian Postal Service Workers Union to US Trade Unions and Labor Federations
content:
Click Here to Endorse This Response to the Urgent Appeal From the Palestinian Postal Service Workers Union to US Trade Unions and Labor Federations

Today in Idhna—as across the West Bank, Gaza, and all of historic Palestine—life for Palestinians is a living nightmare. Part of an accelerated effort to “annex” the West Bank to the Israeli state and to ethnically cleanse the Palestinian population there, the small village just south of the city of Al-Khalil (Hebron) is daily invaded and terrorized by settlers, in full view and with the support of the Israeli Occupation Forces. Villagers such as our union sibling Imad Temeiza are daily assaulted, their properties are vandalized, their livestock are killed, and their crops are burnt. Life has become impossible for Palestinians in the West Bank, as they struggle simply to survive. On the 10th of August, 2026, Imad’s union, the Palestinian Postal Services Workers Union (PPSWU), issued an emergency appeal to trade unions and labor federations around the world to ACT NOW against escalating Zionist settler-colonial violence. The current wave of Israeli state violence–aided and abetted by the government of the United States–is the culmination of what Palestinian historian Rashid Khalidi has called the “hundred years’ war on Palestine.” It is part of the same machine of racism, ethnic cleansing, war, and genocide terrorizing workers and oppressed people around the world, from Palestine, to Iran and Lebanon, to Venezuela, to ICE death camps here at home. author: CNT Galiza
title: La Furia y el Mar: Crónica de una farsa
content:
El 30 de julio de 2026, sucesivas oleadas de inmigrantes comenzaron a llegar a las costas de Ceuta (alrededor de 60.000 personas) y Melilla (entre 1.000 y 2.000). Esta tragedia pone de manifiesto la realidad política y social. A 3 de agosto de 2026, se habían registrado cerca de 100 fallecimientos. No se trata de un fenómeno aislado, sino de algo recurrente: la última vez, en 2021, cerca de 8.000 personas intentaron entrar en Ceuta en menos de 48 horas, 1.500 de ellas menores de edad. En junio de 2022, otras 2.000 lo intentarían, con un saldo de entre 30 y 40 fallecidos. Recordemos las 14 muertes ocurridas en 2005.


Esta no es una historia en memoria de las víctimas; en su honor, solo podemos exigir que se esclarezca la verdadera naturaleza de los hechos. No, esto no es una crisis migratoria. No existe un componente de fuerza mayor, de naturaleza incontrolable. Se trata de un juego, un juego entre Estados que hoy ha dado como resultado un balance de aproximadamente un centenar de peones muertos: una niña de 12 años, inmigrantes procedentes en su mayoría del África subsahariana, muchos jóvenes marroquíes…


Es necesario intentar comprender el escenario que se desarrolla en toda su magnitud, dada la confluencia de actores y fenómenos. En geopolítica, es necesario examinarlo por partes para tener una idea general. Así, tenemos diferentes gobiernos y Estados involucrados cuyas relaciones son asimétricas e interdependientes. Esto significa que, si bien Europa y sus socios son vasallos del bloque EE. UU.-Israel-OTAN, no existe correspondencia en lo que respecta al establecimiento de acuerdos o políticas de ningún tipo. Una parte es más dependiente que la otra. Es fácil ver hacia dónde se dirigen los acontecimientos.


Mientras tanto, en el plano político, los Estados europeos mostraron su repudio a la situación, exigiendo el cierre del espacio Schengen con España (tratados y acuerdos europeos que garantizan la libre circulación por los territorios miembros), con un total de representantes de veintidós países.


En la península, la estabilidad política del gobierno de Sánchez sufre otro ataque de la ultraderecha, que reclama unidad nacional ante una supuesta invasión popular. Pretenden culpar de todo el episodio a las recientes medidas de regularización masiva. Una más de las que se han dado en el pasado en toda Europa, dada la necesidad de mano de obra vulnerable y sumisa, además de afectar al mercado laboral reforzando el desempleo como elemento de control y reduciendo las condiciones laborales y los salarios. La interpretación es la siguiente: primero, el culpable siempre es el inmigrante; y segundo, se trata de una historia donde los intereses más reaccionarios del bloque aliado occidental convergen con los de la derecha indígena. Debemos estar atentos a cómo se cristalizan las tensiones internas de la UE, revelando su verdadera naturaleza. En otoño, la situación empeorará con la crisis energética y el frío extremo.


Porque nuestro problema no son los pobres que vienen de fuera, sino cómo se administran los mecanismos y los recursos propios. Cómo el gobierno actual utiliza su capacidad para distribuir dividendos y apoyar políticas que perpetúan la desigualdad estructural, el desempleo y el miedo. Los trabajadores debemos unir fuerzas contra esta falta de control egoísta para lograr la gestión de los recursos públicos, los medios de producción y la industria que nos permiten decidir.


Al otro lado del estrecho, el reino de Marruecos se alinea con Estados Unidos, Israel y la OTAN. Su futuro depende de ello. Además, las presiones que puede ejercer un socio con la influencia y la posición estratégica de Marruecos lo convierten en un interlocutor privilegiado para la región. Domina físicamente el flanco atlántico sudoccidental; junto con España y el Reino Unido, controla la ruta mediterránea del estrecho de Gibraltar; actúa como nodo entre Europa y África y, además, influye en las rutas hacia el Magreb y el Sahel, el corazón del continente africano.


A pesar de no pertenecer a la organización fascista atlántica, existe una relación estratégica desde la Guerra Fría: cooperación en ejercicios militares, operaciones de inteligencia, contratos millonarios… podemos observar cómo se despliegan las influencias.


En el plano económico, encontramos una serie de intereses estratégicos arraigados entre los diversos estados en conflicto. Estos se caracterizan por la ejecución de procesos que perduran durante generaciones y cuyo …

content:

Olay yerine çok sayıda sağlık ekibi sevk edildi

title: The P85 wage standoff
content:
For most workers who live on a tight budget, the suspension of wage hike is more than a legal development. It is a delay in money they had been counting on.

MANILA – At around 6:00 am, while much of Metro Manila is only beginning to stir, Carlo Palajos, 41, is already preparing for another day of work.

As a saucemaker at a sardines company, his work is tied to production schedules—long hours, daily demands and, when required, overtime.

For most workers like Palajos, the day begins with work. But before the first task is done, another calculation is already running in the back: How far will today’s wage go?

The answer has become harder to stretch as the prices of food and other necessities continue to rise.

“The cost of goods here in Manila is very high. Our current minimum wage of P695 ($11.24) feels like it is only worth P300 ($4.86),” Palajos said, describing the rising cost of living in the capital.

For him, the proposed wage increase is not simply a figure announced through a wage order. It is money that could be converted into something tangible at home—food on the table, transportation to work, or another household expense paid on time.

“It’s disappointing because even P55 ($0.89) is enough to buy a kilogram of rice,” he said, illustrating what even a small increase could mean to a worker’s daily budget.

But the additional income workers were expecting has been put on hold.

The P85 (more than $1) increase under the National Capital Region (NCR) wage order was supposed to provide workers with additional income in two tranches. Its implementation, however, was suspended following a court order, leaving workers like Palajos waiting for relief they had hoped would help ease the pressure of everyday expenses.

For most workers who live on a tight budget, the suspension of wage hike is more than a legal development. It is a delay in money they had been counting on.

Palajos described the difficulty of covering expenses from his existing income, including transportation and other daily necessities. Depending on production, workers may also have to work overtime to supplement their earnings.

The value of the increase becomes clearer when translated into the language of a worker’s household budget.

Eighty five pesos is not simply P85. It is food, fare, bills, a little breathing room.

The expected increase, however, is now at the center of a legal dispute.

Lawyer Arman Hernandez, legal affairs officer of the Center for Trade and Human Rights, said construction companies Rebicon Trading and Construction Corporation and R2 Builders filed a petition for declaratory relief before the Regional Trial Court in Pasig.

The companies argued that implementing the wage order could cause irreparable damage to their businesses and affect their right to a fair return on investment.

The court subsequently issued an order suspending the implementation of the wage order.

But Hernandez questioned whether a regular trial court has jurisdiction to suspend a wage order issued by the Regional Tripartite Wages and Productivity Board (RTWPB).

“The courts have no role in implementing wage orders,” Hernandez said, pointing to provisions of the Labor Code concerning the authority of regional wage boards and the National Wage and Productivity Commission (NWPC).

For workers, the legal dispute has a direct consequence: they cannot yet enjoy the additional wages provided under the wage order while the restraining order remains in effect.

Whether workers will receive the increase retroactively if the temporary restraining order (TRO) is lifted remains subject to guidelines from the wage board.

He also said that workers should receive the increase retroactively.

“The RTWPB needs to issue guidelines. In our stand as lawyers and workers. We want to have a retroactive effect because it’s long overdue,” he said.

For labor advocates, the dispute is rooted in a larger problem: workers’ purchasing power is being squeezed by rising prices.

Jerome Adonis, Kilusang Mayo Uno Chairperson, said workers had pushed for the wage increase amid rising prices and declining purchasing power. The approved increase was supposed to provide P60 beginning July 25, followed by another P25 in January.

The suspension, he said, has frustrated workers who had already been waiting for the increase.

“That’s why the workers are angry,” Adonis said.

author: groundxero
title: They Burned Books Then, They Attack Universities Now: Fascism’s War on Knowledge and  Dissent
content:
They may threaten to ‘sew Jadavpur’s mouth shut’. But a university with thousands of students, teachers and workers cannot be silenced by a threat.


 


By

Tanuj Mullick


 


On 10 May 1933, books were burned by the Nazis in cities across Germany. Known as Die Bücherverbrennung am 10. Mai, the event was not merely the destruction of thousands of books. It was a public political programme aimed at establishing control over knowledge, thought, history and freedom of expression. Books written by Jews, communists, socialists, liberals, pacifists and others who were considered enemies of Nazism were declared ‘un-German’ and thrown into the flames.


 


Nearly a century later, when we look at the events that took place at Jadavpur University on 19–20 August, a question inevitably arises: has fascism changed its methods while continuing to attempt to control knowledge, universities and dissenting voices?


 


On the night of 19 August, BJP MLA for Jadavpur, Sharvari Mukherjee, allegedly issued a call in a video for ‘tandav’ at Jadavpur University. Within a short time of the video going viral on social media and being reported by the news media, at around 12:30 a.m., a mob entered Jadavpur University through Gate No. 4.


 


The mob was carrying ABVP flags, rods and sticks and chanting ‘Jai Shri Ram’. Immediately after entering the campus, they allegedly began vandalism and attempted arson.


 


Videos of the entire episode were subsequently made available by a news outlet called Mrittika TV. The faces of several members of the mob can reportedly be seen in the footage. Students of the university identified most of them as people who were not students of Jadavpur University. The one or two individuals who were recognised as students were identified as members of NSF or ABVP.


 


Among them was Aditya Haldar, a student of the History Department who had recently contested the ICC election as an NSF-supported candidate. Alongside him was Somsurya Banerjee of the Electronics and Telecommunication Department, who is alleged to be an NSF member.


 


Some students who were present on campus found themselves directly in front of the mob. Several of them were reportedly beaten severely. Around thirty students were forced to take shelter inside Aurobindo Bhavan, locking themselves in an attempt to save their lives.


 


The mob allegedly continued its attack for a considerable period. They attempted to set fire to Aurobindo Bhavan, threw chocolate bombs, bricks and water bottles, and continued hurling abuses at the students trapped inside.


 


Here one has to ask a very simple question:


 


How did a mob of this size manage to enter the university at around 12:30 a.m. without facing any resistance whatsoever?


 


Does the university not have adequate security?


 


The available information suggests otherwise.


 


A few months ago, despite protests by several students, the university administration had removed its old security guards and appointed ex-servicemen as guards, supposedly to ensure the safety of students. These guards reportedly check students’ identity cards before allowing them to enter the campus, even during the day.


 


Yet CCTV footage allegedly shows that when a mob of approximately sixty people entered through Gate No. 4 that night, the guards were standing there. They reportedly did not check the identity cards of those entering. Even after the mob entered the campus and began its alleged rampage, the guards did not intervene.


 


The CCTV footage reportedly also shows that, at that moment, a staff member of the English Department, Rasman Kanaujjia, was present alongside the guards at Gate No. 4. He is alleged to be a member of the BJP’s employees’ organisation at the university. Also reportedly present was former Jadavpur University Vice-Chancellor Biswanath Sau, who is known as one of the leading figures of the BJP’s teachers’ organisation at Jadavpur.


 


What were the two of them doing there at midnight?


 


This question alone makes the allegation that the attack on the students was carefully planned particularly serious.


 


After questioning the role of the security guards, one must also question the role of the police.


 


While trapped inside Aurobindo Bhavan, several students reportedly tried to contact the police. According to their accounts, when they identified themselves as students of Jadavpur University, the police allegedly disconnected the calls.

Cette malveillance se conjugue selon nous avec un recul des droits sexuels et reproductifs, poussant les collectivités locales à baisser leurs budgets pour les associations. L'une d'entre elles nommée «

 

Familya

Ces antennes nous semblent en effet particulièrement impactées par les baisses de subventions. Si nous observons souvent une couverture de ce sujet de la part de la presse locale, la presse nationale peine elle à s'en saisir.


L'antenne nationale du Planning a pourtant communiqué en juin 2025 à ce propos. Si une partie de la presse nationale l'a répercuté, elle n'a pas fait de même pour les conséquences que cela entraîne au niveau local.

title: Presse-Umgang mit „Alternative für Deutschland“: Je weniger, desto besser
content:
Dossier


„

Viele Journalisten stellen sich die Frage, ob sie die „Alternative für Deutschland“ (AfD) behandeln sollen, wie jede andere Partei auch? Dabei müsste die Frage eher lauten: reicht es, wenn sich Journalistinnen und Journalisten für Gespräche mit der AfD so vorbereiten, wie bei anderen auch? (…) Für Journalist*innen ist es wichtig zu wissen, wie Populismus funktioniert. Viele Leute denken fälschlich, es gehe darum, dass Politiker einfache Wahrheiten aussprechen und dabei provozieren. Aber Populismus ist kein rhetorisches Stilmittel, sondern eine Ideologie. (…) die AfD würde die unliebsame „Systempresse“ gern abschaffen. Sie hinterfragt die Legitimation unserer Arbeit – insbesondere die der öffentlich-rechtlichen Medien. Gleichzeitig braucht sie die etablierten Medien, um ihre Themen in die Debatten zu einzubringen. (…) Redaktionen könnten sich vor der Berichterstattung diese Fragen stellen: Wie geht man kritisch mit ihrer irreführenden Selbsteinordnung um und ordnet sie richtig ein? (…) Muss man ihr bei jeder/dieser Provokation eine Plattform bieten?

…“

Artikel von Ferda Ataman vom 1. Dezember 2019 aus der dju-Zeitung mmm


 und mehr zur wichtigen Debatte:


Ulrich Siegmund als neuer Posterboy im Spiegel oder Wie die Radikalität der AfD normalisiert wird


Halbloyale Demokraten: Wie die Radikalität der AfD normalisiert wird


„Am 6. September, in gut sechs Wochen, findet die wohl wichtigste deutsche Wahl dieses Jahres statt, nämlich die Landtagswahl in Sachsen-Anhalt. Seit Monaten liegt die AfD in allen Umfragen klar vorn, stets um die 40 Prozent, mit kaum mehr einholbarem Abstand vor der Union, deren Werte bei um die 25 Prozent stagnieren. Damit besteht für die AfD unter für sie günstigen Vorzeichen sogar die Chance auf eine absolute Mehrheit – und damit auf die Alleinregierung. Das Ziel ist klar: Die Partei will in diesem ostdeutschen Bundesland mit seinen zwei Millionen Einwohnern einen Präzedenzfall für ganz Deutschland schaffen. »Wir schreiben gerade Geschichte, und was hier in Sachsen-Anhalt geschieht, ist erst der Anfang«, sagt selbstbewusst ihr Spitzenkandidat Ulrich Siegmund gegenüber der dänischen Wochenzeitung »Weekendavisen«. Die AfD setzt auf die Dominostrategie: Sachsen-Anhalt macht den Anfang, dann folgt Mecklenburg-Vorpommern und am Ende der Bund. So ist der Plan, getreu der Devise: »First we take Magdeburg, then we take Berlin.« (…) Von einer Mäßigung im Sinne einer »Melonisierung« kann keine Rede sein, im Gegenteil: Mit der Aussicht auf den ersten Wahlsieg wird die AfD immer unverfrorener. (…) Die AfD wird zunehmend salon- und regierungsfähig gemacht – vor allem in den Medien. Längst unternimmt ein immer größer werdender Kreis von Akteuren alles mögliche, um eine Koalition mit der AfD vorzubereiten – und zwar durch die systematisch betriebene »Normalisierung« der Partei. Die Idee dahinter ist klar: Wenn die AfD sich nicht entradikalisiert, muss man ihre Radikalität normalisieren, um sie auf diese Weise koalitionsfähig zu machen – durch eine gezielte Verharmlosung der Partei. Anstatt der – zum Scheitern verurteilten – Rödder-Lucke-Linie zu folgen, die AfD über deren Anerkennung roter Linien in die Mitte zu locken, unternehmen diese sich selbst als bürgerlich definierenden Kräfte das glatte Gegenteil: Sie machen die radikale AfD anschluss- und koalitionsfähig, indem sie diese zu einer ganz normalen Partei erklären. (…) Bei dieser Normalisierung der AfD gibt es einen regelrechten Überbietungswettbewerb unter Führung der neuen »sozialen« Medien – aber in markantem Zusammenspiel mit dem Springer-Verlag, sprich: mit »Bild« und »Welt«. (…) Inzwischen gibt es eine fast schon illustre mediale Querfront der AfD-Unterstützer, wenn etwa am »1. Demokratiekongress der AfD-Bundestagsfraktion« neben Roger Köppel – Ex-»Welt«-Chef und heute Chefredakteur der rechten Schweizer »Weltwoche« – auch Holger Friedrich teilnimmt, Verleger der »Berliner Zeitung« und der neuen »Ostdeutschen Allgemeinen Zeitung«, beides Organe, die einen klaren Pro-Russland und Pro-AfD-Kurs fahren. Sollte also tatsächlich am 6. September die Stunde der AfD schlagen, dann wird es auch die Stunde der Reichelts und Poschardts, der Döpfners und Martensteins, der Köppels und Friedrichs gewesen sein. Sie alle haben die AfD erst salonfähig gemacht – indem sie deren rechte Narrative bedienen und damit verharmlosen – und könnten sie so am Ende auch mehrheitsfähig gemacht haben. In wenigen Wochen werden wir es wissen.“

author: Ruby Healer
title: Old traditions of anti-Catholic hate lie beneath UK race riots
content:
Summers in Britain now follow a predictable pattern. 

Southport, England, 2024—racist riots spread after far-right activists falsely blame a stabbing attack on an “illegal Muslim immigrant”. 

Trafalgar Square, London, 2025—anti-Islam hatemonger Tommy Robinson leads the country’s largest ever anti-immigration march after months of rolling protests target refugees and demand mass deportations. 

Belfast, Northern Ireland, 2026—arson attacks, mob violence and protests extend to Scotland and England following a murder committed by a man with Indian heritage.

For three years in a row, Britain has been seized by summertime racist rioting. Islamophobes and nationalists seem to have laid claim to UK streets for the months of June through September. But this is not without precedent: summer has always been high time for bigots and diehard patriots.

It’s the period when Protestant communities in Ireland, Northern Ireland, Scotland and the western part of England habitually mobilise in displays of hatred against Catholics and to show their loyalty to the British state. Colloquially, it has always been “marching season”.

Protestant “loyalism” is a particularly virulent, pro-empire strain of chauvinism that originated with Britain’s historic occupation of Ireland. Beginning in the sixteenth century, English rulers conducted savage campaigns of land confiscation, slaughter and settlement over the whole island. 

British authorities sought to displace local Gaelic-speaking populations, who were largely Catholic. In their place, English and Scottish landlords and aspirational farmers were encouraged to occupy stolen land in resource-rich areas. Catholics were subjected to an oppressive legal regime that denied them the right to vote or hold public office, to own land, to purchase weapons or to freely publish literature. 

From 1690 to 1860, famines and mass evictions of poor peasants from the Scottish highlands compelled large numbers to migrate to the northern part of Ireland. Settlers in the north were explicitly required to adhere to the Protestant faith, speak only English and repudiate any Gaelic heritage they might share with the native Irish population. This was the beginning of the exclusive ethno-religious state that would later become “Northern Ireland”.

Most of Ireland won formal independence from British rule in the 1920s after a particularly fierce decade of revolt against the English crown. But reactionary pro-British capitalists and landowners refused to surrender control of the prosperous industrialised north. They armed and mobilised the Protestant population against the Irish independence movement, deliberately painting a struggle over national liberation in religious colours. In 1921, the British state partitioned the island, granting partial autonomy to a “Free State” in the south (later the Republic of Ireland) but establishing a separate administration in the north-eastern region of Ulster that would remain under British protection.

The modern state of Northern Ireland was officially founded on a two-thirds Protestant demographic majority. This was imposed through tremendous violence. Hundreds of pro-independence Catholics were murdered in Belfast from 1920 to 1922, and 23,000 were hounded from their homes. At least 11,000 Catholic (and many sympathetic Protestant) trade unionists were ejected from workplaces in the north. British troops oversaw mass evictions of Catholic civilians from previously mixed neighbourhoods, and paramilitary brigades of reactionary Protestant settlers were created under British supervision.

Soon after partition, the northern ruling class eagerly agreed to remain under the English crown, joining the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland. Indeed, many northern “loyalists” hoped (and still hope) for a total restoration of British dominance and for the whole island to be ethnically cleansed. It’s this despicable legacy that modern-day loyalism celebrates: loyalty to the British empire, to counter-revolution and to racial supremacy.

This tradition remains one of the key foundations of modern British nationalism. It is not uncommon in Northern Ireland today to see a Protestant child leave the face-painting booth at a summer carnival with the letters “KAT” daubed across their little forehead. “Kill All Taigs” (“Taig” is an ethnic slur for people of native Irish descent) is still a common catch cry alongside “KAC” (“Kill All Catholics”) and “KAI” (“Kill All Irish”) …

author: By L. Cam Anderson, Contributor
title: Minneapolis Once Again Thwarts White Supremacist Jake Lang
content:
Minneapolis, MN — Minneapolis police arrested white supremacist provocateur Edward Jacob “Jake” Lang Saturday afternoon after hundreds of Minneapolis residents came out to protest his second hate rally in front of city hall this year.


After a less than 10 minute exchange and Lang and his security left, the police department charged Lang and several others with probable cause riot, a misdemeanor, and impounded the two vehicles they used for the event. Before the arrests, police allowed Lang to drive along the sidewalk in front of city hall.


This marks the second time Lang met fierce resistance while demonstrating in the City of Lakes,

with his last anti-Islam march resulting in him needing stitches in the back of his head and being rescued by the very people he preaches hate against

. What separates this display, other than him hiding away in a truck and hiring private security guards to accompany him, is the city charging him for a crime.


Lang appeared in the bed of a black Honda Ridgeline followed by a white SUV with flashing lights in its front window before the anticipated start time, with a megaphone and a large sign announcing that “Jake Lang […] hates n*****.” Whatever Lang was shouting was quickly drowned out by the cacophony of counter-protesters who swarmed the truck, which drove on the sidewalk alongside city hall.


Lang first marketed his march as the “N-word March,” he spelled it out in full on his AI created flyer. Lang said the event was to protest

the verdict against Rochester, Minnesota, resident Shiloh Hendrix

, who was found guilty of disorderly conduct in July after being filmed in April last year calling an 8-year-old boy the same racial slur at a playground. The day before the event, Lang began marketing it as the “Crusader Freedom of Speech Rally,” ostensibly to fit the “crusade” that began with his last appearance in Dearborn, Michigan.


In the original flyer, Hendrix was teased as a potential speaker, as if this event would have gone any other way.


Five others appeared alongside Lang in the bed of the truck, including Jayden Scott, 23, of Bay City, Michigan, who held a large, white crucifix resembling a thin, picket fence. Scott, one of Lang’s Christian crusaders, was recently denied custody of his children and has been following Lang while missing his own court dates.


Also in the truck was John William-Kei Irwin, 32, of Sterling Heights, Michigan, wearing a gray Under Armor hoodie and waving an American Flag. 


Laying down in the truck bed and dressed in military fatigues with a beret was Charles Oscar Miles, Jr., 73, of Ecorse, Michigan. On multiple occasions, Miles can be seen pepper spraying protesters approaching the side of the truck from his low-profile position.


A man dressed in a tight-fitting Spider Man suit wasted no time by climbing on top of the truck within a minute of its appearance and lunged at Lang, hitting him multiple times in the face before being pulled over the top by one of the six whose face was concealed under a camouflage balaclava, pulling him overboard head-first onto the concrete.


Private security guards dressed in eclectic military-style gear that included black hardhats and GoPro cameras exited the white SUV and wildly hosed the crowd down with pepper spray, not even sparing Lang and his entourage, who were still being pelted with whatever protesters could get their hands on.


One security guard wearing a beige tactical helmet casually sprayed into the crowd with one hand without looking where he was pointing, passively waving his arm back and forth as protesters and press gagged and coughed on a cloud of noxious fumes.


Minneapolis police officers filed out of city hall where they had been waiting, encircling the truck and providing Lang with an escort as his convoy made its way down Fourth Street from Third Avenue South to Fourth Avenue South, all the while continuing to drive on the sidewalk.


The throngs of angry counter-protesters pelted Lang and the others with bottles, water balloons and debris.


At the end of the sidewalk, police officers cleared the way for the truck by dispersing counter-protesters and moving metal barricades. Ultimately, both trucks were able to speed off, disappearing around a corner.

title: ZH 12.09.26 Demo Justice4Nzoy
content:
Samstag, 12. September 2026, 14 Uhr Landesmuseum Zürich: Justice4Nzoy! Demonstration gegen Rassismus, Polizeigewalt und die Aufrüstung der Herrschenden.


Am 30. August 2021 – vor fünf Jahren – wurde Nzoy am Bahnhof von Morges erschossen. Es fielen drei Schüsse, dann wurde Nzoy minutenlang liegen gelassen – ohne medizinische Hilfe. Die Polizisten, die Nzoy ermordet haben, sind weiterhin bewaffnet im Dienst. Bis heute kämpfen Angehörige und solidarische Menschen für Gerechtigkeit. Der juristische Weg ist zermürbend und lang. Der Prozess gegen die Polizisten steht noch aus. Bei Polizeieinsätzen im Kanton Waadt allein wurden in den letzten Jahren auch Lamin Fatty, Hervé Mandundu, Mike Ben Peter, Michael Kenechukwu Ekemezie, die 14-jährige Camila und der 17-jährige Marvin getötet.


Diese Gewalt existiert nicht im luftleeren Raum. Rassistische und nationalistische Positionen werden normalisiert und schaffen ein gesellschaftliches Klima, das Ausgrenzung und Gewalt legitimiert. Diese Verschiebung bleibt nicht bei Worten. Die Entmenschlichung rassifizierter Menschen, anti-Schwarzer Rassismus, Racial Profiling und tödliche Polizeigewalt – ob an den Grenzen Europas oder im Innern der Gesellschaft – sind keine Fehler des Systems, sondern Teil seiner Funktionsweise. Während die Lebensbedingungen für viele Menschen schlechter werden, investieren die Herrschenden Milliarden in Armeen, Polizei, Grenzschutz und Überwachung. Gespart wird bei Bildung, Gesundheit und Sozialleistungen. Aufrüstung dient dabei nicht nur der Durchsetzung staatlicher Herrschaft, sondern eröffnet zugleich neue Profite für die Rüstungsindustrie und das Kapital. Besonders deutlich sieht man das etwa bei der Unterstützung des israelischen Genozids an der palästinensischen Bevölkerung.


Doch so allgegenwärtig diese Verhältnisse erscheinen mögen – sie bleiben nicht unwidersprochen. Weltweit organisieren sich Menschen gegen Krieg, Besatzung, Aufrüstung, Rassismus und staatliche Gewalt. Auch im Fall von Nzoy hat sich gezeigt, dass organisierter Druck von unten Wirkung zeigt.


Durch den beharrlichen Kampf von Angehörigen, Freund:innen und solidarischen Menschen konnte die Forderung nach Gerechtigkeit nicht zum Schweigen gebracht werden.


Nzoy ist nicht vergessen. Gehen wir am 12. September gemeinsam auf die Strasse und tragen unsere Wut über rassistische Polizeigewalt, die tödliche Abschottung Europas und die Aufrüstung der Herrschenden nach aussen. Gerechtigkeit für Nzoy bedeutet, die Verantwortlichen zur Rechenschaft zu ziehen. Und sie bedeutet auch, jene Verhältnisse zu bekämpfen, die solche Gewalt immer und immer wieder hervorbringen!


Auf ihre Gewalt antworten wir mit Solidarität! Auf ihre Spaltung antworten wir mit gemeinsamen Kämpfen! Gegen Rassismus, Kapitalismus, staatliche Gewalt und die Aufrüstung der Herrschenden!

*Bu yazı ilk olarak Siyasi Haber'de

yayımlanmıştır


9 aydır sürmekte olan süreç nihayetinde, Meclis Komisyonu raporundan sonra ikinci ürününü 10 Ağustos 2026 tarihinde “Milli Dayanışma ve Toplumsal Bütünleşmenin Güçlendirilmesine Dair Kanun” olarak verdi. 


Bugün yasanın eksiklerini söyleyen, onun tekniği açısından taşıdığı hukuksuzluğu dile getiren ve yöntemini eleştiren ya da iktidarın niyetlerinden kuşkulanan herkes süreç ve yasaya pembe gözlüklerle olumlu anlamlar yükleyenlerin bir çoğu tarafından savaşın sürmesini istiyormuş gibi kabullenilip kendilerine “süreç sabotörü” etiketi kolaylıkla yapıştırılıyor ve dolaysıyla da yasanın eleştirel bir gözle ele alınmasının, mevcut haliyle ne tür sıkıntıları peşinde sürükleyeceğinin nesnellik içerisinde değerlendirilebilmesinin ve varsa ilerletilebilmesinin imkanlarının ortaya çıkarılmasının da önüne geçilmiş oluyor. Bunun gelecek açısından yarattığı zaafların demokrasi mücadelesine ve Kürt Özgürlük Hareketine verebileceği zararlarının görülebilmesinin ve karşı tedbirlerinin alınmasının önüne de geçilmiş oluyor.


Barika-i hakikat müsademe-i efkardan doğar vecizesini Marksist temelde kavrayan bir komünist olarak özgürlük mücadelesine ve Türkiye demokrasisine karşı taşıdığım sorumluluğun ve yandaşlığın bir gereği olması açısından çıkan yasa ve bunun işaret ettiği sürecin akıbeti konusundaki eleştirel düşüncelerimi ortaya koymayı 60 yıldır taşıdığım komünist sorumluluğun bir gereği olarak her zaman yerine getirmeye çalıştım ve bu tutumdan da ne özgürlük hareketine ne de demokrasi ve sosyalizm mücadelesine bir zarar geldi. Tam tersine Marks’ın işaret ettiği eleştiriyi kendisine karşı sonuçlar çıkaracak derecede ileriye götürmenin, sosyalist demokrasi, demokratik bir işçi sınıfını perspektifinin geliştirilmesi, işçi sınıfı öncülüğünün mahiyetinin sınıf indirgemeciliğine indirgenerek bürokrasinin egemenliğinin kapılarının sonuna kadar açılmasının engellenmesi, milli meseleler, kadın sorunu, ekoloji sorunlarının kavranışı ve şimdilik dijital/yapay zeka diye adlandırılan insan dışındaki yeni bir zeki varoluşun ortaya çıkmakta olduğu, insanlığın tarih öncesinden özgür insanlık tarihinin girişine ulaştığımız dijital kapitalizm ve yeni çağın kavranmasında ve buna uygun tutumların geliştirilmesinde derinlik kazanılmasına katkısının olduğunu gördük.


İçinden geldiğim Kurtuluş geleneği tüm milli meseleleri birçokları için olduğu gibi, PKK hareketinin bu meseleyi devletin de gözüne sokarcasına gündemleştirdiği dönemde değil, henüz PKK yokken, kuruluşunun başlangıcından beri kendisi için sorun edinmiş ve özel olarak da Kürtlerin kendi kaderlerini tayin hakkını “ayrı devlet kurma hakkı” olarak kabul edip bunu koşulsuz savunmuş ve bedelini ödemiş bir örgütlenmedir. Bu örgütlenme kendi tespitlerine bağlı olarak, PKK önderliğinin Kürdistan devriminin yolunu açtığı tespitine dayanarak, 1991 Kongresinde Kürdistan’da PKK’nin desteklenmesini kabul edip, Kürdistan özerk örgütlenmesine de son vermiştir. PKK’nin 20 yıldır ki benimsemiş olduğu  “her parçanın sorununun sömürgeci devlet çerçevesinde çözülmesi ve bunlar arasında konfederal bir ilişkinin geliştirilmesi” görüşlerinin bugün için olan pratik anlamını kabul etmekle beraber, mili meselelerin gerçek çözümünün önce eşitliği sağlayacak bir ayrılıktan, yani her milletin kendi devletine sahip olup eşitlenmesinden sonra ancak konfederal ilişkilerin her tarafı tatmin eden en demokratik zeminde hayat bulacağına inanıyorum.

author: A.N.A.
title: Fascismo imaginário, a farsa eleitoral e a crítica anarquista
content:
Uma leitura anarquista das eleições como engrenagem de reprodução do capitalismo e da produção de antagonismos imaginários


Por

 

Rick Afonso-Rocha

 | 

16/04/2026


A crítica anarquista às eleições burguesas, formulada por muitos autores, dentre os quais se destaca Errico Malatesta, incide sobre a própria forma da democracia representativa liberal. Longe de denunciar imperfeições ou desvios, o que se põe à mesa é o reconhecimento e a denúncia de que o processo eleitoral burguês constitui, a um só tempo, mecanismo de reprodução da dominação, de neutralização das contradições, de pacificação da luta de classes e de ocultamento do antagonismo real, inclusive pela maximização de antagonismos imaginários, a saber: 

direita vs. esquerda, família vs. perversão, cristianismo vs. destruição dos valores ocidentais, masculinidade cristã vs. ideologia de gênero, liberdade vs. marxismo cultural 

ou ainda

 retrocesso vs. progressismo, 

fascismo

 vs. liberalismo, direitos humanos vs. barbárie, cidadania vs. servidão

 etc.


Em nossa leitura, a eleição não abre possibilidades. Ao contrário, ela as fecha previamente, organizando a política como escolha controlada entre gestores da mesma ordem. Participar desse circuito não tensiona a exploração. Participar desse circuito legitima a exploração capitalista sob a forma de decisão. Cria-se a ilusão de que fazemos parte do processo, que podemos escolher, que somos nós que decidimos o futuro político e que a política exerce dominância sobre o econômico. E o econômico, mesmo quando pulula em nossas narinas, evidenciando a regra do jogo, é moralizado, reduzido à corrupção de alguns políticos, de modo a mobilizar a esperança no surgimento do eterno novo líder, da nova política, da política como gestão, da política como empreendimento.


O econômico sobredetermina. E não estamos falando de interesses ordinários individuais de alguns representantes das facções burguesas que financiam as eleições. O que vemos é um circo, um teatro. Nada se escolhe. Nada se decide. As eleições são uma farsa. Não exatamente porque são fraudadas. Não existe tal necessidade. A farsa eleitoral diz da ontologia da política burguesa, diz da democracia liberal e dos seus limites estruturais, diz da sua razão de ser e do seu funcionamento no edifício mercantil.


Essa engrenagem depende da produção contínua de uma 

cena de conflito

. A polarização entre projetos institucionalizados funciona como encenação reiterada, na qual tudo aparece em disputa enquanto nada de estrutural se transforma. Nesse sentido, simula-se o antagonismo entre dois polos da institucionalidade burguesa. Sim, entre eles temos divergências em relação ao 

modus operandi

 de gerenciamento da ordem capitalista; temos interesses conflitantes entre as facções burguesas. Mas não há divergência quanto à exploração da classe trabalhadora nem quanto à destruição da natureza. Em tempos de, digamos, 

normalidade institucional

 (sempre temporária, dado as crises estruturais do modo de produção capitalista), esse conflito tende a explorar a linguagem humanista civilizatória, mascarando, necessariamente, sua política estruturante imperialista e colonial. Assume-se uma gramática “politicamente correta”. Fala-se em 

direitos humanos

 e em 

progresso

. As eleições são dominadas por termos técnicos e temas menos “polêmicos”. Pauta-se a segurança pública, o investimento em educação e saúde. E os aspectos morais, via de regra, resumem-se às questões de corrupção e desvio do dinheiro público. No espectro político, emula-se a expansão do centro: centro-direita, centro e centro-esquerda. O discurso neoliberal impõe-se sem a necessidade de simular dissenso. A crítica ao neoliberalismo até é formulada, mas sem a necessidade de simular radicalidade.


Essa encenação, contudo, se intensifica precisamente em tempos de crise. E aqui a 

crise

 ultrapassa a noção de dado econômico; ela comparece como operador discursivo estratégico da exploração capitalista. A 

austeridade

, tal como analisada por Clara Mattei, e a lógica da “

doutrina do choque

“, nos termos de Naomi Klein, não apenas respondem à crise, elas a produzem, a dramatizam, a administram e a exploram como condição de possibilidade para o avanço da ordem capitalista. Por isso, a crise é estruturante ao modo de produção capitalista. Nesse cenário, a ordem do capital fabrica e administra o dissenso. Simula-se uma radicalidade que não ameaça o sistema, mas o estabiliza. Inaugura-se a denúncia de …

author: Harriet Williamson & Simon Childs
title: Revealed: The Chart-Topping Music Producer and Animator Behind a Far-Right AI Rapper
content:
The identities of two men behind an AI-generated far-right rapper who sings about how immigration has broken Britain can be revealed for the first time.


Danny Bones is a sharp-cheekboned skinhead whose music videos show him rapping about the decline of Britain, speeding a deportation van through London and fighting a civil war against the “Islamist Front”.


Since we first wrote about him

, Danny Bones has appeared at an event organised by Stephen Yaxley-Lennon – AKA Tommy Robinson. At his Unite the Kingdom rally in May, Robinson told the crowd that a “war of propaganda” is taking place, before the video for the Danny Bones song ‘This Is England’ was played.


But while Danny Bones’ video was projected onto screens outside parliament, he is entirely fictional.


The AI character and the hyperreal universe he inhabits were created by the Node Project, a shadowy creative agency which shares and monetises Danny Bones content. The identity of the individuals behind the Node Project has never been revealed – until now.


A new investigation by the Bureau for Investigative Journalism (TBIJ) in collaboration with Novara Media has identified a series of links between music producer Denver Bamber and the Node Project. Theo Blackledge, a 3D artist and animator from Liverpool, is another founder of the previously anonymous collective.


Bamber is an established music producer and director of a company. He has built his career off working with predominantly black British grime and rap artists. Expense returns for defunct far-right party Advance UK’s Gorton and Denton byelection candidate, Nick Buckley, show the party paid Bamber’s company to produce videos. A previous version of the Node Project’s online shop privacy policy contained the same address as Bamber’s company.


Bamber confirmed that he and Blackledge founded the Node Project and created Danny Bones.


Blackledge separately confirmed his role with the Node Project, although he is not known to be affiliated with Bamber’s company. Bamber said Blackledge is still involved in the project. “Theo and I founded it and are the co-creative directors, working collaboratively across the project with the wider team,” he said.


Asked about their identities and connection to the project, Bamber said that he and the Blackledge “are the founders of the project and the creators behind Danny Bones. We’ve never hidden behind Danny because we’re worried about backlash or because we think we’re doing anything wrong. It’s because this is an art project and Danny is the face of it.”


Bamber described the pair as “two working-class lads exploring ideas that a lot of British people feel and relate to”.


Building the brand.


Bamber is a music producer, audio engineer and songwriter from Greater Manchester who has worked with some of the biggest names in British hip-hop, grime and drill, including chart-topping Manchester rapper Aitch. He boasts industry credits including Warner Music, UMG, NQ Records, Plug Records and GRM Daily. His songs were streamed 120 million times in 2025.


He predominantly works with black British artists including Manchester rapper Kenzo Str8Drop, Liverpool’s Kasst8 and drill artist Tee Zandos from east London. Some of these artists rap explicitly about racism, police harassment and deprivation.


Blackledge has also worked in the UK rap and grime scene. His 3D animation social media accounts have hundreds of thousands of followers. He has previously edited music videos for grime artists including Aystar and Manga Saint Hilare. His recent content includes stylised animations of real musicians and characters from films and video games. In 2019 Bamber and Blackledge worked together on a music video for rapper Gully Pactzz (now Gul Payne).


Bamber also gives artists the chance to learn from him. A

promotional video

 on Bamber’s TikTok account advertises brand development services for “serious artists only”. For £500, as well as recording music, he helps artists with “branding and identity consultation”.


Danny Bones. Image: The Node Project


Bamber appears to have applied these skills to the creation of Danny Bones, whose slick videos convey clear branding and a consistent identity: an angry young man railing against the decline of the UK, which he blames on immigration.


Since first appearing in late 2025, Danny Bones has built an audience for his far-right political message, with more than half a million Spotify streams and 4.5 million YouTube views.
