title: Citizens at memorial ceremony for guerrillas: No more bloodshed, we want peace
content:
A memorial gathering was set up at Koşuyolu Park in Amed’s Rezan (Bağlar) district for HPG and YJA Star guerrillas who were killed in the freedom struggle at different times and in different regions. Organized under the leadership of the Association for Assistance, Solidarity, Unity and Culture with Families Who Have Lost Relatives in the Cradle of Civilizations (MEBYA-DER), the gathering was attended by the families of the fallen guerrillas, representatives of political parties and civil society organizations, and numerous citizens.


Speaking to ANF during their visit to the condolence gathering, citizens said that wars and conflicts must end and that lasting and egalitarian peace must be established. They called for the process to be advanced in line with the demands of society and for the fundamental rights of the Kurdish people to be guaranteed.


 


Everyone should support this process


Sadık Tosun said that everyone should embrace the peace and democratic society process. Pointing out that very heavy sacrifices had been made in previous years, Tosun said that all sections of society needed to take responsibility for the process to genuinely move forward.


Tosun added that existing legal regulations were inadequate: “First and foremost, the leader of the Kurdish people should have been in direct communication during this process. On the other hand, a law to be enacted for the Kurds should have included provisions concerning language and education. If we say that this is brotherhood, then we must be equal and we must all have the same rights. The demands of the Kurdish people are not merely the demands of one people; they are demands for equality and humanity. The right of Kurds to receive education in their own language, culture and history needs to be guaranteed.”


We no longer want memorial gatherings


Maşallah Yıldeniz said their most fundamental demand was peace and that they no longer wanted new condolence gatherings to be held. “Our demand is peace. We want peace. We want our leader to be free and to come among us. We no longer want anyone to become a martyr. We have just come from the condolence gathering for 50 martyrs; we no longer want condolence gatherings. Neither guerrillas nor soldiers should be killed or become martyrs in these valleys. Let everyone experience peace and comfort; let everyone experience peace,” she said.


Mothers have called for peace for years


Emine Özbek, who said she had been active in the Mothers of Peace movement for many years, stated, “As mothers, we want peace; we want democracy. Mothers have been struggling for years. One gave her son and said ‘peace’; another gave her daughter and said ‘peace.’ No mother wanted war; every mother wanted peace. A beginning has been made, but this is not enough. It needs to be expanded. Let’s not deceive ourselves; let’s not say, ‘peace has arrived.’ We need to be strong. Our political will must be strong, and we must always stand firm.”


We want no bloodshed


Berivan Mızrak, who attended the condolence gathering, also emphasized that their only demand was peace, saying, “We want this to happen. We want peace to happen. We want no blood to be shed. What do we want? We want peace. We do not want bloodshed.”

title: Artists in Diyarbakır launch campaign against policies targeting young people
content:
Drugs, prostitution and policies of social degeneration, regarded as key instruments of special warfare policies targeting the social fabric, have prompted artists in Diyarbakır (Amed) to take action.


The artists stressed that art is part of social resistance and the struggle for truth and came together to build a common line of struggle against these policies targeting young people. They announced that they would carry out comprehensive work in the field of culture and art.


Artist Elvan Koçer spoke to ANF about the work to be carried out against drugs and prostitution and the role of art in social struggle.


Special warfare policies target social bonds


Elvan Koçer said that special warfare policies are among the methods most frequently used by dominant powers in social struggles and that their main aim is to weaken the bonds that enable society to sustain itself.


Koçer said that throughout the history of Kurdistan, attempts had been made to achieve various outcomes through wars and massacres, but that despite all these attacks, the people had not abandoned their lands. She said special warfare policies particularly target women and young people:


“By primarily targeting women and young people, they seek to sever the lifelines that enable society to survive and sustain itself, such as social struggle, cultural transmission and social continuity. By detaching individuals from society, they also seek to poison society through its own members. Looking at the history of Kurdistan, even though wars and massacres may have produced partial results, it is not possible to speak of annihilation or a definitive victory for the dominant powers.


The people who have lived on these lands for thousands of years have experienced every dimension of war over the past century. Despite immense destruction and massacres, they have not abandoned their lands.”


Social decay is being imposed


Koçer said that today the social structure is being targeted through different methods:


“At the point we have reached, our society is being faced with the prospect of the grave, becoming refugees or, if people remain, decay and destruction. Therefore, one of the consequences of a practice of war devoid of ethical and moral principles is drugs, and another is prostitution. In this way, our young people are being disconnected from society, and attempts are being made to create individuals who are powerless, ashamed of themselves and seeking to escape from themselves.


First, they seek to detach our young people from their social bonds, but it does not stop there. This rupture also leads to alienation from oneself and from life. At the same time, it is an attempt to erode the social structure and, through different agendas and problems, make both the individual and society unhealthy.”


Art is a ground for resistance


Koçer said that art is one of the fundamental fields through which society’s historical and cultural heritage is carried into the future:


“The most fundamental characteristic of art and culture is that they are deeply rooted and powerful means of transmission. Art brings together the cultural, historical and sociological legacy of thousands of years with aesthetics and turns it into a marker for society. Its role represents a ground for resistance that goes beyond the industrial sphere. At least, this is the case for societies like ours that are engaged in social struggle.


The role of art is to bring together what is right, what is social and the future with the past, deepening and strengthening society’s roots. By understanding it in this way and trying to put it into practice, we seek to fulfil our social responsibilities. As Kurdish artists, this is how we define the task we have set ourselves.”


Kurds have a strong collective memory


Koçer said that the collective memory of the Kurdish people remains strong:


“The collective memory of the Kurdish people and Kurdish artists is still very strong. Therefore, they can very quickly see how every piece of work they carry out in their own field resonates within the social structure. The most important basis for this is that the practical life of Kurds is largely social and collective.


We are not a society made up of artists and individuals who have been isolated by capitalist modernity, who merely consume and live individualistically. We are a collective society, with our artists, workers and labourers, women and young people. This is the most fundamental …

title: Majid Maleki Meighani: Social power in the Middle East must be democratized - Part Two
content:
Majid Maleki Meighani is an Iranian writer, political analyst, translator, and photographer whose work explores the relationship between capitalism, imperialism, class, and political power. 


The first part of this interview can be read

here

. 


The Islamic Republic of Iran was established as the outcome of an Islamic revolution. If it was a revolution, what have the ongoing protests in Iran been directed against, and what is the current situation in the country?


I think we first have to distinguish between revolution as a social process and the political system that emerged from it. The 1979 revolution was genuinely a revolution because it fundamentally transformed the existing political structure and altered the balance of social and political forces in Iran. But revolution does not necessarily mean social emancipation.


A revolution can bring contradictory forces into the political arena, and its ultimate outcome depends on the balance of forces, organizational capacity, and the ability of different political currents to build new institutions. The Islamic Republic incorporated some of the genuine demands of the revolution -independence, social justice, the end of the monarchy, and mass political mobilization- into a new political order. At the same time, however, it restricted and suppressed many of the revolution’s democratic and pluralistic possibilities.


For this reason, subsequent protests in Iran cannot simply be described as protests against Islam or against the revolution itself. They are directed against a specific structure of power: the concentration of political authority, repression, gender discrimination, corruption, economic crisis, declining living standards, social restrictions, and the absence of meaningful participation in political decision-making.


But there is an important qualification. Iranian society should not itself be treated as a unified political actor. Different classes and generations have different interests and demands.


As I argued in my recent article on the crisis of political representation, we cannot interpret every demonstration, every vote, or every protest as the unified position of the “Iranian nation.” Iranian society is a contradictory social totality in which different forces compete with one another.[3]


External pressure and war further complicate these contradictions. War can deepen dissatisfaction with the government, but under conditions of external threat it can also unite sections of society around the idea of national defense.


We therefore cannot assume that military pressure from abroad will automatically produce democracy. In my view, Iran’s future depends not only on the behavior of the state, but also on society’s ability to create independent organizations and connect the demands of women, workers, young people, ethnic communities, and other social groups within a democratic and socially grounded project.


Proxy wars have long been a central strategy for Iran and Turkey in the Middle East. Have the war waged by Israel and the United States against Iran and the developments surrounding it changed these conditions?


Yes, to a considerable extent. One of the most important changes is the erosion of the boundary between proxy warfare and direct war. For years, regional powers attempted to manage their rivalries through armed non-state actors, allied governments, and regional networks. But once Iran and Israel became directly involved in military confrontation, and the United States entered the war, the rules of the game changed.


This does not mean that proxy wars have disappeared. On the contrary, they may become more important in some areas. But regional actors now know that any proxy conflict can rapidly escalate into direct confrontation between states.


For Turkey, this development is particularly significant. Ankara does not want the region to become the arena for a direct war among Iran, Israel, and the United States, because such a war could directly affect Turkey’s security, trade, energy supplies, and the Kurdish question.


Under these circumstances, Turkey is attempting to present itself not as a subordinate actor but as an independent regional power and potential mediator. This is part of the same semi-peripheral power strategy I have analyzed elsewhere: Turkey seeks to exploit the crisis of U.S. hegemony to expand its autonomy and regional influence without being able to fully detach itself from the economic and security …

title: Strategic personality, power of construction, and meaning of law - An analysis by Ergin Atabey
content:
Ergin Atabey is being held on Imralı Island with Abdullah Öcalan and is a member of the Imralı Secretariat. He wrote an article titled “Strategic personality, the power of construction, and the meaning of law” for Özgür Halk Magazine.


The article reads as follows:


“When we look at the discussions being held about the process in general, unfortunately, it is mostly discussed through its technical and what could be called secondary aspects. Although the psychological warfare of the special war regime is influential in this, its most important dimensions cannot be explained by that alone. Especially those of us who have the responsibility of building a democratic communal society are unable, because of the superficiality we experience, to move beyond secondary and technical aspects and think at a strategic level. For this reason, our discussions and work lack substance, and we cannot get to the main agenda. As a result, even when what we say is justified, we remain within the boundaries of psychological warfare. Consequently, we remain removed from the main agenda, discussions, and issues.


Leader Öcalan says, ‘I work strategically.’ The foundation on which strategic work rests is a strategic personality. One of its most important characteristics is determining the agenda, discussion, and work according to what is essential and fundamental. The most advanced psychological warfare in history is being waged against Leader Öcalan. This psychological warfare is being conducted particularly in an attempt to shape, according to their own designs, his agenda, discussions, and work. Yet despite being under a degree of encirclement unparalleled in history or today, no one has been able to direct Leader Öcalan’s agenda, discussions, or work. The secret lies in the strategic personality that Leader Öcalan has built within himself. However, the fundamental disadvantage Leader Öcalan faces is our failure to build the same level of strategic personality within ourselves. For this reason, we cannot fully understand what is happening. We cannot see the traps set by the special war regime through its promotion of secondary and technical issues as the agenda. In general, we fall into this trap. This distances us from the essence of the matter. The result is that this returns as a negative consequence for Leader Öcalan. Objectively, we are unable to advance the strategy he has developed. This is the disadvantage being referred to.


Reaching the level of strategic personality


In general, the encirclement imposed on Leader Öcalan is regarded as a disadvantage. Undoubtedly, the situation would have been different had this encirclement not existed. Yet when we look from the past to the present, the essential issue ultimately comes down to us. In the past, too, we failed to fulfill the requirements of the strategic periods that Leader Öcalan developed through his initiatives. Many strategic initiatives, occurring on average once every decade, were largely rendered ineffective because we failed to reach the level of strategic personality. This is the reality we face today as well. Our failure to reach the level of strategic personality is the most fundamental disadvantage from Leader Öcalan’s perspective.


In explaining his strategic outlook, Leader Öcalan defines it as: ‘Breaking the grip of genocide and war in which the Kurds are held, preventing genocide, and building their sphere as a free existence.’ Half a century of strategic direction, resistance, and work is expressed in its most striking form in this sentence. It is also a reality that expresses the meaning of the process we are currently experiencing. The grip of genocide over the Kurds continues. Although Kurds have been accepted in practice, they are still not a free existence. The latest strategic initiative is intended to enable the Kurds to overcome this position. Let us review what we have done since the day this initiative was launched. What we have done is reflected most clearly in our discourse. The period in which our discourse has been most intense has been the past one to one-and-a-half months. In this sense, what we have said around the phenomenon called ‘law’ shows where we stand in relation to strategic initiative.


We have practically risen with ‘law’ on our lips and gone to bed with ‘law’ on our lips. It would not be unfair to say that these expressions of ‘rising’ and ‘going to bed’ with law represent our stance toward this strategic initiative. In fact …

title: Repression of women in Iran continues
content:
The US-based Human Rights Activists News Agency (HRANA) issued a statement regarding Iran’s repression of women activists in Rojhilatê Kurdistan and Iran.


It was reported that 34-year-old Nazenin Hüseyinpur, a mother of two from Piranshahr district in Urmia, was detained by the city’s Intelligence Department and that her whereabouts are unknown.


It was stated that Nazenin Hüseyinpur was detained after being summoned to the Intelligence Department on August 16, but despite persistent inquiries by her family, no information was provided about the reason for her detention or her whereabouts. It was also reported that Nazenin Hüseyinpur has not been allowed access to a lawyer or family visits.


According to published reports, young Kurdish woman Zehra Rabbanî (18), who was 17 at the time of her detention, was sentenced by the Bojnurd Criminal Court to a total of 15 months and 2 days in prison and a fine of 6 million tomans. Zehra Rabbanî will serve 7 months and 16 days of this sentence in prison.


Zehra Rabbanî, who was detained for participating in protests, was charged with “assembly and collusion with the intention of committing crimes against the country’s internal security” and “producing, transporting, and distributing explosive materials.”


Zehra Rabbanî was summoned to a police station for questioning on January 4 and was made to sign a document stating that she would not participate in protests. However, she was detained the following day. Rabbanî was released after spending 45 days in detention.

title: ABD ve Kanada ticarette anlaşamadı: 20 milyar dolarlık ürüne yüzde 50 tarife
content:
ABD ile Kanada arasında haftalardır devam eden ticaret geriliminde yeni bir aşamaya geçildi. İki ülke arasında üç günlük ek sürede yürütülen görüşmelerden anlaşma çıkmayınca ABD'nin yaklaşık 20 milyar dolarlık Kanada ürününe getirdiği yüzde 50 ek gümrük tarifesi yürürlüğe girdi.

Tarifelerin ilk olarak 19 Ağustos'ta uygulanması planlanmış, ancak Trump yönetimi görüşmelerde ilerleme sağlandığı gerekçesiyle uygulamayı üç gün ertelemişti. ABD Başkanı Donald Trump da bu süreçte tarafların anlaşmaya vardığını açıklamıştı. Ancak son görüşmelerde nihai koşullar üzerinde uzlaşma sağlanamadı.

Kanada Başbakanı Mark Carney, görüşmelerde ilerleme sağlandığını ancak ortaya çıkan şartların Kanada'nın hedeflerini karşılamadığını belirterek müzakere heyetini Ottawa'ya geri çağırdı. ABD Ticaret Temsilcisi Jamieson Greer ise Kanada'nın hafta içinde üzerinde uzlaşıldığını söylediği şartlarla anlaşmayı sonuçlandırmayı kabul etmediğini savundu.

Yeni tarifeler, Kanada'nın ABD'ye yıllık ihracatının yaklaşık yüzde 5'ini kapsıyor. Süt ve bazı süt ürünleri, şarap ve diğer içecekler, hokey ekipmanları, çimento ve çeşitli tüketim ürünleri yeni tarifeden etkilenecek. ABD-Meksika-Kanada Anlaşması'nın menşe kurallarına uygun bazı ürünler de yüzde 50'lik ek tarifeden muaf tutulmayacak.

Enerji ürünleri, potas, kritik mineraller ve başka tarife düzenlemelerine tabi bazı ürünler ise uygulamanın dışında bırakıldı.

Washington, tarifelerin gerekçesi olarak Kanada'nın Amerikan süt ürünlerine yönelik kota sistemini, bazı eyaletlerde ABD menşeli alkollü içeceklere yönelik kısıtlamaları ve otomotiv ticaretindeki uygulamaları gösteriyor.

Kanada Başbakanı Carney, ABD'nin yeni tarifelerine aynı parasal büyüklükte karşılık vereceklerini açıkladı. Ottawa'nın hangi ABD ürünlerini hedef alacağı ve karşı tarifelerin ne zaman yürürlüğe gireceğine ilişkin ayrıntıların ise henüz açıklanmadığı belirtildi.

İki ülke geçen yıl yaklaşık 880 milyar dolarlık mal ve hizmet ticareti gerçekleştirdi. Yeni tarifelerin doğrudan kapsadığı ticaret hacmi toplam ticaretin sınırlı bir bölümünü oluştursa da karşılıklı misillemelerin ekonomik etkisinin büyümesi riski bulunuyor.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Ricardo Sangiovanni
title: Resistindo à IA
content:
E, de repente, eu me dei conta de que era o único da rodinha de amigos que nunca tinha usado nenhuma inteligência artificial.


Claro que, hoje em dia, ao dar um Google, mandar um zap, fazer uma compra – encher, enfim, o peito de ar –, estamos indiretamente usando ou alimentando alguma IA. Mas o uso deliberado de alguma suíte de IA, isso eu juro que ainda não fiz.


Também não estou aqui a dizer que nunca farei, pois pretendo continuar a integrar a população economicamente ativa por uns anos, ainda que de forma compulsória. Queria só mesmo legar à posteridade este depoimento avulso, para o caso de as futuras gerações quererem saber como se sentia alguém na soleira deste grande ponto de inflexão da história da espécie. (E também registrar que, muito antes do ChatGPT, eu já escrevia

usando travessões

).


Vejo pessoas ao meu redor entusiasmadas com a proliferação das IAs e penso que tamanha animação só pode ocultar alguma forma irrefletida de desespero. Estão rindo? Pois eu não estou achando graça nenhuma: eu sinto é medo.


É que, tendo, desde sempre, ganho a vida por meio da escrita conjugada a alguma capacidade de raciocínio, não posso deixar de olhar para a IA com a desconfiança com que a lavadeira à beira do rio olhou um dia para a máquina de lavar roupas. Como pode, do dia para a noite, uma geringonça qualquer ser capaz de fazer — mais, melhor, mais rápido — a única coisa que eu estudei anos e anos para fazer razoavelmente bem na vida?


Além de assustado, sinto-me só. Olho para o lado e uma amiga me revela, sussurrando: “não leva a mal”, que já prefere pagar uma suíte de IA a contratar um estagiário. Olho para o outro e uma colega me conta que conversa diariamente com sua IA personalizada, a quem explica suas angústias e desafios, obtendo dela conselhos e soluções.


Como fazer vista grossa à perversidade de uma tecnologia que substitui pessoas não apenas em funções maquínicas, mas principalmente em atividades sofisticadas? Como aceitar passivamente que o último e mais pacífico recurso de luta pela sobrevivência e ascensão social das classes trabalhadoras — a inteligência, cultivada por toda uma vida de economias investidas em educação — nos seja simplesmente surrupiado?


Sinto-me como meu avô — bancário aposentado, que tinha prazer em perambular de agência em agência, em filas, para pagar boletos — diante do internet banking.


Sinto-me como Seu Valter — ex-montador de fitas de vídeo em uma emissora de TV, que conheci como vendedor de água de coco em frente à Reitoria da UFBA — diante do advento da transmissão via satélite.


Sinto-me como o linotipista diante da impressão

offset

; como o copista diante da imprensa de Gutenberg; quiçá, regresso

ad infinitum

, como um pré-histórico carregador de pedras diante da invenção da roda.


Irmanado à angústia de cada ser humano que viu seu valor social subitamente ameaçado por uma tecnologia nova, busco ânimo para encarar a

IA

, refugiando-me na ideia divertida de que as máquinas jamais nos alcançarão em nossa capacidade de errar.


Porque é justamente por serem feitas para encarnar o fetiche da perfeição que as máquinas não são aptas ao erro. Experimente jogar xadrez contra uma delas: nos níveis mais elementares, comete falhas que, de tão bisonhas, chegam a ser inverossímeis; nos mais altos, acerta tanto que nos irrita, levando-nos ao desestímulo. Só o ser humano é capaz de errar do jeito certo: por cansaço, covardia ou ambição, mas sempre desejando acertar. Errando, manifestamos a imperfeição que nos torna humanos — e só a seres imperfeitos como nós é dada a maravilhosa possibilidade de sonhar.


No dia enfim em que as máquinas souberem fazer tudo; em que não for mais preciso um ser humano sequer para nada; talvez o último de nós sobre a face da terra compreenda, sozinho e inutilmente iluminado, que talvez devêssemos ter dado mais atenção aos nossos medos, aos nossos erros, aos nossos sonhos. Até lá, resistamos.

author: Unknown
title: Baluken: Öcalan’s conditions are a strategic issue for solution
content:
A new phase has begun with the passage of legislation in parliament as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process initiated by Abdullah Öcalan. Despite its many shortcomings, the law has been regarded by the parties concerned as a positive step because it is the first of its kind.


The passage of the legislation, widely known as the Framework Law, has now shifted attention to the steps the government will take to implement it. Once the law enters into force, many Kurdish politicians and patriots currently imprisoned or living in exile are expected to benefit from its provisions.


Kurdish politician Idris Baluken, who is living in exile, spoke to ANF about the Framework Law and the next stage of the process.


Historical experience provided important lessons to both the state and the Kurdish movement


Baluken said the current stage had not been reached within just a few years and recalled that the Kurdish people had paid a heavy price over the past four decades: “It would be incomplete to view this process solely through the developments of the past few months or years. The point reached today is in fact the result of the historical experience accumulated through the Kurdish people’s struggle for rights, identity and equal citizenship spanning more than a century, and particularly the determined resistance sustained at great cost over the past forty years.


Despite severe repression, including denial, assimilation, forced displacement, unsolved killings, mass arrests and military operations, the Kurdish people have preserved their political will and have not abandoned their demand for a democratic solution. This unbroken social and political will is one of the most important factors shaping the stage reached today.


Since the 1990s, there have also been direct and indirect attempts at negotiations at various times. Each time, however, the collapse of the negotiating table or the termination of the process for political reasons only deepened the deadlock. Society endured greater suffering and paid an even heavier economic and human cost.


This historical experience has produced important lessons for both the state and the Kurdish movement. It has become clear that security-based policies have failed to resolve the issue, while negotiation efforts conducted without a legal framework have likewise failed to produce lasting results. The Framework Law adopted today can therefore be regarded as a first step towards establishing a legal basis for negotiations.


The Framework Law should not be viewed as a favour granted by the state, but as an outcome of the Kurdish people’s struggle spanning more than a century. It must be stressed once again that this law is not a final solution. It marks the beginning of a new phase aimed at resolving a century-old issue through democratic means.”


Mr. Öcalan’s working conditions are a strategic issue


Baluken stressed that the legal status of the parties to the negotiations must be clearly defined in the next stage and said: “The next stage will gain meaning not simply through the law entering into force, but through the institutionalization of negotiations. First and foremost, the legal status of the parties to the negotiations must be clearly defined. One of the most significant shortcomings of previous processes was that negotiations largely depended on political will and were conducted without legal guarantees.


Mr. Öcalan’s conditions for negotiations and work are not a technical issue but a strategic one. In this context, restructuring Mr. Öcalan’s conditions for negotiations and work in line with international law and the principles of democratic politics is vital to the healthy progress of the process. It is also important to establish open channels of communication, form technical delegations and create mechanisms to oversee the process.


Complementary steps will also be necessary to make the climate of peace lasting. These include expanding the space for democratic politics, introducing reforms to strengthen freedom of expression and association, adopting measures to advance local democracy, reforming sentence enforcement legislation and the Anti-Terror Law, implementing the rulings of the Constitutional Court and the European Court of Human Rights, and establishing mechanisms for social reckoning and truth. The Framework Law essentially provides the legal foundation for opening the way to a democratic solution.”


Kurds in Europe are among the strongest …

author: Unknown
title: Open letter expressing solidarity for political prisoners in Iran
content:
Twenty-six Iranian academics, writers, and political and human rights activists declared their solidarity with political prisoners in Iran through an open letter.


Published under the title “End the Imperialist War and the Government’s Executions,” the letter stated that Iranian political prisoners are caught between two different forces of repression.


According to a report by Nujinha, the signatories, including figures such as Angela Davis, Judith Butler, Rashid Khalidi, Keeanga-Yamahtta Taylor, and Michael Löwy, said that the Iranian government uses detention, torture, and executions to suppress dissidents.


The letter stated that the Islamic Republic of Iran relies on prisons, torture, and executions to maintain political and social control.


The letter called on civil society organizations, activists, and anti-imperialist groups to increase their support for political prisoners in Iran. It also called for pressure to be placed on the Iranian government to immediately end all executions and release political prisoners.

author: Unknown
title: Annelerimizi gerçekten sevmek zorunda mıyız?
content:
“Sonunda öldürürüz annelerimizi çünkü artık yalan söylemek istemeyiz”*


Doğumlarına karar verilenler, doğumlarına karar verenlerle ilk gerçek yüzleşmelerini yaşamları boyunca sürdürürler. Bize ebeveynlik yapmış, ilk bakımımızı üstlenmiş kişilerle ilişkimiz; anlamaya, alışmaya ve bazen de onlardan ayrışmaya çalıştığımız uzun bir sarmal içinde kimliğimizi kurar. Bu ilk karşılaşmanın ve hesaplaşmanın önemli eşiklerinden biri erinlik dönemidir. Dünyaya getirilmelerine karar verilmiş çocuklar bir gün büyür ve “anneleriyle de hesaplaşır” (1).


Anneliğe dair temsiller, çocukluk boyunca sorulmamış soruların ve anlatılmamış hikâyelerin içinde gizlidir. Dünyaya henüz kendi başına tutunamayacak kadar hazırlıksız gelen çocuğun erken döneminde yaşanan krizlerin, sarsıntıların ve taşkınlıkların bir bölümü anneyle kurulan ilişkinin içinde anlam kazanır. Bu nedenle çocukluk, annelik mitosunun daha gerçekçi bir biçimde ele alınabilmesi açısından önemli bir alandır.


Annelik, yüzyıllardır kutsanan üreme işlevinin ardından yerleşmiş, zaman içinde bunun çok ötesine taşınmış büyük bir rolün üzerinde varlığını sürdürür. Kadınlık deneyiminin içine yerleşen annelik anlatısı, birçok kadın için beklenmedik, sarsıcı ve kendi varlığını bölen bir deneyime dönüşebilir. Anne olurken kadın, henüz kendi olma hikâyesini tamamlamamışken yeni bir pozisyonun içine yerleşir. Bu nedenle anneliğin tarihi biraz da pozisyon alma, o pozisyonları benimseme ve gerektiğinde onlardan sıyrılma tarihidir.


Çocukla kurulan yoğun bedensel ve duygusal bağ, anne ile çocuğun birbirlerinin sahnesinde kendilerini görmelerine neden olur. Çocuk anneye bakarken, anne de çocuğun bakışında hem kendisini hem kendi çocukluğunu görebilir. Biyolojik bağın ve toplumsal anlamların birbirine eklenmesiyle ayrışma, yalnızca psikolojik bir tema olmaktan çıkar; çocuk açısından zamanla sahiplenilmesi gereken bir hakka dönüşür.


Peki bütün bu iç içeliğin ve kutsanan ilişkinin içinde çocuk, anneyi sevmeme hakkını taşıyarak büyürse ne olur? Onunla ilişkilenemediğini kabul eder ve bu ilişkisizliğe sahip çıkarsa? Ya da annenin çocuğa yönelttiği talepler, beklentiler ve müdahaleler çocuğun kendi mevcudiyetini kapattığında, çocuk annesinden uzaklaşmayı istediğinde ne olur?


Margit Schreiner’in

Sevmek Dedikleri

 kitabı tam da böylesi bir bağ kuramamanın ve ilişkilenmeme hakkının sahiplenildiği, sevginin anlamının dahi sorgulandığı bir anlatı kuruyor. Bir kız çocuğunun, seksen üç yaşındaki annesini bakım evine yatırdıktan sonra onun son günlerinde yaşadığı içsel hesaplaşmayı konu edinen kitap, “Ölüm” öyküsüyle başlıyor; annesinden sevgi almayı beklediği “Düğün” hayaliyle devam ediyor ve kendi annelik deneyimiyle yüzleştiği “Doğum” öyküsüyle çocukluğuna yeniden bakıyor.


Birbirine bağlanan üç öykü boyunca yetişkin kız çocuğu, annelik ve çocukluk deneyimini yeniden düşünürken, anneliğe dair klasik kodların dışına çıkıyor. Anlatı, tam da bu nedenle, sevgi ile yükümlülük arasındaki sınırları ve bir çocuğun annesiyle ilişkilenmeme hakkını tartışmaya açıyor.


Çocuğun iktidar karşısındaki sarsıcı durağı olarak “Anne”


Geleneksel psikoloji ve psikanaliz kuramlarının önemli bir bölümünde anne, çocuğun erken gelişiminde merkezi bir figür olarak ele alınır. Bu merkezi konum farklı kuramlarda farklı biçimlerde açıklansa da, anneyle kurulan ilişkinin çocuğun ruhsal gelişimi açısından belirleyici olduğu düşüncesi güçlü bir yere sahiptir.


Psikanalitik düşüncenin önemli bir bölümü de dünyaya henüz kendi başına varlığını sürdüremeyecek kadar hazırlıksız gelen çocuğun ilk bakım ilişkileri, bedensel temasları ve ötekiyle kurduğu erken bağlar üzerinden şekillenir. Anne burada yalnızca biyolojik bir figür değil, çocuğun dünyayla kurduğu ilişkinin önemli taşıyıcılarından biridir.


Ancak bu merkezi konumun başka bir sonucu da vardır: Anneyle ilişkinin kendisi çoğu zaman sorgulanması güç bir alan haline gelebilir. Özellikle anneliğin toplumsal olarak kutsanmasıyla birlikte, annenin yokluğu, yetersizliği, zarar vericiliği ya da çocuk tarafından reddedilmesi konuşulması zor meseleler olarak kalabilir.


Bağlanma kuramları açısından da erken bakım ilişkileri çocuğun gelişimi bakımından temel bir öneme sahiptir. Bununla birlikte bağlanma literatürü bakım veren kişiyi zorunlu olarak anneyle sınırlandırmaz; çocuğun birincil ya da sürekli bakımını üstlenen farklı kişilerle kurduğu ilişkiler de bu çerçevede ele alınabilir. Dolayısıyla mesele yalnızca “anne” ile çocuk arasındaki bağdan değil, çocuğun bakım …

title: 23 août 1996 – 23 août 2026 : 30 ans de luttes des Sans-Papiers !
content:
Ensemble, pour l'égalité des droits de toutes et tous, contre le racisme et le fascisme, reprenons le chemin de Saint-Bernard

 

! Manifestation samedi 22 août 2026, 15 heures Place de la République à Paris


Il y a 30 ans, le 23 août 1996, plus de 300 familles, avec de nombreux enfants, réfugiées dans l'église Saint-Bernard à Paris sont violemment expulsées par les forces de l'ordre. Le bâtiment est pris d'assaut et les portes sont fracassées à coups de hache. Les occupants sont aspergés de gaz lacrymogènes avant d'être jetés à la rue ou mis en centre de rétention. Ces images qui ont fait le tour du monde illustraient le slogan que scandent les Sans-papiers dans leurs manifestations : «

 

Nous ne sommes pas dangereux, nous sommes en danger

 

».


Le 23 août 1996, d'autres images firent également le tour du monde : celles de la solidarité concrète. Avertis par les réseaux militants de l'imminence de l'intervention de la police à l'église Saint Bernard, des milliers de citoyennes et de citoyens s'y étaient rendus et se donnaient la main pour dresser une barrière humaine devant l'église. Ils et elles furent frappé·es et piétiné·es par les policiers au moment de l'assaut mais leur exemple marquera toute une génération de militants. Des dizaines de milliers de manifestant·es défilent alors dans la plupart des grandes villes de France pour exiger la régularisation des Sans-papiers. Dans les mois suivants, plus de 75% des occupant·es de Saint-Bernard sont régularisé·es, les autres le seront un an plus tard sous le gouvernement Jospin qui succède à celui de Juppé qui a ordonné les coups de hache.


Saint Bernard eut un autre résultat : l'organisation du mouvement des sans-papiers. Dans les mois qui suivirent l'évacuation brutale de l'Église des collectifs se mettent en place dans de nombreuses villes avant de se fédérer plus tard en une coordination nationale des Sans-papiers. Puis fut créée l'Unsp et ensuite la Marche des solidarités. Plus récemment, les collectifs de sans-papiers d'Île-de-France se sont regroupés au sein de l'Intercollectif des Sans-Papiers. Aux côtés de celui-ci et de la

CSP59

, de nouveaux collectifs se créent. Des collectifs de jeunes mineurs isolés se sont créés un peu partout en France à l'initiative du collectif des jeunes de Belleville. La Marche des Solidarités vise à fédérer toutes les personnes, partis politiques, associations, collectifs et syndicats, qui souhaitent lutter contre le racisme et les discriminations quelles qu'elles soient et contre l'extrème-droite et le fascisme.


Il y a 30 ans la dynamique autour des Sans-Papiers se traduisit aussi par une mobilisation pour rejeter une loi raciste, la loi Debré tandis que 50 000 manifestant·es défilaient en mars 1997 contre le congrès du

FN

 à Strasbourg.


Alors que se profilent les élections présidentielles, nous appelons à reprendre le chemin de St Bernard pour exiger l'égalité des droits, la régularisation de tous les Sans-Papiers, la fin des politiques racistes et pour barrer la route au

RN

.


Seule l'union de toutes les forces permettra le rapport de force nécessaire pour que la lutte paie

 

!


Manifestation samedi 22 août 2026


15 heures Place de la République à Paris


A l'initiative des collectifs de sans-papiers et mineur.e.s isolé.e.s en lutte : Association Droits devant

 

!!,

CISPM

 (Coalition Internationale des sans-papiers et Migrants), Collectif des Jeunes du Parc de Belleville, Collectif des Travailleurs Sans Papiers de Vitry,

CSP59

,

CSP75

, Intercollectif des sans-papiers d'Île-de-France


De la plateforme de la Marche des Solidarités.


Et plus de 130 collectifs, syndicats, associations, partis.

title: Ephéméride des luttes : 22 août
content:
Aujourd'hui 22 août, l'éphéméride des luttes rentre de vacances. Mais ce n'est pas pour ça qu'elle s'est arrêtée entre temps. On maintient un esprit de lutte, d'antifascisme et de solidarité par delà les saisons.


1831 :

 A Southampton County en Virginie, juste après minuit, c'est le début de la rébellion des esclaves menée par Nat Turner, l'une des premières grandes rébellions d'esclaves aux Etats-Unis.


1917 :

 A Turin, une grande émeute du pain a lieu : "

lors d'une manifestation de protestation contre la guerre et ses conséquences (le manque de vivres), une foule composée en majorité de femmes s'attaque à des magazins. La police intervient en tirant sur les manifestant(e)s, ce qui provoque des morts et des blessés. Dès le lendemain, la grève est générale à Turin, la première barricade est élevée tandis que la police occupe la Bourse du travail. Le 24 août, l'état de siège est proclamé, mais les affrontements se poursuivront jusqu'au 26 août. Une église sera investie par la foule et la grande quantité de vivres qui se trouvait entreposée dans le couvent sera distribuée aux nécessiteux. Les anarchistes ont pris une part active à ces d'émeutes et notamment le compagnon Anselmo Acutis. Ces événements "fatti di Torino" se caractérisent par une féroce répression policière qui causera la mort de centaines de personnes.

"


Repris de

l'éphéméride anarchiste

.


1936 :

 A Barcelone, sortie du premie numéro du journal

L'Espagne Antifasciste

.


1968 :

 A Prague, invasion des chars russes pour écraser un soulèvement populaire, passé à la postérité comme 'Le Printemps de Prague', soulèvement contre le pouvoir staliniste qui connu une brutale répression.


1972 :

 - En Floride, 891 personnes sont arrêtées alors qu'elles participent à une manifestation de contestation du congrès du Parti Républicain.


 En Argentine, des membres de l'armée assassinent seize militants d'organisations armées de gauche alors incarcérés dans une prison militaire à Trelew.


1978 :

 A Managua au Nicaragua, des guérilleros du Front Sandiniste s'emparent du Palais National lors d'une session du Congrès.


1992 :

 En Irlande du Nord, la barre des 3.000 mort-e-s est atteinte au sein des conflits qui agitent la région depuis plus de 23 ans.


2003 :

 A West Covina en Californie, l'ELF (Front de Libération de la Terre) attaque plusieurs concessionnaires auto, brûlant des dépôts et vandalisant plus de 125 SUV et Hummer, faisant plus de 2.3 millions de dollars de dégâts.


2011 :

 - A Nantes, la caravane du Parti Socialiste est saccagée par des opposant-e-s à l'aéroport de Notre-Dame-des-Landes.


2012 :

 A Athènes, dans le quartier de Peristeri, la camionnette d'une entreprise appartenant au député néonazi d'Aube Dorée de Corinthe est incendiée par les anarchistes.


2017 :

 A Orbeil dans le Puy-de-Dôme, une antenne relais est incendiée. Lire le communiqué du B.A.R.J.O. (Barbecue d'Antennes Relais Joliment Osé) sur

Indymédia Nantes

.


Voir

l'éphéméride anarchiste

 du 22 août.

La Biblioteca Popular

Del Otro Lado del Árbol,

un espacio que Paula Kriscautzy y amigos lograron sacar del abandono para promover la magia, la invención y la lectura durante 15 años, quedó en el centro del conflicto por las futuras reformas que la Municipalidad de La Plata proyectó para el Parque Saavedra. Hoy, patrulla de por medio, intentaron desalojarla poniendo en jaque la continuidad de este precciado espacio cultural para las infancias, uno de los más importantes de la ciudad La Plata. Mañana, sábado 22, a partir de las 11.00 la comunidad se autoconvocó para acompañar el mal trance y evaluar procedimientos. Desde el Municipio prometieron una reunión para el lunes próximo. Por

@fedebiott.ph

 (ANRed).


El 21 de agosto las autoridades municipales informaron que la biblioteca debe desalojar el espacio que ocupa desde 2011, en el marco del cierre de la locación y de las reformas que sufrirá el parque. Y para reforzar el pedido enviaron incluso a la patrulla municipal. Desde el Municipio también hicieron referencia a un episodio de suicidio ocurrido en el parque, como parte de los argumentos para intervenir el lugar.


El conflicto expone una situación jurídica que dejó al espacio en una posición vulnerable. Según explicó Paula Kriscautzky, fundadora de la biblioteca, el Municipio permitió desde 2011 su funcionamiento en un antiguo galpón del Parque Saavedra, pero nunca formalizó un comodato ni una tenencia que garantizara su continuidad.


Biblioteca Popular: Del otro lado del árbol. Foto: @agenciaxfoto; @martinlp8


La biblioteca nació como homenaje a Pilar, la hija de Kriscautzky. Y durante más de quince años se convirtió en un espacio de lectura, arte, juego y acompañamiento de las infancias con actividades junto a escuelas, familias, hospitales y organizaciones comunitarias.


No alcanza con que el Municipio asegure de palabra que la biblioteca seguirá funcionando: la comunidad reclama garantías concretas para su permanencia y el reconocimiento del trabajo comunitario que fue construyendo durante durante años.


Biblioteca Popular: Del otro lado del árbol. Foto: @agenciaxfoto; @martinlp8


El desalojo subraya lo que ocurre con los espacios culturales creados por la comunidad que, pese a haber funcionado a lo largo de los años con autorización estatal, como un refugio para la cultura y un servicio para la ciudad en su conjunto, siguen sin contar con una herramienta legal que garantice su continuidad.

author: Gladys Stagno
title: Suicidios: Argentina padece la crisis de salud mental más grande de su historia
content:
Un informe del Observatorio de Política Criminal muestra que en 2025 la tasa de suicidios rompió el techo histórico y posicionó a la Argentina en el tercer lugar de la región. “Se está muriendo gente y estamos haciendo caso omiso”, aseguró Ariel Larroude, su director.


Por Gladys Stagno


Desde 2017, el suicidio en la Argentina ha mostrado “un crecimiento vertiginoso”. La expresión es parte del informe del Observatorio de Política Criminal (OPC) que analizó los casos registrados por el Sistema Nacional de Información Criminal del Ministerio de Seguridad Nacional desde ese año hasta 2025.


El estudio –titulado 

Cuando matarse aparece como una opción en la Argentina

, que fue presentado esta mañana por el OPC junto a la Asamblea Permanente por los Derechos Humanos (APDH)– arroja un dato contundente: 2025 es el año con mayor tasa de suicidios del que se tenga registro en el país, 11,8 casos cada 100.000 habitantes. Y representa la principal causa de muerte en jóvenes adultos (15 a 34 años).


“Argentina padece la crisis de salud mental más grande de su historia. Ni siquiera en 2001, ni en los años 90, ni en la dictadura cívico-militar en el marco del genocidio llegamos a tener una tasa de suicidios tan elevada. Esto nos sumerge en una profunda reflexión porque son momentos críticos”, aseguró Ariel Larroude, analista criminal y director del OPC.


La tasa de suicidios superó a la de muertes por accidentes de tránsito y cuadriplica la de homicidios (11,8 versus 3,6), lo que el OPC llama “transmutación de la violencia letal”.


En algunas provincias es peor


A nivel territorial, la triste estadística la lideran Entre Ríos (20,8), San Luis (18,9), Salta (17,4), Santa Cruz (16,0) y Catamarca (14,2). Las más bajas correspondieron a Río Negro (6,5), Neuquén (7,8), CABA (8,0) y Corrientes (8,0).


“Las tasas permiten comparar poblaciones de distinto tamaño, pero deben leerse junto con los casos absolutos. En 2025, Buenos Aires concentró 1.977 hechos, equivalentes al 38,0% del total nacional. Le siguieron Santa Fe, con 461 casos; Córdoba, con 371; y Entre Ríos, con 288. En conjunto, estas cuatro jurisdicciones reunieron casi seis de cada diez casos del país”, detalla el informe.


En cuanto a la región, la tasa de 2025 dejó a la Argentina en el tercer lugar de Latinoamérica, únicamente por detrás de Uruguay y Chile.


Elaboración: Observatorio de Política Criminal (OPC).


Algunas causas


En este paso de la violencia interpersonal a la violencia hacia uno mismo, desde el OPC ahondaron en las causas posibles.


Desde APDH señalaron que “los discursos de odio han hecho que aumente 

el acoso escolar, el bullying, que afectan a los jóvenes”,

 junto con la ludopatía, que ha multiplicado el endeudamiento en esa franja etaria.


El titular del OPC, por su parte, apuntó también hacia el discurso del gobierno nacional, por el que “se ve al Estado como un enemigo”. “Probablemente, lo que estamos haciendo es decirles a los pibes que el Estado es una puerta menos a la cual acudir ante un problema”, detalló.


Y advirtió: “Si bien el suicidio es multicausal, también influyen la 

crisis de endeudamiento

 y la crisis de empleo, sumadas al recorte presupuestario”.


Sobre este último punto, hace hincapié el estudio.


El impacto del recorte


Si bien la Ley Nacional de Salud Mental (26.657) establece que el presupuesto destinado al área debía incrementarse progresivamente hasta alcanzar un mínimo del 10%, ese objetivo –de 2017 a 2015– nunca llegó a cumplirse. Sin embargo, hubo fluctuaciones que tienen mucho que ver con los resultados.


Así, de 2015 a 2019 se registraron “reducciones significativas en los recursos asignados al Programa Nacional de Salud Mental” y la ejecución presupuestaria resultó irregular, lo que limitó el desarrollo de programas, dispositivos comunitarios y acciones de promoción, prevención y asistencia.


Entre 2020 y 2023, en el contexto de la pandemia de COVID-19, “se observaron intentos por fortalecer las políticas públicas de salud mental”, aunque “diferentes organizaciones especializadas señalaron que los recursos continuaron siendo insuficientes para responder al aumento de las necesidades de la población”.


Pero a partir de 2024, en el marco de una política nacional de reducción del gasto público achicamiento del Estado, las partidas se redujeron drásticamente.


“Nunca en la historia del país hubo tan poco presupuesto en el área de salud mental como en el período 2025-2026. En el contexto de 

cierre de …

title: İsveç'te bir okula saldırı düzenlendi: 1 kişi öldü, 3 kişi yaralandı
content:
İsveç’in orta kesiminde bulunan Fagersta kentindebir okula saldırı düzenlendi. İsveç'te yayın yapan SVT kanalının haberine göre, Fagersta'da bulunan bir okula öğle saatlerinde kesici aletle giren saldırgan, birkaç kişiyi yaraladı. Saldırıda 1 kişi hayatını kaybetti.

Olay yerine gelen polis ekiplerinin saldırganı yakaladığı ve olaya ilişkin incelemenin sürdüğü aktarıldı.

Saldırının ardından olay yerine ambulans ve özel polis birlikleri geldi, çevredeki diğer okullarda da güvenlik önlemleri alındı.

İsveç Başbakanı Ulf Kristersson da basına yaptığı açıklamada, Fagersta'daki saldırının "ciddi bir olay" olduğunu kaydetti.

Kristersson, "Yaralıların olduğu bilgisi ulaştı. Olayın arkasında ne olduğunu henüz bilmiyoruz ancak polis büyük bir titizlikle çalışmalarını sürdürüyor" dedi.

Polis yetkilileri, olay yeri incelemesinin ardından düzenledikleri basın toplantısında, 1 kişinin hayatını kaybettiğini, 2'si ağır 3 kişinin yaralandığını açıkladı.

Polis Şefi Tommy Alriksson, saldırganın, 18 yaşında İsveç vatandaşı olduğunu ve vurularak gözaltına alındığını söyledi.

İsveç medyası ise saldırganın sosyal medya hesabından ırkçı paylaşımlar yaptığını kaydetti.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Leanne Sanders
title: First Nations leaders reflect as they commemorate the signing of Treaty 6
content:
First Nations from across Treaty 6 territory are celebrating and in Saskatchewan, will commemorate 150 years since the signing of the historic Treaty document.


Treaty 6 spans a wide swath of what is now northern Alberta and Saskatchewan.


It was signed on Aug. 23, 1876, at Fort Carlton and Sept. 9 at Fort Pitt. There were later adhesions to the Treaty through 1950.


Negotiated between the British Crown and Cree, Nakota (Assiniboine), Saulteaux, and Dene leaders, it covers central portions of present-day Alberta and Saskatchewan. It was intended to share the land in exchange for vital guarantees and meant to last “as long as the sun shines, the grass grows, and the river flows.”


Events are scheduled across the territory over the coming weekend-one of the largest being the Treaty 6 Commemoration at Fort Carlton, 100 kilometres north of Saskatoon by highway. The original Treaty parchment that was signed is available for viewing through Saturday.


First Nations leaders and Indigenous commentators have been weighing in about the importance of the Treaty and its anniversary.


“Today we honour our ancestors who stood together and entered into Treaty with hope for the generations yet to come,” said James Smith Cree Nation Chief Kirby Constant in a Facebook post while also calling on Canada to remember the promises that were made.


“We remember their strength, their sacrifices, and the promises that were made. A century and a half later, we are still here, still strong, still carrying our language, culture, ceremonies and our inherent rights forward. We honour the Treaty, we honour our ancestors, and we continue the work until every promise is fulfilled. We ask Canada to do the same.”


Another post by John Brady McDonald, a Nehiyawak-Metis writer and artist with ties to Muskeg Lake Cree Nation said the anniversary is an emotional one.


“Chief Mistawasis is my great great great grandfather. I am a direct descendant, as my great grandfather, Chief George Dreaver, was his grandson.


“150 years ago this weekend, Chief Mistawasis was the first signatory to Treaty Six at Fort Carlton.150 years ago, he made a decision he felt was the best for the survival of his family and those of his band. I will forever be proud of him, for he set the example of thinking of the survival of others,” McDonald said.


He shared a quote from a speech by Chief Mistawasis the day the Treaty was signed.


“I have heard my brothers speak, complaining of the hardships endured by our people. Some have bewailed the poverty and suffering that has come to Indians because of the destruction of the buffalo as the chief source of our living, the loss of the ancient glory of our forefathers; and with all that I agree, in the silence of my teepee and on the broad prairies where once our fathers could not pass for the great number of those animals that blocked their way; and even in our day, we have had to choose carefully our campground for fear of being trampled in our teepees,” Mistawasis said.


“With all these things, I think and feel intensely the sorrow my brothers express.


I speak directly to Poundmaker and The Badger and those others who object to signing this treaty. Have you anything better to offer our people? I ask, again, can you suggest any-thing that will bring these things back for tomorrow and all the tomorrows that face our people? I for one think that the Great White Queen Mother has offered us a way of life when the buffalo are no more. Gone they will be before many snows have come to cover our heads or graves if such should be,” his speech concluded.


“What we speak of and do now will last as long as the sun shines and the river runs, we are looking forward to our children’s children, for we are old and have but few days to live,” said a signatory at Fort Pitt, Sept. 9, 1876, Chief Weekaskookwasayin, or Chief Sweet Grass Abraham Wikaskokiseyin.


The Confederacy of Treaty 6 First Nations, headquartered in Alberta said “150 years later, we are still here.”


”Still gathering. Still dancing. Still singing our songs. Still carrying our languages, our ceremonies, our teachings and our responsibilities to Treaty,”said Grand Chief Joey Pete.


“This week was more than a commemoration of history. It was a reminder that Treaty No. 6 is not something of the past. Treaty is living. Treaty is forever.”

author: The Canadian Press
title: Studies show year-round shipping potential from Port of Churchill
content:
Manitoba’s premier says studies showing that year-round shipping is possible from the Port of Churchill boost the case for expanding the Arctic deep-sea port.


“Churchill could be a year-round port right now, with current technology and using icebreakers and ships that are a lot cheaper, a lot more affordable than we previously thought,” said Kinew at a press conference Friday.


The reports say advances in marine technology and declining sea ice due to climate change mean shipping can be greatly expanded from the current four-month window.


They show the waterways could be navigated year-round by icebreakers costing between $100 million and $410 million, rather than the billions of dollars it would cost for more heavy-duty ships.


Properly designed bulk carriers costing between $60 and $70 million could also navigate the route for nine to 10 months a year under most conditions, one of the studies says.


“What that means is a longer shipping season, more economic opportunity. It means that doing (liquefied natural gas) off the Hudson Bay coast is much more realistic,” said Kinew.


Shipping with lighter-duty vessels is made more possible as the amount of sea ice shrinks.


The window of ice-free water has grown by about a month since the 1980s. Every half-degree of warming adds about two weeks more, another study found.


The studies were conducted by the University of Manitoba, Fednav Ltd. and the Arctic Research Foundation, while funding came from the Manitoba and federal governments, as well as the Indigenous-owned Artic Gateway Group that owns the port.


Kinew has championed a port expansion, including potential fossil fuel exports, as a key economic driver for the province.


 


But the cost of making it an export terminal for liquefied natural gas could be in the range of $70 billion to $80 billion, he said.


“In order for Churchill to move energy products and to be economically viable, we basically have to build a project of that scale.”


The port has seen limited shipping activity in recent years, but Arctic Gateway Group has been working to bring back shippers since buying it from an American firm in 2018.


“We have invested into the Hudson Bay rail line. We have strengthened the port. We have improved reliability, introduced modern safety technologies and work towards bringing customers and cargo back,” said Michael Spence, mayor of Churchill and chair of Arctic Gateway.


He said the first grain shipment is set to sail out next week and the first potash shipment soon after.


While limited shipments have restarted, business groups are still wary of committing to the port that requires significant upgrades and has shipping limitations.


The federal government launched a study in February to gauge business interest in the port. It said the study should be done by the end of March but not what it might include.


Kinew declined to reveal those findings, saying it’s not his report to release.


The port is among the projects referred to the federal major projects office as a transformative strategy. It was not among the first round approved for fast-tracking.


Story by Ian Bickis

Studies show year-round shipping potential from Port of Churchill
