author: The Canadian Press
title: Yukon First Nations Wildfire say they haven’t been called to help in B.C.
content:
Fire crews with

Yukon First Nations Wildfire

 say they are ready, willing and able to help with out-of-control fires burning in B.C. and are wondering why they haven’t received the call.


Statements from the organization posted online say its crews are trained and certified and could be on the B.C. fire line faster than any crew flying in from overseas, but that instead firefighters are being brought to B.C. from countries like Mexico and Costa Rica.


Wildfire resources across Canada and internationally are co-ordinated through the Canadian Interagency Forest Fire Centre, which says in a statement that it is up to each provincial or territorial fire management agency to decide who they want to hire.


It says that hiring and contracting protocols vary from agency to agency, so specifics regarding which resources are brought in fall outside the organization’s purview.


The centre says it is working with Indigenous partners to better understand and address barriers to the participation and deployment of Indigenous wildfire resources.


Neither the BC Wildfire Service nor the provincial Ministry of Emergency Management immediately responded to a request for comment.


Yukon First Nations Wildfire says it’s not asking for special treatment but wants to know why it’s being “skipped.”


“Every dollar spent flying in international crews is a dollar that could go straight to the First Nation crews we have standing by. We guarantee that it costs less to deploy a crew from the Yukon to B.C. than it does from Mexico or Costa Rica,” an online post says.


Large fires burning in B.C.

 have required help from crews around Canada and internationally, including from Australia, Mexico, New Zealand and Costa Rica.


The Yukon’s territorial wildfire services also sent some members to B.C. last month.


Story by Ashley Joannou


The post

Yukon First Nations Wildfire say they haven’t been called to help in B.C.

 appeared first on

APTN News

.

author: anred
title: Misiones: campesinos denuncian golpizas, detenciones arbitrarias y una escalada de violencia de la empresa forestal Arauco
content:
Dos viviendas incendiadas de familias productoras


Mientras las 123 familias que conforman la Comisión de vecinos unidos por las chacras San Pedro reclaman una intervención del Gobierno de Misiones, ante el conflicto territorial con la multinacional forestal Arauco, nuevos testimonios de p

roductores de Puerto Argentino 1, 2 y 3, Palmera Boca, La Chacrita, San Juan Bosco y otros parajes suman sus voces a las denuncias que desde hace semanas vienen realizando debido a las detenciones, golpes, amenazas, secuestro de herramientas y motocicletas, viviendas incendiadas, cultivos destruidos y animales muertos, desaparecidos o heridos. 

Saúl Lindao, productor de Puerto Argentino 2, denunció que fue reducido hasta perder el conocimiento mientras trabajaba en su chacra, y que posteriormente un policía lo amenazó para que no contara lo ocurrido ni fuera al hospital. Y el testimonio de Angel Rivero, trasladado y detenido sin orden judicial.

El relevamiento comenzó con unas 123 familias, pero las organizaciones que acompañan el reclamo estiman que el conflicto alcanza a 300 grupos familiares, más de mil personas.

En el centro del conflicto se encuentra Arauco Argentina, la multinacional forestal chilena; uno de los mayores propietarios privados de tierras de Misiones.

Por Clarisa Néztor (i

ntegrante de

 Rebelión o Extinción Misiones y de la Red de Apoyo a Puente Quemado II),

 para ANRed.


Lo que sucede en las colonias rurales de San Pedro representa la cara real del extractivismo forestal en Misiones. Mientras las familias continúan reclamando respuestas y mantienen un acampe frente a la Municipalidad, siguen sumándose testimonios sobre procedimientos realizados en las chacras que describen un escenario de violencia institucional cada vez más preocupante. Esto deriva en un conflicto más profundo, que es la enorme concentración territorial alcanzada por Arauco en Misiones, y un modelo forestal que durante décadas contó con promoción, incentivos y vínculos permanentes con el poder político provincial. 


Arauco está presente en Misiones desde 1996. Se convirtió en el principal actor del sector forestal y en uno de los mayores propietarios privados de tierra de la provincia. Su expansión territorial acompañó el crecimiento de un modelo basado en grandes extensiones de monocultivos de pino y eucalipto destinados a abastecer la industria forestal. En una provincia donde existen cientos de miles de hectáreas de bosques implantados, la empresa llegó a concentrar por sí sola más de 230.000 hectáreas. 


Esa dimensión permite entender la desigualdad que atraviesa el conflicto actual. De un lado aparecen familias que necesitan pocas hectáreas para plantar mandioca, maíz, poroto, sandía o zapallo, criar animales y sostener a sus hijos. Del otro, una multinacional que controla una superficie extraordinaria, posee recursos jurídicos, económicos y logísticos que responden a sus intereses porque mantiene una relación institucional permanente con las máximas autoridades provinciales. 


Productores de Puerto Argentino 1, 2 y 3, Palmera Boca, La Chacrita, San Juan Bosco y otros parajes denuncian desde hace semanas detenciones, golpes, amenazas, secuestro de herramientas y motocicletas, incendio de sus viviendas, destrucción de cultivos y animales muertos, desaparecidos o heridos. En el centro del conflicto se encuentra Arauco Argentina, la multinacional forestal chilena y uno de los mayores propietarios privados de tierras de Misiones.


El relevamiento comenzó con unas 123 familias, pero las organizaciones que acompañan el reclamo estiman que el conflicto podría alcanzar a 300 grupos familiares y más de mil personas.


Saúl Lindao: “cuando desperté estaba esposado”


Saúl Lindao vive en Puerto Argentino 2 y forma parte de las familias campesinas de una zona que comprende 2500 hectáreas, donde ellos hacen uso de 200. Alrededor de las diez de la mañana del miércoles 19 de agosto se encontraba trabajando en los canteros de su chacra cuando llegaron efectivos de la Policía de Misiones acompañados por dos oficiales de Arauco, llamados los Verdes, por su vestimenta.


Lindao asegura que los representantes de la empresa llevaban machetes, mientras que los policías portaban distintas armas de fuego: escopetas, ametralladoras y una pistola calibre 9 milímetros. L

os efectivos le preguntaron si podían revisar el campamento y su vivienda, y Lindao les negó el paso sin una orden judicial. La policía reconoció que no tenían orden de allanamiento …

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Premier optimistic ahead of Canada-U.S trade deal deadline
content:
Nunavut Premier John Main says he feels “encouraged” by the progress in trade negotiations as yet another tariff deadline looms Friday at midnight.


Canada-U.S. Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc and Canada’s lead negotiator Janice Charette are in Washington, D.C., to negotiate a new Canada-U.S.-Mexico, or CUSMA, trade agreement with U.S. officials such as trade representative Jamieson Greer.


Canada is trying to avert a new round of tariffs that U.S. President Donald Trump has threatened on nearly $30 billion of Canadian goods if a new deal isn’t reached. At issue is the export of American milk and sale of American liquor north of the border, among other items.


“Although there are still several outstanding issues under active consideration, I’m confident that these efforts will lead to a mutually beneficial agreement,” Main said Thursday in a statement to Nunatsiaq News.


He said a new deal stands to strengthen supply chains that “matter deeply in northern and remote communities,” and that he feels optimistic it can be achieved.


But any deal would need to take into account “unique pressures” Nunavut is facing, like affordability, Main said, pointing to transportation costs, greater supply chain vulnerability, and the high cost of living.


“No single agreement solves everything,” he said.

“Our government is focused on making sure the North is part of the economic benefits that come from a strong and stable trade relationship.”


Prime Minister Mark Carney updated premiers Wednesday on the talks and urged them to restock American alcohol in their liquor stores.


Main said he’s ready to comply so that American products can be available for purchase again in Nunavut. 


“Whether Canadians want to buy American alcohol is up to them,” the premier added.


Former Nunavut premier

P.J. Akeeagok is also advocating for the territory as part of Carney’s Advisory Committee on Canada-U.S. Economic Relations.


Akeeagok is the only Inuk voice on the committee and previously stated his goal is to put the Arctic at the “centre of Canada’s strategic investment agenda and at the forefront of nation‑building.” 


“I have consistently emphasized the central importance of the Arctic to Canada’s sovereignty, security, defence posture, and critical minerals strategy,” Akeeagok shared in a short written statement to Nunatsiaq News.


“We hold significant opportunities for the country, and Inuit regions have a great deal to offer in shaping Canada’s long‑term economic and strategic position.”

author: Maira Escardovelli
title: Flávio Bolsonaro fez 3 propostas de lei sobre segurança da mulher em 24 anos de política
content:
Investigamos o que importa para os brasileiros além do que passa na campanha eleitoral. Leia mais reportagens como essa clicando

aqui

.


O senador e candidato à Presidência da República Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) tem feito vários acenos ao eleitorado feminino, estratégia explicada pela vantagem do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) na intenção de votos entre mulheres. Dados da última pesquisa Nexus/BTG Pactual, de 17 de agosto, apontam que Lula alcança 46% deste eleitorado, contra 32% de Flávio. 


Não à toa, no lançamento da pré-candidatura de Flávio em São Paulo, no mês de julho, no anúncio do candidato a vice em Brasília, no último dia 5, e no seu primeiro ato como candidato oficial no Rio de Janeiro, domingo passado, não faltaram menções às pautas femininas. Entre elas, críticas à violência contra mulheres e promessas de que agressores “vão mofar na cadeia”, além da citação a uma das bandeiras da campanha, o programa Brasil por Elas. 


Na atividade legislativa, porém, o cenário foi diferente. Um levantamento inédito realizado pela

Agência Pública

 mostra que

em quase 24 anos como parlamentar, entre 2003 e 2026, Flávio Bolsonaro apresentou apenas três propostas legislativas relacionadas à segurança das mulheres.

 Foram dois Projetos de Lei (PL), um no Senado e outro na Assembleia Legislativa do Rio de Janeiro (Alerj), e uma Proposta de Emenda Constitucional (PEC) no Congresso Nacional. 


Durante sua trajetória política, Flávio protocolou, no total, 306 propostas sobre diversos temas. Como senador, desde 2019, apresentou 59 PLs e 93 PECs. Já nos anos como deputado estadual na Alerj, cargo que ocupou por quatro mandatos consecutivos, de 2003 a 2019, protocolou 140 PLs e 14 Propostas de Emendas à Constituição Estadual do Rio de Janeiro.  


Para se ter ideia, as propostas relacionadas à segurança ou proteção de mulheres representam menos de 1% de todos os projetos assinados pelo filho 01 de Jair Bolsonaro ao longo de sua carreira política.


Entre as três propostas citadas, uma foi apresentada no primeiro semestre de 2026, em março, quando o parlamentar já era pré-candidato à presidência. Já a proposta de mudança constitucional é de novembro de 2025, um mês antes de Flávio Bolsonaro anunciar que seria pré-candidato à Presidência pelo PL. O terceiro foi enviado em 2017, durante o seu último mandato como deputado estadual. 


A reportagem questionou o candidato, por meio de sua assessoria, sobre a ausência de projetos para a proteção e segurança das mulheres durante os demais anos de sua atividade parlamentar. Por nota, ele respondeu que “a proteção às vítimas de violência, o combate aos crimes sexuais, a promoção da saúde feminina e o fortalecimento do planejamento familiar sempre estiveram entre as principais bandeiras defendidas por Flávio Bolsonaro, desde sua atuação como deputado estadual até o exercício do mandato no Senado Federal. Como costuma afirmar, trata-se de ‘uma pauta da direita’”. A íntegra da nota pode ser lida

neste link

.


Por que isso importa?


O Brasil registrou um número recorde de feminicídios em 2025 em dez anos de monitoramento pelo Fórum Brasileiro de Segurança Pública. Foram 1.568 mulheres assassinadas por razão de gênero no ano passado, um aumento de 4,7% em comparação a 2024.


De que tratam as propostas? 


No Congresso Nacional, quase completando oito anos de mandato, o senador protocolou duas proposições sobre segurança voltadas às mulheres. Uma delas, o

PL 1400/2026, altera a Lei Maria da Penha (Lei nº 11.340, de 7 de agosto de 2006) para permitir que a autoridade policial possa conceder, em caráter imediato, medidas protetivas de urgência

 em casos de violência doméstica e familiar contra as mulheres. A legislação, no entanto, já autoriza a polícia a conceder proteção imediata à vítima quando há risco iminente e não há juiz disponível na delegacia no momento da ocorrência. 


O projeto ainda não teve andamento para as Comissões da Casa legislativa e aguarda despacho desde o dia 25 de março, data em que foi publicada no Diário do Senado. 


“O que o projeto faz é transformar essa exceção em regra geral. O avanço, se existir, não está em criar algo novo, mas em tentar reduzir o tempo de resposta, isso pode ser visto de modo positivo”, explica Anabel Pêssoa, professora de direito da UFRPE e cofundadora do Instituto Maria da Penha. 


Já a proposta de emenda à Constituição (PEC 41/2025), apresentada em 11 de novembro de 2025, propõe alterar o artigo 5º da Constituição …

author: Antimídia
title: Ataque a Aratikuty
content:
Dia 17 de agosto de 2026 a polícia militar e fazendeiros deram início a mais uma série de ataques a indígenas Guarani-Kaiowá, desta vez na retomada Aratikuty, em Dourados, nos territórios ocupados pelo Estado do Mato Grosso do Sul.


No dia 19, a polícia militar realizou um despejo sem ordem judicial. Atacando indígenas com gás lacrimogênio, balas de borracha e munição letal. E prendendo cinco pessoas.


Os ataques já deixaram mais de 10 pessoas feridas, incluindo três crianças. Também incendiaram moradias, destruiram alimentos e estruturas comunitárias. Há inclusive relatos de tortura. Uma escavadeira foi usada para cavar uma vala, para impedir a passagem de indígenas.


Os latifundiários por trás dos ataques têm histórico de agressão contra indígenas. São do mesmo grupo que criou o chamado "caveirão rural". Têm conexões com grandes escritórios de advocacia, cooperativas do agronegócio, o sindicato rural e empresas de segurança privada que atuam em conjunto com pistoleiros.


Políticos de extrema-direita, como Marcos Pollon e Rodolfo Nogueira, do PL de Bolsonaro, foram ao local para intimidar e criminalizar a retomada. Ambos têm ligação com a milícia Invasão Zero, que atua contra as retomadas em diversas partes do país.


Apesar da violência de que são alvo há séculos e em resposta à paralisação das demarcações pelo governo federal, Guarani-Kaiowá intensificaram as retomadas na região.

author: Rizomatica
title: Se realiza funeral de El Vejetal en Padre de las Casas bajo fuerte resguardo policial,  familia no logra revertir catalogación de alto riesgo
content:
Luego de 4 días de incertidumbre, hoy viernes 21 de agosto, el Servicio Médico Legal de Temuco entregó el cuerpo de Gabriel Utreras Sanhuenza aka Vegetal, a su familia y comunidad, quienes debieron dirigirse directamente al cementerio de Padre de las Casas, sin haberlo velado y seguidos por un fuerte contingente policial.


La Delegacion Presidencial de La Araucanía, basảndose en informes de Carabineros y la Policia de Investigaciones (PDI), categorizó el funeral de Gabriel como de alto riesgo, decision que no pudo ser revertida por la familia y su abogado.


Durante la noche del 20 de agosto,  se desarrolló un punto de prensa  en las afueras del hogar de Gabriel, quien murió por un disparo de carabineros el día lunes 17 de agosto.


El abogado querellante y representante de la familia, Rodrigo Pizarro Rosales, declaró que por disposición del delegado presidencial de La Araucanía, en base únicamente a los informes de carabineros y PDI se catologo el «funeral de alto riesgo», impidiendo que la familia y comunidad pueda velar al joven rapero. Pese a que desde el lunes la familia realizó todas las diligencias para solicitar a la delegación presidencial que emita una resolución que cambiara la categorización del funeral, este respondió con una negativa, pese a que existía respaldo jurídico. Por su parte, la familia ha presentado una querella criminal, para que se investiguen los hechos y se acredite la participación de quiénes resulten responsables, lo que el abogado cataloga como homicidio lo ocurrido en la madrugada del lunes 17 de agosto.


Jonathan Gonzalez, presidente de la organizacion social y comunitaria Mucho Flow Sureño dió una declaración en nombre de la familia y la comunidad rapera, expresando el gran cariño y legado que dejó Vegetal, desde el crear arte consciente que se reflejaba en cada una de sus canciones y el gran aporte que generó a su comunidad. Así mismo, se hace un llamado a la calma y acompañar a la familia el día de mañana viernes a las 11 am en el Cementerio de Padre las Casas, donde se desarrollará su funeral. Además de señalar que, el funeral estará bajo resguardo policial, debido a que la Delegación presidencial de la Araucanía lo catologó como «funeral de alto riesgo».


Esta información se publicó en

Radio Kurruf

.

author: Unknown
title: Ankara/Çayırhan: Maden göçtü: 1 ölüm 19 yaralanma bildirildi
content:
Ankara'nın Beypazarı ilçesine bağlı Hırkatepe Mahallesi'ndeki Çayırhan Enerji İşletmesi sahasında cuma günü saat 18.00 sıralarında maden kazası meydana geldi.


Ankara Valiliği'nin açıklamasına göre, "ilk tespitlerde çalışma sahasının arkasındaki tavanın çökmesi sonucu oluşan basınç" işçilerin savrulmasına yol açtı.


Kazada madenci Erdi Kahveci öldü. Valilik olaydan toplam 20 kişinin etkilendiğini, yaralanan 19 işçinin hastanelerde tedavi altına alındığını bildirdi.


Olay yerine jandarma, emniyet, itfaiye, AFAD, UMKE ve sağlık ekipleri sevk edildi. Yaralıların hastanelere taşınması için 15 ambulans görevlendirildi.


İlk saatlerde haber ajanslarına yansıyan yaralı sayısı önce 8, ardından 12 olarak açıklanmıştı. Ankara Valiliği'nin daha sonra yaptığı açıklamayla bilanço 1 ölü, 19 yaralı olarak güncellendi.


Valilik kazanın ardından gerekli inceleme ve soruşturmanın başlatıldığını açıkladı.


YENİ Parti'li Murat Emir: “İş cinayetleri kader değildir”


YENİ Parti Grup Başkanvekili Murat Emir, Ankara’nın Nallıhan ilçesindeki Çayırhan Kömür İşletmeleri’nde meydana gelen bir işçinin hayatını kaybettiği maden kazasına ilişkin sosyal medya hesabından açıklama yaptı: 


“Ankara Nallıhan'daki Çayırhan Kömür İşletmeleri'nde meydana gelen maden göçüğünde bir emekçinin hayatını kaybettiğini ve 12 emekçinin yaralandığını derin bir üzüntüyle öğrendim. Hayatını kaybeden madencimize Allah’tan rahmet, acılı ailesine sabır; yaralılarımıza acil şifalar diliyorum. İş cinayetleri kader değildir”


Dört işçinin durumunun ağır olduğu bildirildi


Ankara Valisi Yakup Canpolat, Sözcü TV'ye yaptığı ilk açıklamada yaralılardan dördünün durumunun ağır olduğunu bildirdi.


İlk haberlerde yaralı işçilerin Beypazarı Devlet Hastanesi'ne kaldırıldığı belirtildi. Yaralıların sağlık durumlarına ve ağır yaralıların hangi hastanelerde tedavi edildiğine ilişkin ayrıntılı resmi açıklama henüz yapılmadı.


Kazanın kesin nedeni, çökmenin meydana geldiği galerideki çalışma koşulları ve iş sağlığı ve güvenliği önlemlerine ilişkin, henüz yetkili ya da uzman kuruluşlardan bir açıklama yapılmadı.


(AEK)

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Hind Rajab’s Family Says Israel’s Investigation Into Hind’s Death Just a PR Ploy
content:
“Even now, all I hear is her crying, ‘I’m scared,’ and her plea: ‘Come here, Mama, take me,’” Hind’s mother said.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Hind Rajab’s mother has dismissed the Israeli military’s announcement this week that it is opening a supposed criminal investigation into the killing of her 5-year-old daughter, saying that it is nothing more than a PR move meant to distract from Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza.

“Why did the investigation and the acknowledgment of the shooting at Hind’s car and at the paramedics come only after more than two years?” Wesam Hamada, Hind’s mother, told the Associated Press on Friday. “It’s an attempt to distract from what’s happening in Gaza and improve the [Israeli] army’s image to the world. That’s it.”

On Wednesday, Israel’s military acknowledged that its soldiers played a role in the horrific series of events in January 2024, in which Hind, her 15-year-old cousin, and five members of their family were killed.

The military admitted to the slaughter of her adult family members, but did not take responsibility for the killing of Hind or her cousin Layan Hamada specifically, despite numerous independent investigations finding that they were shot by Israeli soldiers in a tank. Israeli soldiers have been found to be targeting children in Gaza, often with gunshots to the head, countless other times since Hind’s killing.

“I don’t trust the Israeli authorities, I don’t trust their government, and I don’t trust any justice system they have,” Hind’s mother said in an interview with NBC. “I don’t want an investigation used to whitewash anyone’s image.”

Hind’s grandmother, who is also named Hind Rajab, similarly dismissed the investigation. “For us this is not an admission but rather an attempt by the Israeli army to justify to the world how it committed the crime and how they executed Hind,” she told AFP. “The army is trying to justify its position to the world, claiming that what happened was a mistake and that the soldiers who committed it will be prosecuted.”

An Israeli tank sprayed the car carrying Hind and her family members with hundreds of bullets, despite having a clear line of sight to the children inside, an investigation by Forensic Architecture found.

After her family was killed, Hind remained trapped in the car with their bodies for hours, a tank looming nearby, as Palestinian Red Crescent workers waited for the Israeli military to give clearance for them to rescue her. In those hours, she spoke with rescuers and her mother on the phone. Recordings from the Palestinian Red Crescent documented the terrifying last hours of the little girl’s life before she was gunned down.

“I’m so scared, please come. Please call someone to come and take me,” Hind said to emergency dispatchers.

Rajab noted that Israel only acknowledged Hind’s killing because her harrowing phone call to rescuers became so widely known, pointing out that there are many other similarly horrific killings that Israel will never follow up on.

Hind’s family still mourns her death.

“She died with the most heartbreaking sound I’ve ever heard,” Hamada told NBC. “Even now, all I hear is her crying, ‘I’m scared,’ and her plea: ‘Come here, Mama, take me.’”

Hamada has demanded an independent investigation that will actually lead to answers. “I want to know who killed my daughter, who killed my family members, and who killed the paramedics who went to rescue her. Who gave the orders? Who fired the shots?”

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Former manager of Arctic Bay hunting association charged with fraud
content:
Justice Aug 21, 2026 – 2:30 pm EDT

Investigation flagged more than $230,000 in unauthorized transactions

A fraud investigation involving the Ikajutit Hunters and Trappers Association in Arctic Bay, seen here, has led to the arrest of the organization’s former manager. (File photo by David Venn)

RCMP have charged a former manager of Arctic Bay’s hunters association with defrauding the organization of more than $200,000.

Officers were informed about the alleged crimes in November 2024, RCMP said Friday a news release. The investigation flagged more than $230,000 in unauthorized transactions between 2022 and 2024.

Amy Barnabas, 39, faces charges for fraud over $5,000, bookkeeping fraud, and criminal breach of trust.

When reached by phone, the Ikajutit Hunters and Trappers Association declined to comment.

Barnabas is scheduled to appear in court in Arctic Bay on Oct. 5.

title: Rakı içerken görüntülenmişti: AKP Bozcaada Başkanı görevden alındı
content:
AKP Bozcaada İlçe Başkanı Burak Aktan, 19 Mayıs’ta getirildiği görevinden alındı. Aktan’ın Çanakkale’de bir restoranda içki içerken partide görevli bir avukat tarafından gizlice kameraya alındığı ve Genel Merkez’e şikayet edildiği öne sürüldü.

Birgün’den Serkan İlik’in haberine göre, 2017-2021 yılları arasında da Bozcaada İlçe Başkanlığı yapan Burak Aktan ise sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı açıklamada yaşananların ayrıntılarına girmeyi doğru bulmadığını belirtti.

Öte yandan Çanakkale AKP’de devam eden parti içi çekişmelerin teşkilatta bölünmelere neden olduğu iddia edildi.

Parti kulislerinde Çanakkale Milletvekili Ayhan Gider ile eski Milletvekili ve halen İçişleri Bakan Yardımcısı olan Bülent Turan arasında yaşandığı öne sürülen siyasi gerilimin teşkilat içerisinde farklı grupların oluşmasına yol açtığı konuşuluyor.

author: Abigail Boggs
title: Trump Administration Is Reviving a Visa Rule That Could Disrupt Higher Education
content:
These new rules will make it harder for some international students to visit and stay in the US.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The Trump administration is revising a visa rule for international students that in part determines how long, and under what conditions, they can stay in the country. The change sounds technical. Its effects are not.

Beginning Sept. 15, 2026, most students entering the U.S. on F-1 and J-1 visas – meaning visas for international students and exchange visitors, including students and scholars – will no longer be admitted for “duration of status.” Duration of status means they can remain in the U.S. as long they are enrolled in their academic program, or shortly thereafter.

Now, academic visa holders will instead be able to stay in the country for a predetermined period of time, generally four years.

Those who need more time to complete a degree will have to reapply to U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services for permission to stay.

The change could also complicate international travel: Students returning to the U.S. will have to make sure their fixed period of admission has not expired, in addition to having the valid visa and school documents normally required for reentry.

The rule also lets full-time international students stay 30 days in the country after they complete their program, as opposed to the 60 days they currently have to remain in the U.S.

I study the history of international students in U.S. higher education. Universities rely on international students for tuition, teaching, research and other kinds of skilled work.

These new rules will make it harder for some international students to visit and stay in the country, a result that will likely have negative consequences for universities and colleges, too.

U.S. colleges and universities hosted 1,177,766 international students in the 2024-25 school year, an all-time high that made up approximately 6% of all higher education students.

Most of them were working toward degrees in in science, technology, engineering and mathematics.

Nearly 488,500 of those international students were seeking graduate degrees. More than 294,000 of them participated in a federal program called Optional Practical Training, which helps some international students work in jobs related to their field of study before or after they graduate.

International enrollment grew steadily at U.S. colleges and universities, from about 565,000 students in the 2004-05 school year to more than 1 million by the 2015-16 academic year.

Growth then slowed during the first Trump administration but began rising again after 2021.

The concentration is much higher in some programs and institutions. At Purdue, for example, international students make up 63% of graduate students in mechanical engineering. At Columbia University, non-U.S. residents made up 53% of graduate students in the fall of 2024.

Since 2024, the greatest number of international students has come from India. The next largest group is students from China. For more than a decade, students from China made up the largest group of international students in the U.S. But the number of Chinese students has dropped over the past several years.

International students are important for university finances, too.

Most of these students are not eligible for U.S. federal student aid or loans.

More than half of international students report “personal or family funds” as their primary source of financial support to help pay for their education. These students contributed nearly US$55 billion to the U.S. economy in 2024, according to the international student exchange nonprofit Institute of International Education.

International graduate students also frequently teach undergraduate courses, conduct experiments and staff research laboratories.

Until now, most international students did not have to reapply to maintain or extend their standard F-1 student visa midway through their course of study.

And if a student remained enrolled and complied with immigration rules, a university could extend the student’s expected completion date of their program when more time was needed.

The new rule introduces a separate federal immigration review for every student whose course of study goes beyond four years. This, according to the Department of Homeland Security, will add 393,500 new visa reviews to the U.S. government workload each year.

title: Neuquén: sigue la amenaza de desalojo contra la Lof Melo y mañana habrá movilización
content:
El operativo represivo pudo completar sólo una parte de su agresión contra las Lof Kinxikew (Quintriqueo) y Melo el miércoles 19, y el pueblo mapuche se mantiene en su territorio ancestral. Pero hoy, el juez Francisco Astoul Bonorino rechazó el pedido de la comunidad mapuche Lof Kinxikew para suspender la medida. Según el magistrado,

cuya familia es propietaria de una inmobiliaria

, es válido expulsar a la comunidad de su territorio aunque no haya un fallo de fondo sobre la propiedad comunitaria mapuche, beneficiando de facto a la familia belga Broers.


Foto: Alejandra Bartoliche


Reporte de Maitén Cañicul de la FM Che.


Con información de FM Che, Agencia FARCO y Confederación Mapuche de Neuquén.


Luego de un enorme operativo desplegado en la mañana del miércoles 19 de agosto promovido por el juez Francisco Bonorino, se efectivizó el desalojo a la comunidad mapuche Kintxikew de uno de los predios que comparte con la comunidad mapuche Melo.


Sin embargo, a las 14 horas, las fuerzas represivas se retiraron del paraje El Pedregoso sin poder desalojar a la comunidad Melo, argumentando que no estaban dadas las condiciones para llevar adelante un desalojo con presencia de menores y adultos mayores en el lugar. El operativo desplegado solo incluía fuerzas represivas y no había ninguna otra institución para garantizar el procedimiento.


Por eso el territorio comunitario de las comunidades Melo y Kintxikew (Quintriqueo), a aproximadamente 30 kilómetros de la ciudad de Villa La Angostura, aún se encuentra bajo su resguardo. Pero la amenaza persiste.

La Confederación Mapuche de Neuquén informó este jueves

 que las fuerzas represivas del Estado volvieron a desplegarse en el lugar, específicamente en el sector del Pedregoso que fue desalojado de manera sorpresiva, ilegal y violenta el 19 de agosto.


Astoul Bonorino reafirmó el desalojo


Este viernes,

el juez Francisco Astoul Bonorino rechazó el pedido el pedido de la comunidad Kinxikew para frenar la ejecución de desalojo

. El fallo no define el reclamo de fondo sobre la propiedad comunitaria mapuche, pero permite que continúe la ejecución de una sentencia firme mientras ese otro juicio sigue en trámite.


La decisión fue adoptada por el juez Francisco Astoul Bonorino, titular del Juzgado Civil, Comercial, Laboral y de Minería de Villa La Angostura, quien resolvió que la ejecución de la sentencia de desalojo puede continuar mientras sigue tramitando la causa principal iniciada por la comunidad. En términos prácticos, el fallo significa que la Justicia no frenó el desalojo y que la medida solicitada por la comunidad fue rechazada.


Bonorino beneficia de esta manera a la familia de origen belga Broers, que reclama la titularidad del territorio ancestral mapuche. Villa La Angostura no es cualquier lugar en la Patagonia: ubicada en el corazón del Corredor de los Lagos, rodeada por el Parque Nacional Nahuel Huapi, es una locación codiciada por su alto valor turístico.


En este contexto, este sábado 22 las comunidades convocan a una caravana de los pueblos en solidaridad que tendrá dos puntos de concentración: uno a las 14 horas desde el Puente de las Piedritas en Villa de la Angostura, y otro a la misma hora en el estacionamiento ferroviario en la terminal de Bariloche para confluir en el territorio en resguardo.


Amancay Quintriqueo Lonco de la Lof Kintxikew (Quintriqueo) y Noelia Huenumir Pigen, lonco de la Lof Melo, convocaron a movilizar: “El día de ayer (por el miércoles 19) fue desalojada nuestra comunidad pero el objetivo de esta caravana es también demostrar la resistencia y que no nos van a mover de acá, que hoy hay que resguardar también el territorio de la Lof Melo porque no podemos seguir entregando un metro cuadrado más a todos estos extranjeros que hace tiempo vienen quedándose con nuestros territorios”.


“Hay que evidenciar todo lo que viene haciendo este gobierno junto con el Poder Judicial, el Poder Ejecutivo, que son ellos quienes hoy entregaron nuestro territorio a un extranjero de descendencia. El pedido desde el territorio comunitario es acompañar de manera presencial el resguardo, hacen un llamado a organizaciones sociales, colectivos y vecinos y vecinas que deseen acercarse al lugar”, expresaron.


Además, denunciaron la complicidad del gobierno provincial de Rolando Figueroa y del ministro Jorge Tobares. Las comunidades denuncian que el poder político de la provincia, lejos de intervenir para evitar el desalojo violento y teniendo las …

Loui Ridi, a Palestinian American man who lives in Ohio, traveled to the occupied West Bank on Monday to help relatives defend their family home in the village of Qusra, south of Nablus. Israeli settlers have surrounded the home, which Ridi owns, for more than a week. Settlers have besieged several Palestinian houses in the village, trapping people inside and cutting off water and electricity in some cases.

“I’m not getting no protection here. I still fear for my life. I still fear for my family’s life here,” says Ridi, who joins Democracy Now! from the occupied West Bank. Ridi has raised an American flag on his home and reached out to the U.S. Embassy for help. “The IDF is not even making it better here. They’re not allowing us to leave the house. They’re not allowing anyone to come to my house freely,” says Ridi, explaining that getting food to the house takes “hours, if not days.”

The settlers “can act like this because of the active support from the Israeli government that gives them weapons, gives them ATVs,” says Israeli reporter Oren Ziv, who has traveled to Qusra twice in recent days. Ziv says the Israeli government also supports “the establishment of more and more [settler] outposts that are kind of front bases for these terror attacks.”

author: Leanne Sanders
title: Whitecap Dakota Nation gets new money from Ottawa for virtual health project
content:
Progress on a unique virtual care facility housing technology to connect Indigenous, rural, and remote communities with healthcare services was unveiled at Whitecap Dakota First Nation Thursday.


Called the Virtual Health Hub (VHH), it is located on Whitecap Dakota Nation land, 26 kilometres south of Saskatoon. The facility is the first of its kind in Canada.


Indigenous Services Canada (ISC) Minister Mandy Gull-Masty was on hand to announce $5.4 million in new money for the VHH.


That’s in addition to the over $28.2 million ISC has already invested toward the construction of the facility.


Construction costs are being shared between federal and provincial governments with Saskatchewan providing $9.1 million, covering one-third of the facility’s construction budget.


“We know that communities like Whitecap, when you give them the tools and you get out of their way, and you support their vision, they are able to take these benefits far beyond what we can envision as a government,” Gull-Masty said.


Construction on the state-of-the-art building officially started in September 2025 and is due for completion in early 2027.


According to the VHH website, the facility is intended to eventually serve as a national hub for virtual patient care. It uses telehealth, artificial intelligence, robotics, and other emerging technologies to bring services to communities that have long faced systemic barriers to care.


A video demonstrating how robotics will be used (featured on the website) shows a pregnant woman from Stony Rapids, located more than 1,000 kilometres north of Saskatoon, undergoing a virtual ultrasound. An ultrasound technologist at the current VHH office in Saskatoon is shown employing a device remotely while a health care worker in Stony Rapids facilitates. The woman is able to see her baby on a monitor and the images can then be used for diagnostics.


Gull-Masty related her personal experience with being pregnant while she was living in her home community in Quebec.


“Far too many Indigenous peoples, including myself, have had to leave communities to access health care,” Gull-Masty said. “I am one of the people that also had to travel three days to receive an ultrasound when I had children. And I can really, you know, personally understand the stress that that takes. Not only having to leave your community, but to plan for the care of your other children as well as the time that you lose when you’re employed.


“This is something that, you know, really spoke to me in a very personal way and resonated with me.”


Travel from remote communities like Stony Rapids and Black Lake for health and other services in the south can be gruelling. While most people from those communities travel to Prince Albert or Saskatoon primarily by air via Stony Rapids Airport on carriers like Rise Air, travelers can also drive. However, the trip on the rough, unpaved Hwy 905 and seasonal winter roads heading south can take 20 to 22 hours and requires overnight stays. And it’s only available when the weather and road conditions allow.


”Families do have to travel. They have to be away from home. For elders especially, this can be very stressing. We have many elders that are traveling for medical appointments and at times are not fluent in English or French and speak a whole other language. And this is an additional, I think, source of stress for them when they’re on the road,” Gull-Masty said.


Chief Darcy Bear said the use of technology at the VHH will not replace health care workers, something he said some people fear.


“That’s not the case at all. We are actually empowering the health care professional to be available remotely in northern and remote communities. We’re already in 18 communities and that’s including hospitals in this province,” Bear said.


“If you look at Canada, spending $400 billion in health care, but the quality of health care is going in the opposite direction…how can we deliver more effective, efficient public health care? It’s true. It’s all the remote technologies.”


Bear said the VHH will not only benefit Indigenous communities, noting that an office had opened in the town of Gravelbourg, 295 kilometres south of Saskatoon.


The facility at Whitecap Dakota First Nation is scheduled for completion in early 2027.


Other projects underway

title: First step taken to open mass graves in Shengal
content:
In 2015, after Shengal was liberated from ISIS gangs, a mass grave containing the remains of 62 people who were killed during the genocide (ferman) was discovered near the town of Khanasor. At the time, regional government officials brought the bodies to the area and buried them near the Sharafadin Shrine for propaganda purposes, without conducting DNA tests or identifying the victims.


This approach deeply hurt the memories and feelings of the victims’ families, who had spent years trying to establish the identities of their loved ones and bury them in accordance with Yazidi (Êzidî) religious rituals.


Today, the Baghdad Institute of Forensic Medicine and the Iraqi Directorate for Mass Graves took the first official step. A special delegation was present in front of the Sharafadin Shrine, records of the victims’ families were collected, and an official ceremony to begin the excavation of these graves is expected to take place in the coming days. The remains will also be sent to the Forensic Medicine Center in Baghdad for identification and will then be returned to their families.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: AIPAC Loses Yet Another House Race It Poured Millions of Dollars Into
content:
AIPAC funneled money into opposing a candidate who has barely mentioned Israel on the campaign trail.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

AIPAC has lost yet another race into which it poured millions of dollars on Thursday after California state Sen. Aisha Wahab won her special election to serve out the rest of Eric Swalwell’s term in the U.S. House of Representatives.

The Associated Press called the race on Thursday evening for Wahab, who received 53 percent of the vote compared to Democratic opponent Melissa Hernandez’s 47 percent. Wahab is the first Afghan American ever elected to the U.S. Congress, and was the first Muslim woman elected to the California legislature.

Wahab is slated to serve out the rest of Swalwell’s term, which ends in January, after he resigned over sexual assault allegations made against him. She will represent a swath of the Bay Area, and will face off against Hernandez again in the general election in November for a full term.

AIPAC’s super PAC, United Democracy Project (UDP), poured $2.5 million into opposing Wahab and backing Hernandez, the New York Times reports, much of it in the final weeks of the race.

The spending has been somewhat puzzling, baffling even pro-Israel leaders in the state who question why the lobbying powerhouse would spend so much on a race that, unlike many others this election cycle, has not been defined by the candidates’ stances on the U.S.’s policies toward Israel. One Bay Area pro-Israel leader even characterized Wahab as “not an anti-Zionist … like Rashida Tlaib or Ilhan Omar,” per Haaretz.

Wahab has expressed some support for Palestinian rights, but it has been limited to a few hints along the campaign trail: In a candidate’s forum in April, Wahab answered “yes” to a question about whether or not Israel was committing genocide.

When asked by streamer Hasan Piker if she believes the U.S. should end all aid to Israel, Wahab said “yes, but, like I said, humanitarian aid is important to me, too.” In that interview, she also touted that legislation that she introduced in 2025 regarding Gaza discusses “holding the perpetrators accountable from both sides.”

The race was already a longshot for AIPAC and Hernandez. Wahab had already won two prior primaries over Hernandez in June by double digits, before AIPAC’s late spending blitz. That spending seems to have helped AIPAC to close the gap a bit, but Wahab still won by a decisive six points.

Wahab herself had questioned the spending in an interview with Politico last week.

“They seem to have more money than God,” she said. “On every single credential, I am the most qualified. So what’s the elephant in the room? At the end of the day, all I can say is that it’s based on prejudice and racism.”

Indeed, Wahab also doesn’t fit the profile of progressive candidates typically opposed by AIPAC, which has long supported conservative candidates in both parties. Wahab’s campaign platform says nothing about progressive priorities like Medicare for All, abolishing ICE, or a moratorium on the construction of AI companies’ data centers. She claimed support for these issues in her interview with Piker, but has otherwise been muted about them on the campaign trail.

title: Palestine Action ‘Barclays 5’ Will Not Be Sentenced As Terrorists
content:
Five Palestine Action activists who broke windows and threw red paint at a Barclays branch will not be sentenced under terrorism charges,

a judge ruled today

.


Brendon O’Hagan and Mohammed Malik, both 28; Amanda Kelly and Hmeera Atiqnisar, both 31; and Alma Yaniv, 70, were found guilty in June of causing more than £200,000 of damage of the Burnley site after spray painting it red and smashing its windows with hammers in the early hours of 5 August 2024.


Prosecutors had retrospectively requested they be sentenced under terrorism charges, despite not having been charged or convicted under terrorism laws. But ruling at Preston crown court today, Judge Altham said that “while the damage was undoubtedly significant,” he was “not satisfied that it amounted… to ‘serious damage’” under the Terrorism Act 2000. Celebrations broke out among supporters who had gathered outside the court. 


During the trial, the defendants argued their actions were part of a wider campaign by Palestine Action against Barclays bank over its investment in Israeli weapons manufacturer Elbit Systems. Barclays

divested from Elbit Systems

 in October 2024.


The five will be sentenced on 4 September.


Speaking to Novara Media immediately after the ruling, Malik said the decision was “a massive relief” after an “emotional rollercoaster”.


“But while this is a victory for us, and shows we can’t be backed into a corner, we must not forget all of the Filton 25,” he said, referring to fellow Palestine Action activists convicted of terrorism offences. “We pray for a positive outcome for them, too, and hope their convictions will be overturned.”


Welcoming the news, Ruth Ehrlich, director of external relations at Liberty, said the process would nevertheless “

have a chilling effect on people’s willingness” to protest.


She added that it was particularly concerning that the defendants and jury were unaware that terrorism legislation could be applied after the verdict.


The judge also warned that the same ruling would not necessarily apply to similar actions resulting in criminal damage. 


Coinciding with the ruling, a

s many as 200 people are believed to have taken part in a sit-in outside Preston crown court. The protest, organised by activist group Defend our Judges, resulted in several arrests and people were taken away for holding banners pledging their support for Palestine Action.


The Barclays Five said: “

The state is doing everything possible to deter direct action for Palestine precisely because it has been so effective against the Israeli war machine, but we could never regret trying to stop a genocide.”

author: Marina Amaral
title: Casas Bahia: o peso do jornalismo investigativo em um negócio “de família”
content:
Quer receber os textos desta coluna em primeira mão no seu e-mail? Assine a Newsletter da Pública, enviada sempre às sextas-feiras, 8h. Para receber as próximas edições,

inscreva-se aqui

.


Curiosamente foi uma voz do mercado, e não um jornalista, que fez a ligação da crise de reputação das Casas Bahia na derrocada da empresa, que anunciou o pedido de recuperação judicial no domingo passado (16).


Com uma pergunta no título “Casas Bahia, passivo reputacional ou crise do varejo?”

Camila Farani, investidora de capital de risco há 15 anos, presidente da G2 Capital respondeu em sua


coluna


no Estadão: “A resposta é os dois, um alimentou o outro de formas que o balanço não consegue mostrar sozinho”.

 E avisou: “Tem uma história anterior ao balanço que precisa ser contada”.


O interessante é que foram os jornalistas que levantaram os fatos que a investidora descreve como anteriores ao balanço, embora agora a maior parte das reportagens tenha se fixado na “crise do varejo”, que está longe de ser nova, ao explicar o endividamento de 17 bilhões do grupo que, na era pré-Amazon e Mercado Livre, foi um dos mais influentes no país, e também um dos maiores anunciantes da mídia também abalada pela Internet.


“Samuel Klein, o fundador, construiu a Casas Bahia do zero. Imigrante polonês que sobreviveu à guerra, chegou ao Brasil sem nada e ergueu uma das maiores redes de varejo da América Latina. A narrativa do self-made man foi repetida por décadas pela imprensa, pelos livros de gestão, pelas palestras de empreendedorismo.

O que ninguém contou, até a Agência Pública investigar em 2021, é que Klein manteve por décadas um esquema de aliciamento e exploração sexual das crianças e adolescentes dentro da própria estrutura da empresa. O caso ganhou nome:


‘Caso K’

”, pontua a investidora.


Farani também lembra o caso do filho de Samuel, Saul Klein, que se tornou réu em maio deste ano por favorecimento à prostituição, tráfico de pessoas incluindo menores de idade e organização criminosa. Se o pai não foi processado, porque a imprensa silenciou até a sua morte, mesmo com a existência de registros policiais e judiciais desde os anos 1990, o caso Saul mereceu maior cobertura depois que passou a ser investigado pelo Ministério Público no final de 2020.


Ainda assim, o escândalo do fundador das Casas Bahia rendeu consequências depois da publicação da reportagem da Pública, em abril de 2021, a primeira a fazer justiça às vítimas,

 muitas delas menores quando os crimes foram cometidos, e que só adultas descobriram que os crimes já haviam prescrito.

Entre outros impactos, a

reportagem resultou em um Projeto de Lei, o PL Caso Klein

, que propõe alterar o Código Civil para ampliar de 3 para 20 anos o prazo de prescrição para as vítimas de crimes sexuais cometidos contra crianças e adolescentes. Aprovado pela Câmara em 2023, está parado no Senado desde então.


Até a família Klein reagiu às revelações suspendendo as atividades do Instituto Samuel Klein, criado pelos netos de Samuel depois da sua morte, em 2014, para preservar um legado, manchado pela revelação dos crimes do patriarca. Embora parte das ações da família nas Casas Bahia tenha sido vendida em 2013, e a empresa tenha se tornado uma sociedade aberta em 2019, até hoje a família tem presença na administração: Raphael Klein, neto de Samuel e filho de Michael Klein, faz parte do Conselho de Administração e participa dos comitês de Finanças e de Pessoas e Governança.


Como observa Farani, o que as Casas Bahia vendiam era o sentimento de pertencimento e confiança aos clientes de baixa renda, que adquiriam carnês a juros que engordavam o patrimônio dos Klein

, mas os permitiam realizar sonhos de consumo de bens que já eram essenciais para os mais endinheirados, como fogões, geladeiras e TVs. Essa confiança foi quebrada quando esses bens se tornaram “presentes” para as filhas de famílias pobres exploradas sexualmente por Samuel Klein, como mostraram as

manifestações

 feitas às portas da sede das Casas Bahia depois da reportagem da

Pública

.


É por isso que apesar da crise do varejo desde a chegada do e-commerce e do peso dos altos juros que dificultam toda a economia brasileira (sobre isso, veja a

coluna

 de Clara Saliba), não se pode ver esse caso apenas como financeiro: “A crise financeira tem solução técnica. Renegocia dívida, fecha loja, corta custo, busca comprador. É doloroso, é caro, mas tem caminho. A crise de identidade é outra coisa. Ela acontece quando o que …

author: Christine Ahn
title: Trump Moves to Scale Back US War Drills in Korea. We Should Support That.
content:
While any diplomatic overture from Trump should be viewed with skepticism, we should welcome a chance to advance peace.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

President Donald Trump’s social media post on August 16 calling for a substantial reduction in U.S.-South Korea military exercises triggered panic across partisan lines. Instead of just pointing to the high costs of the exercises and unnecessarily hostile approach towards North Korea, Trump also highlighted his “very good relationship with Kim Jong Un” and chastised South Korea for refusing to join the disastrous U.S.-Israel war on Iran. Attacks came from Republicans, including North Carolina Sen. Thom Tillis, who defended South Korea as “a solid military ally for over 70 years,” but then made the bizarre claim that reducing joint war drills frees up North Korean troops “to support Putin’s” war on Ukraine.

Democrats, naturally, piled on, attacking Trump for undermining yet another major ally to side with an authoritarian leader. Hillary Clinton, the champion of the failed policy of “strategic patience” during the Obama administration, posted: “The president is making US policy friendlier to North Korea and Russia than Canada and Oman. Are you kidding me?”

While any diplomatic overture from this administration should be viewed with skepticism — this is, after all, the same White House that condemned South Korea for declining to join its war against Iran — progressives shouldn’t miss an opportunity to take a principled position that advances peace, a reduced U.S. military footprint, and the security of the American and Korean people.

First and foremost, reducing tensions with North Korea is the right policy. Period. The United States has been at war with North Korea since the Korean War was temporarily halted in 1953 when the United States signed a ceasefire. This has meant that the United States is still technically at war with North Korea, justifying the presence of roughly 28,500 U.S. troops on dozens of U.S. military bases and installations on the Korean Peninsula. To maintain “readiness,” the U.S. and South Korean militaries regularly conduct provocative war drills involving tens of thousands of troops simulating the invasion of North Korea with the use of B-2 nuclear bombers, nuclear-powered aircraft carriers, and submarines. These joint military exercises are a well-known source of tension with North Korea as they have included training for “decapitation” strikes against the leadership, invasions, and preemptive strikes. Far from deterring North Korea, these exercises may do the opposite. Research suggests that these war drills tend to escalate rather than ease tensions, provoking a more threatening security environment instead of the deterrent effect they’re intended to have.

Second, Seoul has been calling for peaceful coexistence with Pyongyang and has abandoned the idea that North Korea would have to give up its nuclear program before dialogue. On July 23, Unification Minister Chung Dong-young announced South Korea’s “peace-first” approach, which aims instead at freezing North Korea’s nuclear program through a three-step process: halt the production of new weapons, reduce the stockpile, and end with dismantlement. South Korean President Lee Jae Myung has a phrase for the fact that North Korea is never going to give up its nuclear weapons: “harsh reality.”

Given this reality, President Lee has been nudging Trump to do exactly this. At the June 2026 G7 summit in Evian, France, a 90-minute dinner conversation between Presidents Trump and Lee produced commitments from both leaders to a peaceful resolution of North Korean issues — notably, without invoking denuclearization.

Seoul, then, is not an ally being blindsided, regardless of Trump’s lashing out about the Iran war. This is an ally that has been asking for exactly this shift, and finally has a U.S. president willing to upend the Washington political-military-industrial complex establishment that views South Korea as its floating aircraft carrier.

That’s where the so-called sacrament of the “alliance” deserves scrutiny. The narrative that Trump is abandoning South Korea obscures a longer, less flattering story about the actual purpose of the U.S. military presence there. author: Randi Beers
title: New docuseries takes viewers on a walrus hunt with Terry Uyarak
content:
Musician Terry Uyarak is set to take viewers across Canada on a walrus hunt.


His life in Igloolik is on display in the first episode of a new six-part APTN docu-series,

 Go North

. Each 60-minute episode explores a different aspect of living north of 60 and highlights Indigenous travel and resilience.


Uyarak takes the show’s crew on a hunt to demonstrate the process of catching, killing and butchering the animal. 


“We are known to be walrus people, so why not do something with walrus,” Uyarak said in an interview, describing how he landed on the decision to focus on the hunt.


“I just want to educate the people that what we are living here is not anything new and we’ve been doing this practice for … we don’t even know how long.”


Uyarak’s walrus hunt is just one example examined in

Go North

 of how Indigenous communities adapt to change while maintaining and protecting traditions. Other episodes focus on how people in the North still use traditional methods of travel like dogsled and kayaking.


“I really want to educate the world that we’re welcoming, wonderful people here,” he said.


The show is narrated by Shina Nova, an Inuk social media personality, singer and activist.


Go North


premiéres Sept. 3 on APTN.

title: Fate of Kurdish woman arrested in Iran remains unknown
content:
The fate of Nazanin Hosseinpour, a 34-year-old Kurdish woman from the village of Shinabad in Piranshahr, remains unknown five days after her arrest by Ministry of Intelligence forces.


The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has learned that Hosseinpour was arrested on 16 August after being summoned to the Ministry of Intelligence office in Piranshahr and was taken to an undisclosed location.


Since her arrest, she has been denied access to a lawyer, family visits and telephone contact with her family.


Despite repeated enquiries by her family about her condition, security and judicial authorities have refused to respond or provide any information.


Hosseinpour is the mother of two young children, and her husband is seriously ill with cancer.

title: „8×5“: Der auch gewerkschaftlich innovative Kampf der Arbeitsmigrant:innen der Textilindustrie in der Toskana
content:
Dossier


„Florenz und Prato gelten als das textile Zentrum von „Made in Italy“: Berühmte und sehr teure Designerlabels lassen hier unter oft menschenunwürdigen Arbeitsbedingungen (v.a. pakistanische und bengalesische) bei Unterauftragnehmern produzieren. Den bislang nicht organisierten kleinen Zulieferern haben sich Gewerkschaften wie Sudd Cobas und CNA Federmoda gewidmet. In den letzten Jahren (ca seit 2001) ist dabei in den italienischen Provinzen Florenz und Prato die Arbeiterbewegung „8×5“ entstanden, die einen Achtstundentag an fünf Tagen in der Woche sowie die Einhaltung von Verträgen und Arbeitsgesetzen fordert. Dank der Streiks und der gewerkschaftlichen Organisierung von unten in vielen ausbeuterischen Fabriken sind die Rechte und ein wenig Gerechtigkeit zurückgekehrt. Trotz der Tatsache, dass alle großen Luxusmarken unglaubliche und wachsende Gewinnmargen haben, ergreifen sie viele Maßnahmen, um der Bewegung und der Erlangung von Rechten durch die Arbeiter in ihren Lieferketten entgegenzuwirken. Siehe die

Kampagne „8×5“ bei Sudd Cobas


 (ital.), unsere 2 Dossiers zu den Beispielen Texprint und Montblanc sowie weitere Informationen dazu:


Solidarität mit den Streikenden von Acca in Prato gegen die „Scheinschließung“ des Logistikunternehmens und die Angriffe gegen die Streikposten


„

Seit dem 19. Juni befinden sich die Beschäftigten von Acca im Streik, nachdem die Schließung des Unternehmens angekündigt wurde – eine Entscheidung, durch die 95 Menschen ihren Arbeitsplatz verlieren würden. Tatsächlich handelt es sich um ein weiteres Beispiel für eine „Scheinschließung“: Textilunternehmen in Prato greifen regelmäßig auf diese Praxis zurück; sie schließen und eröffnen dann unter einem anderen Namen wieder, um nicht alle offenen rechtlichen Angelegenheiten klären zu müssen, darunter alles, was mit den Rechten der Arbeitnehmerinnen und Arbeitnehmer zu tun hat. Prato, in der Nähe von Florenz, ist das größte Textilzentrum Europas; hier wird der Großteil der Billigkleidung hergestellt.


Seit Jahren führen die Gewerkschaften, darunter SUDD COBAS, den Kampf gegen die systematische Ausbeutung an, die in den Unternehmen der Textilbranche herrscht, einschließlich der Logistikunternehmen wie Acca.


So wurden die Arbeitnehmerinnen und Arbeitnehmer von Acca bis 2023 bis zu 12 Stunden am Tag, 7 Tage die Woche ausgebeutet. Dank des Streiks gelang es ihnen, einen Arbeitsvertrag zu erwirken, der den gesetzlichen Vorschriften entspricht. Es handelte sich um einen harten und schwierigen Streik, bei dem es zu mehreren Übergriffen auf die Streikenden mit Eisenstangen vor ihren Wohnhäusern durch vom Arbeitgeber bezahlte Milizen kam. Das Kräfteverhältnis ermöglichte die Durchsetzung von Vereinbarungen, die über den geltenden Tarifvertrag hinausgingen.


Zusätzlich zu den Schulden gegenüber den Arbeitnehmerinnen und Arbeitnehmern ist die Geschäftsführung von Acca Gegenstand zweier Ermittlungen: einer wegen Steuerbetrugs in Höhe von 70 Millionen Euro und einer wegen illegaler Einstellung und Ausbeutung von Arbeitskräften. Deshalb „schließt“ das Unternehmen … um besser wiedereröffnet zu werden und seine sozialen Raubzüge fortzusetzen.


Seit dem 19. Juni stehen Streikposten vor den Toren des Unternehmens. Der Kampf geht weiter. Die Gewalt seitens der Unternehmensleitung und der Polizei hält an: Angriff durch eine aus 150 Personen bestehende Miliz der Unternehmensleitung, Polizeieinsätze gegen die Streikposten… Unterstützen wir die Streikenden!

“ span.

Solidaritätserklärung vom 18. August 2026 von Laboursolidarity

Bitte beachtet

die Streikkasse

„Die Fahnen der Basisgewerkschaft Sudd Cobas sind mit Klebeband am Werkstor befestigt. Ausnahmsweise weht jetzt ein Wind und mildert ein wenig die Hitze am Streikposten. Seit sieben Wochen sind hier die Zelte aufgeschlagen, harren Arbeiter und Gewerkschaftsaktivisten aus und blockieren die Warenströme des Logistikriesen Acca in Prato, um ihre Streikforderungen durchzusetzen. Prato, 20 Kilometer nördlich von Florenz gelegen, war ab dem 19. Jahrhundert ein Zentrum der italienischen Textilindustrie. title: Statue of Salih Muslim to be erected in Sulaymaniyah
content:
As part of efforts to honor the Kurdish people’s struggle, national values, and symbols of resistance across the four parts of Kurdistan, a statue project dedicated to Salih Muslim, a prominent politician and leading figure from Rojava Kurdistan, has been completed in Sulaymaniyah.


The project was carried out by renowned Kurdish sculptor Çêner Nezar with the support and initiative of Dr. Taha Resul, a prominent figure in Sulaymaniyah.


The location where the statue of Salih Muslim will be erected is expected to be determined in the coming days.


“We are one people”


Sculptor Çêner Nezar, speaking about the significance of the statue and the emotions it evoked in him, said that when Dr. Taha Resul approached him with the proposal to create a statue of Salih Muslim, he accepted without hesitation.


Stressing that Salih Muslim deserves every form of respect at the national level, Nezar said: “Salih Muslim is a politician from Rojava Kurdistan. But what matters to me is that, as Kurds, we achieve this cultural and national transformation. As we always say, we are one people. If the Kurdish people remain united, no force can divide us. The Kurds are a people who have struggled for freedom and independence throughout history. Therefore, everyone’s fundamental duty is to serve the Kurdish cause in their own field and to introduce our national identity to the world.”


Regarding the location and installation of the statue, Çêner Nezar said that discussions with Dr. Taha and the relevant parties are ongoing. Efforts are underway to place the statue at a prominent and suitable elevated location in Sulaymaniyah, he added.


“Salih Muslim is a symbol of resistance and Kobanê”


Dr. Taha Resul, a prominent figure in Sulaymaniyah known for his national commitment, highlighted Salih Muslim’s position and role, describing him as a national symbol. Stating that the project is an expression of gratitude for the history of the struggle in Rojava, Taha Resul continued:


“For me, Salih Muslim is a symbol of resistance and Kobanê; he is a hero and a son of difficult times. He carried a weapon, but his mind was always focused on peace and coexistence. Salih Muslim became a source of hope. The mark of his efforts and labor on this people’s struggle can clearly be seen, and he wrote an honorable chapter in history for his people. For this reason, I am very pleased that his statue has been created by the talented sculptor Çêner Nezar and that he will remain forever as a symbol in our history.”


Dr. Taha Resul also emphasized that the Kurds are the people of the Zagros, Taurus and Mesopotamia. Despite all oppression and massacres, the Kurds have continued to stand on their own feet, while the enemies of the Kurds have disappeared, he said, adding that the history of Kurdish resistance will always remain alive.


Salih Muslim


Salih Muslim, a member of the Co-Presidential Council of the Democratic Union Party (PYD), has passed away at the age of 75. 


Salih Muslim Mohammed was born on 3 March 1951, in Kobanê, where patriotic values were strong. He completed his education in Rojava and Syria until high school. He later attended Istanbul Technical University, graduating in 1977. For a period, he went to Saudi Arabia to work. Having strong patriotic feelings, Muslim visited Abdullah Öcalan in 1983. Following the Qamishlo Massacre in 2003, he was arrested and imprisoned for seven months because of a letter he wrote to Bashar al-Assad.


After being released from prison, he joined the newly established Democratic Union Party (PYD) in 2003 and became a member of its executive council. In 2010, he was elected co-chair of the PYD. During those years, he held meetings with officials of the Turkish state to negotiate the future of Syria.


In September 2017, he served as the head of foreign relations for the Movement for a Democratic Society (TEV-DEM). During his time as PYD co-chair and in his role within TEV-DEM, he became an important actor through his work at both national and international levels.


At the 9th congress of the PYD held on March 19, 2022, he was re-elected as PYD co-chair. Two years later, at the 10th congress, he handed over the co-chair position and continued his role as a member of the PYD Co-Chair Council.


Salih Muslim died on March 11, 2026, in Erbil, where he had been receiving treatment for kidney failure.

title: Conversatorio: Endeudados para sobrevivir
content:
En la Argentina de 2026, miles de familias trabajadoras ya no se endeudan para comprar una casa, un auto o una heladera: se endeudan para comer.


El endeudamiento familiar se convirtió en una forma de explotación y disciplinamiento. Tarjetas de crédito, préstamos, financieras y billeteras virtuales aparecen como la salida para llegar a fin de mes, mientras crecen la morosidad y las tasas usurarias.


Frente a esta realidad, proponemos un espacio para reflexionar, conocer herramientas jurídico-políticas y construir estrategias colectivas de lucha contra la usura y el endeudamiento.

Leonardo Elgorriaga, Abogado de FORA y coordinador del Grupo de Estudios de la Asociación de Abogados y Abogadas Laboralistas (AAL).

title: Memorial ceremonies in Amed for 49 martyrs of the Kurdish freedom movement
content:
In the province of Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır), memorial ceremonies have been taking place at six locations since Friday for 49 people who lost their lives at different times and in different places in the Kurdish freedom struggle. The multi-day gatherings are being organized by MEBYA-DER, an association representing families of the martyrs, and are set to conclude with a joint commemoration ceremony.


The main memorial gathering was set up in Koşuyolu Park in the Bağlar district, where relatives of fallen guerrilla fighters, representatives of political parties and civil society organizations, as well as numerous local residents, have gathered since the morning hours. Portraits of the 49 martyrs are displayed on tables alongside carnations. Participants observed a minute of silence in their memory and then sang the march “Çerxa Şoreşê.”


Police attempt to prevent banner from being displayed


During the memorial ceremony, Turkish police attempted to prevent a banner bearing the words “Şehîdên me rûmeta me ne” — “Our martyrs are our dignity” — from being displayed. Those present responded by chanting “Şehîd namirin” [Martyrs are immortal] and “Bijî Serok Apo” [Long Live Leader Öcalan]. Following the protests, the banner was eventually hung at the site. Visits to the main memorial gathering in Bağlar are continuing.


Memorial ceremonies at six locations


In addition to Koşuyolu Park, memorial gatherings were set up in the rural neighborhoods of Kabaxidir and Arvalî in Bağlar district, Kizlal in Silvan district, Pornag in Çınar district, and the Hola neighborhood in Bismil district.


In Pornag, YJA-Star fighter Gülcan Kaya (Raperin Bahoz) is being commemorated. She lost her life in the Gare region of southern Kurdistan on August 25, 2019. Numerous people visited the memorial gathering held for Kaya and offered prayers in her memory.


In Bismil, a memorial gathering is being held for Süleyman Akkalp (Rêber Zagros). Numerous people have also been gathering there since the morning. His portrait is displayed in the memorial tent in the Hola neighborhood, where prayers are offered.


Memorial event to conclude the ceremonies


Ahead of the ceremonies, MEBYA-DER called on the public to attend the memorial gatherings. “We invite all our people to the memorial ceremonies in Koşuyolu Park, Silvan, Bismil, Çınar and the villages of Bağlar,” said co-chair Ramazan Dengiz.


The memorial ceremonies will continue for three days. A commemorative event is scheduled for the final day.

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Israeli Soldiers Mark Palestinian Captives With Numbers
content:
Israeli soldiers in the illegally occupied West Bank marked Palestinian captives with numbers earlier this week, drawing comparisons to the behaviour of Nazis during the Holocaust.


Soldiers used marker pens to write numbers on the foreheads and arms of detainees during a raid in Qabatiya, south of Jenin, on Monday 17 August.


Dozens of Palestinians were

rounded up at around 5am

 and taken to a home that had been turned into a makeshift interrogation centre, where they were bound and questioned for around ten hours while some were beaten.


​“They treated us with extreme brutality,”

 said Ahmad al-Hathnawi

, a detainee who was marked with the number 44, in a video published by Quds News Network. It was the fifth time he had been detained, he said, but the first time soldiers had written a number on him.


There were around 50 detainees in the house, “including blindfolded women”, he added.


Mahmoud Nazzal, who lives in the house where the interrogations happened, said troops stormed his home by breaking down the doors just after dawn prayers, Middle East Eye reported. 


They handcuffed his father and took him outside, while Nazzal was handcuffed and kept indoors.


“I was left lying on the ground unable to move for ten hours while handcuffed. I was also prevented from using the bathroom. I saw someone being beaten as he left the house after his interrogation,” Nazzal said.


Ahmad Tibi, a Palestinian-Israeli lawmaker in the Knesset, condemned the detainees’ treatment on X. “This is what dehumanisation looks like: erasing the person and turning them into a number. An image that recalls dark periods, and should shock every person.”


The Israeli

 military

admitted soldiers

 had marked people with numbers and said “lessons were drawn from the matter” – but this is only the latest of several such incidents. In April, Israeli forces


marked dozens of women

 with numbers at a refugee camp in Jenin, and in 2024 men were marked with numbers


on their foreheads

 in the West Bank town of Dura.


The treatment, especially in the context of the genocide in Gaza, has elicited widespread comparisons to the Holocaust, during which


Nazis wrote serial numbers

 in indelible ink on detainees at concentration camps.


Israeli soldiers and violent settlers have significantly ramped up their attacks against Palestinian in the West Bank in recent years, killing at least 1,185 and


detaining over 24,000

 since October 2023.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Luego de 18 años, detuvieron en Posadas a 16 policías por la desaparición de Mario Fabián Golemba
content:
A pedido de la titular de la Fiscalía Federal 2 de Posadas, Silvina Gutiérrez, y por orden de la jueza María Verónica Skanata, 16 efectivos de la Policía de Misiones, algunos en actividad y otros retirados, fueron detenidos el pasado lunes 10 de agosto en el marco de la investigación por la desaparición forzada de Mario Fabián Golemba, ocurrida en marzo de 2008. “Hubo un pacto de silencio institucional”, afirmó la fiscalía federal.


La fiscalía les atribuye distintos grados de participación en la privación ilegítima de la libertad de Golemba, su permanencia bajo una custodia estatal clandestina y las maniobras posteriores destinadas a ocultar lo ocurrido. En ese marco, sostiene que los hechos formaron parte de un plan común en el que los imputados habrían realizado aportes funcionales cada uno desde su respectivo rol. “Se configuró una maniobra coordinada entre policías para encubrir la desaparición mediante falsas hipótesis, omisiones en registros oficiales, versiones uniformes y contradicciones entre las actuaciones judiciales y administrativas”, informó el sitio del Ministerio Público Fiscal que señaló la fiscalía federal.


El 27 de marzo de 2008 Mario Golemba, de 27 años, salió de su casa, recorrió los diez kilómetros del camino de tierra roja hasta la ruta 14 para ir a Oberá a una consulta médica con una nutricionista. Le mandó un mensaje de texto a su novia para decirle que tenía que esperar los resultados de unos estudios, que volvería ya de noche, pero nunca regresó. Dos días después su familia denunció su desaparición. La investigación judicial recayó en el Juzgado de Instrucción 1 de Oberá, a cargo de la jueza Alba Kunnzman de Gauchat, que impidió el acceso a la causa a la abogada de la familia.


Como es habitual en estos casos circularon varias hipótesis, sin respaldo en el expediente, que sugerían que Mario podría haber salido del país por voluntad propia. Todas fueron descartadas. Tres presos aseguraron que Mario entró esposado a la comisaría de Dos de Mayo, le dieron una paliza y se lo llevaron en un patrullero. Habría sido torturado para que reconociera que él era otra persona a la que estaban buscando. Sin embargo, la jueza jamás realizó un careo entre los testigos y la causa no tuvo ningún avance significativo.


A la fecha continúa sin conocerse el paradero de Mario y tampoco fueron hallados sus restos. “Necesitamos saber la verdad, la Justicia debe esclarecer el caso porque no puede haber democracia con desaparecidos”, afirmó su hermano Eliezer Golemba.


Tras un largo periodo de inactividad, testigos de identidad reservada declararon ante la justicia provincial y federal que Golemba estuvo detenido en la comisaría de Dos de Mayo, dependiente de la Policía de la provincia de Misiones donde habría sido golpeado, tal como habían asegurado los tres detenidos a los pocos días de la desaparición sin que los funcionarios judiciales a cargo de la causa siguieran esa línea de investigación.


En junio de 2021, a partir de un planteo de la querella que representa a los familiares de Golemba, el expediente pasó a la justicia federal de Posadas, que inició una investigación por el delito de desaparición forzada de persona.


La causa cuenta con la intervención del Centro de reunión de información Misiones (CRIMIS) de la Gendarmería Nacional Argentina, y en la investigación también colaboraron la Procuraduría de Violencia Institucional (PROCUVIN) y la Dirección General de Acompañamiento, Orientación y Protección a las Víctimas (DOVIC) del Ministerio Público Fiscal de la Nación.


Los procedimientos de detención de los 16 policías fueron realizados por la Gendarmería Nacional Argentina en distintos puntos de la provincia de Misiones. Hay una persona que permanece prófuga y tiene pedido de captura.


Entre los imputados se encuentran el comisario retirado Evaldo Katz, los oficiales de guardia Edgardo Andrés Arce y Liliana Margarita Saft, el jefe de guardia retirado Carmelo Alberto Cerdán Cruz, el secretario José Roberto Pereyra Da Silva, el chofer de turno Alejandro Alfonso González Samudio, Wiliams Gabriel Lunge (cumple funciones en Seguridad Vial), los guardias Maximiliano Gabriel Gutiérrez, Ramón Aníbal Cardozo, Mario Francisco Villar y Diego Armando Amarilla, los radioperadores Alfredo Lorenzo Ortiz y Cristian Andrés Silva (retirado), Baldemar Parra, Juan Ramón Ferreyra (retirado), Ofelia Gladys Ziller y Eduardo Pellizer (retirado).

title: Yeni Parti Grup Başkan Vekili Günaydın: “Üye sayımız 300 bini aştı”
content:
Yeni Parti Grup Başkan Vekili Gökhan Günaydın, Yeni Parti Tokat İl Başkanı Çağdaş Kurtgöz ve parti üyeleriyle bir araya geldi. Günaydın, partisinin örgütlenme düzeyine ilişkin açıklama yaptı.

Yeni Parti’nin bir hafta içerisinde 65 ilde örgütlendiği bilgisini paylaşan Günaydın, “Kısa süre içerisinde 81 ilin tamamında yapılanmamızı tamamlayacağız. Bürokratik engellere ve hız eksikliklerine rağmen üye sayımız an itibarıyla 300 bini aşmıştır. Hedefimiz çok kısa sürede 1 milyon üyeye ulaşmaktır” ifadelerini kullandı.

Partiye yapılan bağışlar hakkında bilgi veren Günaydın, “Bize 'Paranız, binanız yok' dediler. Başlattığımız bağış kampanyasında toplanan miktar 411 milyon lirayı aştı. MHP'ye verilen devlet hazine yardımı 600 milyon lirayken, vatandaş bir ayda bize 411 milyon lira emanet etti” dedi.

Günaydın, bugün itibariyle 236 belediye başkanının Yeni Parti'ye geçiş yaptığını belirtti.

Erken seçim ihtimali ya da 2028 Mayıs ayındaki genel seçimler için parti olarak hazırlıklarını sürdürdüklerini vurgulayan Günaydın, "Seçimlere girebilmek için kurultayımızı ekim ayında yapmamız gerekiyor. 12 Eylül'de ilçelerde, 18 Ekim'de ise illerde üye bazında seçimlerimizi gerçekleştireceğiz. Genel başkanımızı da aynı şekilde üye bazında seçeceğiz” şeklinde konuştu.
