title: Hatimoğulları visits prisoners in Silivri Prison
content:
Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) Co-Chair Tülay Hatimoğulları visited prisoners in Silivri Prison. Hatimoğulları made the following statement after the visit:


“Today, we are addressing the entire public in Turkey from Silivri Prison. We have just met with our imprisoned friends. We met with Socialist Party of the Oppressed (ESP) Co-Chair Murat Çepni, former Peoples’ Democratic Party (HDP) municipal co-mayor Bekir Kaya, and political prisoner Nasrullah Kuran. We held the meeting together with our Bitlis MP Hüseyin Olan. Of course, we mutually assessed the process during this meeting. We discussed both the recently adopted framework law and what political openings, what expected democratic openings, will follow this framework law in Turkey.


 


I would like to begin by recalling the major operation against our component, the ESP, on 3 February, which resulted in detentions and arrests. On the 200th day since this operation, we once again reiterate our call from here for the release of our ESP comrades. Detention orders were issued for 110 people in the operation against the ESP, and 84 socialists were arrested at the time. Forty-eight of our friends, including ESP Co-Chair and former HDP MP Murat Çepni, remain imprisoned. ESP Deputy Co-Chair Sezin Uçar, DEM Party Women’s Coordination member Fatma Çelik and Limter-İş President İleri Devrim Yurtsever have also been imprisoned for exactly 200 days.


Why were ESP members, socialists, revolutionaries and patriots detained? Why were they arrested? Prisons in Turkey today are overflowing with political prisoners simply for exercising freedom of thought and expression and the right to democratic action. Why? Because they want a fair and democratic order in Turkey. Because they demand an end to violence against women and femicides in Turkey. They are now in prison because they defend the rights of workers, labourers, the poor, farmers and tradespeople against rising unemployment and poverty in Turkey. They are in prison because they stood alongside people searching for their disappeared relatives and showed solidarity with Emine Ocak and others like her. They are in prison because they opposed the 10 October Ankara Train Station Massacre, when the doves of peace and democracy were massacred. They are in prison because they defended the right to life. ESP and Socialist Refoundation Party (SYKP) youth who wanted to take toys to children in Kobanê were subjected to the brutality and violence of ISIS in Suruç, where we experienced a major massacre. We lost many of our comrades there. Today, revolutionaries and socialists in Turkey are in prison because they defended the right to life against the massacres carried out by ISIS, those bloodstained murderers. Look at what is in the case file of ESP Deputy Chair Uğur Ok. They are being prosecuted because they said, ‘The Kurdish question must be resolved through a just and democratic peace,’ and because they established the ‘Tribune of the Oppressed’ in connection with this.


There are very important developments in Turkey today. On 10 August, a framework law was adopted with the support of a large majority in Parliament. We regard the framework law as a first step against the approach that has confined the Kurdish question within the framework of ‘terrorism’, against 50 years of war and conflict in this country and the unresolved Kurdish question. Today, we are talking about peace. Today, while negotiating for peace, we are also struggling for it. At every opportunity, we stress that while negotiating for the Kurdish question to be resolved through peaceful and democratic means in these lands, the struggle for democracy must also be strengthened across the broadest possible spectrum. Because we know that the adoption of this law alone will not democratize Turkey, but it can open the way wide for democratization. That is why we value this law and consider it important.


At a time when this law has been adopted and the dialogue process is continuing, Figen Yüksekdağ, Selahattin Demirtaş and our Central Executive Board members from that period are still in prison because of the Kobanê Case. We happened to see them in the prison just a short while ago and exchanged greetings. Osman Kavala, Can Atalay, Çiğdem Mater and Tayfun Kahraman are still imprisoned here in Silivri behind us. Once again, we want to convey this message to the government, the state and the entire public in Turkey: At a time when the peace and …

author: Brian Hioe
title: What Do Comments by Malaysia’s Prime Minister Mean for Taiwan?
content:
MALAYSIAN PRIME MINISTER Anwar Ibrahim has stoked controversy after comments read as not only reinforcing a view of Taiwan as part of China, but also expressing support for China retaking Taiwan by force if necessary.

In particular, during an interview with Al-Jazeera, Ibrahim stated, “I see Taiwan as part of China, period. You may disagree with [that] there are some excesses. Yes, express your view, but it must be in the context. It is one China. It is accepted by all.”

Ibrahim next went on to suggest how he might act if in a similar situation. He stated that if in the same situation as prime minister of Malaysia, “If one province decides to break away, do we use force? I think I will protect the sanctity and unity of the nation.” In the same interview, Anwar defends China, claiming that concerns about Chinese aggression are ramped up by western concerns.

Subsequent comments saw Ibrahim refuse to retract the comments, unusually highlighting the US Civil War to suggest how the US has historically acted under similar circumstances–though, of course, one notes that the US previously fought a war of independence from Great Britain. Still, Ibrahim later stated, “Of course, we respect China’s position, but a peaceful path is best. That is what is being pursued now.”

Malaysia has historically maintained a One China Policy since 1974 that acknowledged but did not recognize the Chinese position on Taiwan. Yet more recent statements by Malaysia have suggested that Malaysia now not only acknowledges, but recognizes China’s position, as seen in statements in 2004, 2024, and 2025. Some have interpreted Ibrahim’s comments as suggesting that Malaysia has now shifted away from the One China Policy toward a direct recognition of China’s One China Principle.

Taiwan has hit back at the comments, denying that Taiwan is a province of China. Though not likely a short-term response, Ibrahim’s comments may, in the long term, affect Malaysia’s efforts to become an AI powerhouse if they dissuade Taiwanese semiconductor companies from setting up facilities in Malaysia. Certainly, the Taiwanese government may use semiconductors as a point of leverage over Malaysia, as it did when South Africa previously tried to force Taiwan to move its representative office out of the capital of Pretoria in a move that was also perceived as pleasing China.

What should be concerning for Taiwan, however, is that Ibrahim’s statements reflect a trend of ASEAN leaders pivoting to China. One has seen signs of Indonesia possibly pivoting toward China under the presidential administration of Prabowo Subianto, with a recent joint naval exercise held between the Indonesian navy and People’s Liberation Army Navy in waters east of Taiwan.

The Indonesian government has denied that the exercises were meant for anything apart from routine, peaceful practice of maritime coordination; it is possible that the Prabowo administration intends to build closer ties with China. So, too, likely with Malaysia.

What the Prabowo administration or Ibrahim administration would share, of course, is that they are far-right-wing political administrations with authoritarian tendencies. It may not surprise that they would seek to align with China, if only out of frustration from criticisms on human rights grounds from Western countries.

While Taiwan may have a far different record on human rights and democracy than such countries, Taiwan does stand to lose trading partners through such realignments. Taiwan has, after all, in past years sought to strengthen economic ties with Southeast Asian countries in order to diversify investments away from overreliance on the Chinese market.

Still, it proves ironic when the Prabowo and Ibrahim governments are sometimes seen as Islamist governments. China, after all, imprisons Muslim-majority Uyghurs en masse in what it claims to be “reeducation camps” because of their religion. Yet if the governments of both countries have been accused in the past of fanning up Islamist sentiment in such a manner that targets minorities, perhaps then they do have commonalities and shared values with the Chinese government.

title: Mine workers’ protest enters its 12th day
content:
Workers from Doruk Mining and Elazığ Eti Gümüş, companies affiliated with Yıldızlar SSS Holding, are continuing their protest in front of the Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources on its 12th day, demanding unpaid wages and compensation, under the leadership of the Independent Mine Workers’ Union.


On Thursday night, almost 100 miners were taken into custody. They were released this morning and said they will go to the Ministry of Energy and Natural Resource. 


Speaking at the press statement held in front of the ministry on Thursday, Başaran Aksu, an organizing specialist with the Independent Mine Workers’ Union, said: “We will not leave here; we will wait. The result may be another detention, so be it. We are trying to meet with the deputy minister, but there is a wall in front of us.” He added: “When the Interior Minister spoke by phone with Union General President Gökay Çakır, he said that he was ‘under pressure to resolve the problem.’ The deputy energy minister had thanked us before; now, for 11 days, he has been avoiding meeting with us.” Aksu was one of the miners taken into custody.


Murat Çelik, a worker at Elazığ Eti Gümüş, reacted to the fact that they had been detained five times since arriving on August 10 to demand all their employment rights. He said: “I am married and the father of four children. Three of my children have to go to the hospital, and I cannot send them money. Am I the heartless one, or is it Sebahattin Yıldız, or the Ankara Police Chief? I am calling out to those who are treating us heartlessly: our children are in a terrible situation. One of our friends who is resisting here has a son whose wedding he could not attend; another friend’s wife is pregnant and he cannot take care of her. We have friends here whose children are sick. They need to take care of their children, but those children see on the news that their fathers have been detained. Have you ever questioned Sebahattin Yıldız?”

title: Majid Maleki Meighani: Social power in Middle East must be democratized - Part One
content:
Majid Maleki Meighani is an Iranian writer, political analyst, translator, and photographer whose work explores the relationship between capitalism, imperialism, class, and political power. Writing from a critical Marxist perspective, he is particularly interested in the political and social dynamics of Iran, West Asia, and the wider Global South, with a focus on societies located within the periphery and semi-periphery of the world-system. His writing brings together political economy, geopolitics, and the experiences of ordinary people and social movements, shaped in part by years of travel and direct engagement with communities across Iran, Turkey, Iraq, and Syria. His own experience of political imprisonment in Iran has also informed his understanding of state power, repression, resistance, and the possibilities of political transformation. He has translated Walter LaFeber’s 

Inevitable Revolutions: The United States in Central America

 and 

Voices of the Arab Spring

 into Persian. His writings have appeared in ZNetwork, Akhbar-e Rooz, Tribune Zamane, and other independent publications.


Majid Maleki Meighani, who analyzes developments in the Middle East, emphasizes that events in the region need to be examined on three levels: the global political economy, geopolitical competition between states, and social struggles within individual countries. Meighani notes that, in the Middle East’s current landscape, states occupy different positions within the hierarchy of the world system, and that each is part of a global capitalist order built on inequalities. For this reason, he points out that understanding the conflict-ridden and crisis-stricken processes in the Middle East requires examining who controls capital accumulation, trade, technology, security mechanisms, energy corridors and political decision-making processes. Drawing on his experience as a political prisoner in Iran, Meighani highlights the power of the state, repression, resistance and the possibilities for political transformation. In our interview, in which he discusses the uprisings that have developed across the region stretching from Morocco to Pakistan, the consequences of the Arab Spring, the competitive multipolar dynamics among actors such as Iran, Turkey, Israel and Saudi Arabia, as well as the Abraham Accords and the Mecca Pact, he points to the democratization of social power as the central issue.


The writer argues that a transformation must take place by transferring part of the power concentrated in states, armies, major concentrations of capital and geopolitical networks to organized society. Otherwise, he says, even if the wars come to an end, this will not mean that the crisis in the Middle East has ended; rather, the form of the war will simply change.


The Middle East, stretching from Morocco to Pakistan, is at the center of wars, crises, and conflicts. Can this situation be explained simply through the plunder of resources?


In my view, no. Reducing the crisis of the Middle East to the plunder of resources explains part of the reality, but it is not sufficient to understand the structure of the region. Oil, gas, trade routes, ports, water, and other natural resources are undoubtedly important, but the problem goes deeper than the direct appropriation of resources. What we are witnessing in the Middle East is part of an unequal global capitalist system in which states occupy different positions within the hierarchy of the world-system.


The Middle East has to be understood simultaneously at three levels: the global political economy, geopolitical competition among states, and social struggles within individual countries. If we look only at geopolitics, people become spectators while regional and global powers compete over them. If we look only at economics, we lose sight of the role of the state, ideology, religion, nationalism, and history. And if we look only at domestic politics, we overlook its relationship with the global structure of power.


In this sense, the central question in the Middle East is not simply, “Who controls the oil?” It is also: Who controls the processes of capital accumulation, trade, technology, security, energy corridors, and political decision-making?


The United Arab Emirates is an interesting example. It is a small country that has acquired influence far beyond its demographic weight through capital, ports, financial networks, technology, relations with major powers, and military projection …

title: İşkenceye uğrayan mahpus, suç duyurusunda bulundu
content:
Van F Tipi Yüksek Güvenlikli Cezaevinde tutulan Nevzat Öner, 11 Ağustos'ta gittiği Van Yüzüncü Yıl Dursun Odabaş Tıp Merkezi'nde kelepçeli muayeneyi kabul etmediği gerekçesiyle görevli askerler tarafından darbedilerek işkenceye maruz bırakıldı. İşkence, Öner'in haftalık telefon görüşmesinde durumu ailesine aktarmasıyla ortaya çıktı. Yaşadığı sağlık problemi sebebiyle gittiği hastanede jandarma tarafından kelepçeli muayene dayatmasına maruz kaldığını aktaran Öner, dayatmaya karşı çıktığı için hastaneden ring aracına oradan da cezaevine getirilene kadar işkenceye maruz bırakıldığını aktardı.

Mezopotamya Ajansı'ndan Ceylan Şahinli'nin haberine göre, cezaevinde görüşmeye giden avukatların edindikleri bilgilere göre Öner, hekimin kelepçelerin çıkarılması yönünde aksi bir talebi bulunmamasına rağmen, görevli jandarma personeli tarafından "Kelepçeli muayene olacaksın" denilerek muayene olmaya zorlandı. Öner’in kelepçeli tedaviyi reddetmesi üzerine hastane koridorunda darbedilmeye başlandığı belirtildi. Bindirildiği ring aracında yetersiz hava şartlarına ve taleplerine rağmen kapıları açılmayan Öner, götürüldüğü cezaevinde idarenin darp izlerini fark etmesi üzerine mahpusu o halde içeri almayı reddetti. Öner, cezaevine götürülmeden yeniden hastaneye götürülerek darp raporu aldı. Öner’in uğradığı darp ve işkence, sevk edildiği hastaneden alınan sağlık raporuyla da belgelendi. Öner uygulanan işkenceye dair suç duyurusunda bulundu.

Eşini ayda sadece 2 kez görebildiklerini ve ayda sadece 2 haftada bir yapabildikleri telefon görüşmesiyle sesini duyabildiklerini belirten Adalet Öner, "O gün de bizi telefonla aradı. Hastaneye götürüldüğü günü anlattı. Eşim, 'Kelepçeli tedaviyi kabul etmeyince, onu kelepçeyle sürükleyerek elini kanatıyorlar. Eşimin durumundan telefonda haberdar olduk. Eşim 7 yıldır cezaevinde. Bizle, avukatla görüş hakları kısıtlı" dedi.

Cezaevinde yaşanan işkencenin ardından ailenin başvurusu üzerine cezaevine gittiklerini ifade eden Özgürlük İçin Hukukçular Derneği (ÖHD) Van Şube üyesi Murat Özçiçek, Öner'in düşme sonucu kolunun ezilmesi üzerine revir doktorunun hastaneye sevki yaptığını aktardı. Özçiçek, jandarmanın muayene olması gereken Öner ile birlikte odaya girdiğini ve kelepçeli muayeneyi dayattığını belirterek, "Jandarma, Öner'e kelepçe ile muayene olacağını başka türlü izin vermeyeceklerini söylemiş ve onu zorlamış. Nevzat, bunu kabul etmeyince darbedip ring aracına götürmüşler. Darp sırasında Nevzat'ın kol, bilek ve ellerinde sıyrık ve çizikler oluşmuş. Özellikle kelepçe bileklerinde yaralanmalara sebep olmuş. Bunun yanı sıra vücudunun başkaca bölgelerinde de darp izleri mevcut. Nevzat, ringe bindirildiğinde astım hastası olduğunu ve içerinin havasız olduğunu jandarmaya söylemiş. Buna rağmen uzun bir süre ring aracında kapılar kapalı bir şekilde bekletilip cezaevine geri götürülmüş" dedi.

Cezaevi girişinde haber verilen cezaevi müdürünün, Öner'in darbedildiğini fark etmesi üzerine "Onu bu halde cezaevine almam" diyerek hastaneye geri gönderdiğini söyleyen Özçiçek, Öner'in geri gönderildiği hastanede darp raporu aldığını aktardı. Görüştükleri cezaevi müdürünün durumdan haberdar olmadığını aktaran Özçiçek, "Mahpuslara dönük kelepçeli muayene dayatmaları devam ediyor. Bu uygulama, insanlık onuruna aykırı ve mahpusların sağlık hakkına erişimleri üzerinde en büyük engeldir. Hemen hemen tüm hapishanelerden bu yönlü şikayetler almaktayız. Birçok mahpus hastalığı ne kadar ağır olursa olsun bu uygulama sebebiyle tedavi olmadan dönüyor. Bu uygulamalar işkenceye varmış durumda. Defalarca kez bu yönlü şikayetlerde bulunduk. Fakat ne bakanlığın ne de başkaca bir kurum veya kişinin bu duruma yönelik bir çalışması olmadı" diye konuştu.

Kelepçeli muayene dayatmasının insan hakkı ihlali olduğunun altını çizen Van-Hakkari Tabip Odası ve Türkiye İnsan Hakları Vakfı (TİHV) Van Temsilcisi Hüseyin Yaviç, tabip odasına kelepçeli muayene dayatmasına dair çok sayıda suç duyurusu geldiğini kaydetti. Yaviç, uzun yıllardır buna karşı mücadele verdiklerini ancak yeniden aynı hak ihlalini protesto etmek zorunda kaldıklarını söyledi. Yaviç, "Sağlık hakkı ihlali kabul edilir bir durum değil. Kelepçeli muayene, ağız içi dayatması gibi durumlar insan onurunu zedeleyen ve mahpusların sağlık haklarını ellerinden alan uygulamalardır. Uluslararası sözleşmelerde güvence altına alınan sağlık hakkı, sağlık kurumlarında mahpusların tedavi süreçlerini engelleyen bu uygulamalarla engelleniyor. Bu durum kabul edilemez. title: Nijerya'da çiftçi ve işçileri taşıyan tekne alabora oldu: 52 kişi yaşamını yitirdi
content:
Nijerya'nın kuzeybatısındaki Sokoto eyaletinde çiftçi ve işçilerin bulunduğu teknenin alabora olması sonucu 52 kişi hayatını kaybetti.

Nijerya Ulusal Acil Durum Yönetim Ajansının (NEMA) Sokoto Operasyon Başkanı Tukur Abubakar, bu sabah itibarıyla kazada 52 kişinin öldüğünü açıkladı.

Abubakar, ölenler arasında aynı aileden 11 kişinin de bulunduğunu belirtti.

Kaza, perşembe günü Sokoto eyaletine bağlı Goronyo bölgesindeki Gorau kasabasında meydana geldi. Yaklaşık 70 kişiyi taşıyan tekne, çiftçi ve işçilerin pirinç tarlalarına gitmek için su yolundan geçtiği sırada alabora oldu.

Sokoto Eyalet Meclisi Üyesi Nasiru Adamu, yaptığı açıklamada 40'tan fazla kişinin öldüğünü, ekiplerin 16 kişiyi kurtardığını ve teknedeki yolcuların çoğunun 10 ila 15 yaşlarındaki çocuklardan oluştuğunu söylemişti.

Nijerya'da aşırı yolcu taşınması, teknelerin bakımsızlığı ve güvenlik kurallarına yeterince uyulmaması nedeniyle özellikle yağışlı mevsimde tekne kazaları sık yaşanıyor.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: The reality of change and transformation
content:
The bill widely referred to as the “Framework Law” was passed by parliament on the night of 10 August, shifting attention to the practical steps that will follow and to the political forces responsible for taking them. The law itself is intended to open the way for politics and place responsibilities on political institutions. This means that all political institutions now face the task of correctly understanding these duties and responsibilities and undergoing the change and transformation necessary to fulfil them.


The parties concerned are well aware that the Peace and Democratic Society Process is not based on an agreement or a give-and-take arrangement, but is instead the product of a profound transformation in mentality and political approach. The parties are taking steps required by the changes they have made in their understanding and methods. Those that have undergone a fundamental transformation in their approach and methods are therefore taking more determined and effective steps, while those that struggle with such change and remain weak in this respect appear to be doing little more than taking certain steps out of necessity.


Abdullah Öcalan, who is well aware of this reality, defines change and transformation as the first truth in the Manifesto for a Democratic Communal Society, in which he sets out the theoretical foundations and framework of the Peace and Democratic Society Process. He regards dialectical materialism’s definition of change alone as truth as incomplete. Öcalan argues that change by itself has no direction and that its outcome cannot be known in advance, whereas considering change together with transformation means moving towards something new. On this basis, he argues that dialectics should be understood not merely through its destructive dimension, but above all through its constructive dimension.


The Peace and Democratic Society Process was developed not only as a result of the pressures and requirements created by political and military developments, but also as the outcome of such a transformation in mentality and political approach. Despite all the difficulties and obstacles, the successful completion of the first stage of the process and the step towards the second stage taken with the Framework Law adopted on the night of 10 August were essentially made possible by this change and transformation in political thinking. Almost everyone who has reflected on and debated the process recognizes this reality and acknowledges that Abdullah Öcalan was the driving force behind it. 


The practical steps required for the second stage must now be taken one after another. Indeed, there is already widespread debate over what these steps will or should entail. The Kurdish side and consistent democratic circles do not consider the law sufficient and have voiced criticism. They argue, for example, that as a foundational law, it should explicitly provide the basis for further legislation on freedom and democracy aimed at democratizing Turkey and resolving the Kurdish question. They also stress that the status of Abdullah Öcalan, the architect of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, should be clearly defined, including conditions in which he can live and work freely. Criticism and proposals have also been put forward regarding the language and structure of the law.


The law passed parliament with a record number of votes and, with the exception of some racist-fascist circles and certain social-nationalist groups, its historic significance and importance have been openly acknowledged and supported. This places a responsibility on political institutions, both government and opposition, right and left, to take new and creative practical steps. For this to happen, politics itself must undergo a profound and multidimensional transformation in both mentality and approach. The need for a new democratic breakthrough in politics has therefore become more urgent than ever.


The first significant development in this context was the split within the Republican People’s Party (CHP) and the establishment of a new party under the name YENİ Party. Led by Özgür Özel, YENİ Party has to some extent maintained the enthusiasm it generated within the CHP. However, its approach to the Framework Law has raised serious doubts about whether it can become the kind of social democratic party required by the new process. Social-nationalist influences appear to be placing pressure on YENİ Party, while it has yet …

title: CItizens in Mazıdağı block construction machinery brought in for solar power plant
content:
Residents continue to oppose a Solar Power Plant (GES) project planned on pastureland in the rural Girêsor neighborhood of Şemrex (Mazıdağı) district in Mêrdîn. Construction machinery was brought back to the area today to begin work as part of the project.


Villagers opposed to the GES project blocked the machinery from entering the construction site. The machinery was halted following the villagers’ intervention, while gendarmerie units were also dispatched to the area. Villagers, who make their living from livestock farming, gathered in the area to oppose the opening of the pastureland they use to the GES project. As the machinery and gendarmerie continue to wait in the area, the villagers have said they will not allow work to begin and are continuing their vigil at the site.

author: Tom Midlane
title: Israel Is Trying to Game ChatGPT Results About Gaza and the IDF
content:
Israel is planting sanitised PR stories online in an apparent attempt to influence how ChatGPT and other LLMs answer questions about the genocide in Gaza, the IDF and Zionism. 


More than 100 anonymous articles on Israel and Palestine were posted online within a week earlier this month by a new think tank connected to the Israeli government’s favoured PR firm in the US.


The articles are framed as questions that might be asked of a search engine or LLM, such as ‘

Who Is the Aggressor in the Israel-Palestine Conflict?

’

 and ‘

Does Hamas Account for Deaths Caused by Hamas Itself?

’ 


The ‘data reports’ appeared on the website of the Hanover Institute for Public Policy, a body created by a boutique ad agency called Piro as part of its work for Havas Media, the French PR company that handles most of Israel’s foreign influence work in the US,

Politico reports

.


Other LLM-friendly articles published on the Hanover website are titled ‘

Is There a Policy of Starvation in Gaza?

’ and ‘

Is the IDF the World’s Most Moral Army?’

 None of the AI-optimised articles have bylines, and no researchers are named on the website.


In public US records filed in August, the articles were described as being part of a $100,000 campaign aimed at “the creation and dissemination of factual, source-supported informational materials intended to educate the US public regarding Israel”.


Piro co-founder Daniel Rosenberg confirmed to Politico that his ad agency was retained by the Israeli state “to put accurate, sourced facts into the public record and to counter misinformation about Israel with verifiable information.” Havas Media and the Hanover Institute did not respond to Politico’s request for comment.


According to tests run by Piro, LLMs including ChatGPT were found to be drawing on articles published by the Hanover Institute when responding to questions about Gaza, the IDF, anti-Zionism and antisemitism. 


When Novara Media ran similar tests on ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity, none used Hanover as a source when asked similar questions. However, reporters at the

Jerusalem Post

 found that Perplexity, an AI aggregator, did rely heavily on Hanover when asked ‘Is the IDF the most moral army?’

title: Japonya'da oyun salonunu yakarak 5 kişiyi öldüren fail idam edildi
content:
Fotoğraf: Christopher Politano/Unsplash

Japonya’da 2009 yılında Osaka kentindeki bir oyun salonunu ateşe vererek 5 kişinin ölümüne neden olan Sunao Takami’nin idam edildiği bildirildi.

Japonya Adalet Bakanı Hiroshi Hiraguchi, 58 yaşındaki Takami’nin ölüm cezasının infaz edildiğini açıkladı. Böylece ülkede geçen yıl haziran ayından bu yana ilk kez bir mahkumun idam cezası uygulanmış oldu.

Takami’nin infazı, Başbakan Sanae Takaichi’nin görev döneminde gerçekleştirilen ilk idam olarak da kayıtlara geçti.

Takami, 2009 yılında Osaka’daki bir oyun salonunun zeminine benzin dökerek yangın çıkarmıştı. Yangında biri oyun salonu çalışanı, 4’ü müşteri olmak üzere toplam 5 kişi yaşamını yitirmiş, 10 kişi de yaralanmıştı.

Olayın ardından yakalanan Takami hakkında cinayet ve kundaklama suçlarından dava açıldı.

Yargılama sırasında Takami’nin olay sırasında akıl sağlığının yerinde olmadığı yönündeki savunma mahkeme tarafından kabul edilmedi.

Mahkeme, 2011 yılında Takami hakkında ölüm cezası verdi. Karara yapılan temyiz başvurusunun Japonya Yüksek Mahkemesi tarafından reddedilmesinin ardından ölüm cezası 2016 yılında kesinleşti.

Japonya, idam cezasını uygulamaya devam eden sınırlı sayıdaki gelişmiş ülkeler arasında bulunuyor. Takami’nin infazıyla ülkede geçen yıl haziran ayından bu yana ilk kez bir ölüm cezası uygulanmış oldu.

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: Right(s) Up: Spy-tagging as deflection tactic
content:
Photo by Raymun B. Villanueva/Kodao Productions

Context: The National Task Force to End Local Communist Armed Conflict (NTF-ELCAC) submits cases of “spy-tagging” to the United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (UN-OHCHR) despite their bloody credibility on red-tagging and human rights violations

Human rights: Civil and political rights, international humanitarian law

Rights-holder: Public, human rights defenders, civil society

Duty-bearer: Armed Forces of the Philippines, Administration of Ferdinand Marcos Jr., United Nations

MANILA – The term “spy-tagging” is a deflection tactic, according to Amnesty International Philippines, as it is being used by the NTF-ELCAC to shift the accusation of human rights violations to non-state actors.

The statement came after the NTF-ELCAC published a post, with a photo showing UN Senior Adviser for Human Rights Signe Poulsen receiving a document from an NTF-ELCAC representative.

Cristina Palabay, secretary general of human rights group Karapatan, said that the recent post of the NTF-ELCAC is an act of “desperation for legitimacy when there is none at all.”

“International human rights mechanisms including UN Special Procedures, treaty bodies and the OHCHR itself have either questioned or called for the NTF-ELCAC’s abolition – a major indication that its existence is most unwanted,” Palabay said.

United Nations Special Rapporteurs Irene Khan and Ian Fry previously supported the call for the NTF-ELCAC’s abolition.

National Union of Peoples’ Lawyers President Ephraim Cortez said in a Facebook post that it was “misrepresented as proof of an alleged agreement for collaborative work.”

“Any collaborative work with a red-tagger like NTF-ELCAC will violate [UN] OHCHR’s very reason for existence. Its mandate is to promote and protect human rights by monitoring violations and assisting the government to strengthen its capacity to uphold international human rights standards,” Cortez said.

The UN OHCHR coordinates human rights activities throughout the United Nations System and acts as the secretariat of the Human Rights Council in Geneva, Switzerland. Its mandate includes assisting governments in fulfilling their human rights obligations, as well as providing assistance for the implementation of the international human rights laws.

Amnesty International Philippines reminded the NTF-ELCAC that under international law, the government is responsible for human rights violations committed, not only by its own state actors but also by non-state actors.

For the Commission on Human Rights, the two types of human rights violations are commission which refers to the violations perpetrated by state actors and omission which refers to the government’s failure to address violations committed by non-state actors.

“Government forces, led by NTF-ELCAC and recently DND Secretary Gilbert Teodoro, accuse communities of supporting rebel insurgency, a blatant practice of red-tagging which President Marcos, Jr. continues to condone,” said Ritz Lee Santos III, section director of Amnesty International Philippines, in a statement. He said that red-tagging has already resulted in deaths and destruction for the marginalized.

Under the Marcos Jr. administration, Karapatan documented 137 extrajudicial killings related to the government’s counterinsurgency program, 85 frustrated extrajudicial killings, 16 enforced disappearances, and 53 torture cases. There were hundreds more illegally arrested and searched.

Red-tagging has also been declared a threat to the right to life, liberty, and security, based on a Supreme Court decision in 2024.

“Their failure to take reasonable steps to prevent or respond to abuses committed by non-state actors is in itself a human rights violation. But framing criticisms of the government as communist propaganda while publicly tagging activists as terrorists are equally violations of international human rights laws as well,” Amnesty International-Philippines said in a social media post.

The group repeated the call to abolish the NTF-ELCAC as part of the human rights legislative agenda for the 20th Congress. In a press conference, Karapatan also called on the abolition of the task force for vilifying the victims of the April 19 massacre in Toboso, Negros Occidental and for continuously red-tagging individuals, organizations, and communities.

The UN OHCHR has yet to release a statement on this issue. (DAA)

title: Tuncer Bakirhan: Divê Îran dev ji êrişên li ser Kurdan berde û pirsgirêkê weke Sûriyê bi dîyalogê çareser bike
content:
Hevserokê Giştî yê Partiya Wekhevî û Demokrasiyê ya Gelan(DEM Partî) Tuncer Bakirhan têkildarî pêvajoya çareseriyê, gavên hiqûqî yên ku tên çaverêkirin were avêtin, vegera gerîlayên PKKyê û rola Abdullah Ocalan, bandora şerê Îranê ya li ser herêmê û yekîtiya Kurdan û Rojavayê, rola Herêma Kurdistanê, kongreya DEM Partiyê gelek mijarên din ji Rûdawê re axivî.


Tuncer Bakirhan li ser dema vegera gerîlayên PKKyê got ku ew li bendê ne qonaxên fermî dawiya meha Îlonê yan jî meha Cotmehê temam bibin.


Bakirhan diyar kir ku divê Hikûmeta Herêma Kurdistanê di pêvajoya vegera PKKyiyan de roleke girîng bilîze.


Bakirhan anî zimên ku aliyên hiqûqî, îdarî, lojîstîk û mirovî yên pêvajoyê eleqedarî Hewlêr, Silêmanî û Enqereyê ne.


Her weha Bakirhan bal kişand ser pêşhatên li Sûriye û Rojavayê jî û diyar kir ku divê piştgirî ji bo diyaloga di navbera hikûmeta Sûriyeyê û Kurdan de were dayîn.


Bakirhan diyar kir ku bi bicihanîna yasaya çarçoveyê re dê Selahattîn Demîrtaş, Fîgen Yuksekdag û gelek siyasetmedar ji nû ve tevlî jiyana siyasî bibin û anî zimên ku dê navên ku ji sirgûnê vegerin û kesên ji qadên cuda yên têkoşînê jî tevlî pêvajoyê bibin.


 Tuncer Bakirhan behsa nêrînên Ocalan ên ji bo êrişên Îranê û rewşa Herêma Kurdistanê jî kir. Her weha Bakirhan nêrînên Ocalan li ser çar xalan dabeş kir:


Divê nakokiyên di navbera Hewlêr û Silêmaniyê de li ser bingeha demokrasiyê bi dawî bibin û hikûmeteke navendî bê avakirin.


Di vê hikûmetê de divê mafê siyasetê û gotinê ji bo hemû hêzan hebe da ku Herêma Kurdistanê di hemberî êrişan de xurt bibe.


 Divê Îran êrişên li ser xaka Herêma Kurdistanê demildest rawestîne û dawî bi darvekirina Kurdan bîne.


 Divê Îran mafên Kurdan nas bike û Tirkiye jî roleke erênî bilîze. Ger Îran êrişan ranewestîne, ji bo Kurdan ji bilî parastina hevbeş a bi vîna xwe ti rêyeke din namîne.


Hevpeyvîna taybet a Hevserokê Giştî yê DEM Partiyê Tuncer Bakirhan a bi Rûdawê re weha ye:


“Pêvajo êdî di çarçoveyeke fermî de dimeşe”


Pêvajo êdî di çarçoveyeke fermî de dimeşe. Biryar di Rojnameya Fermî de hat weşandin, komîteya ku di yasayê de tê pêşbînîkirin bi serokatiya Alîkarê Serokkomar hat avakirin. Niha qonaxeke din a girîng heye: Biryara tesdîq-tesbîtê ya Komîteya Ewlehiya Neteweyî. Gava ku ev biryar di Rojnameya Fermî de were weşandin, yasa dê bi temamî bikeve meriyetê.


Ji niha ve dayîna demeke tekez ji bo vegeran ne rast e. Zehmet e ku mirov teqwîma pêvajoyeke ew qas hestyar bi dayîna rojan biaxive. Lê hemû nîşan nîşanî me didin ku dê ev qonaxên fermî dawiya meha Îlonê yan jî meha Çiriya Pêşîn temam bibin û yasa dê bikeve pratîkê. Bersiva pirsa "vegerên ewil dê kengî dest pê bikin" a ku her kes meraq dike jî bi vê teqwîmê ve girêdayî ye.


Li vir ez dixwazim bi taybetî balê bikişînim ser xalekê. Ji bo ku ev pêvajo bi awayekî tendurist bi rê ve biçe û hatin ewle û bi rêk û pêk bin, şert e ku Birêz Ocalan bi awayekî çalak di nav de be. Vê yekê tenê em nabêjin. Serkirdeyên PKKya hatiye fesixkirin jî bi israr heman rastiyê ducare dikin: Ew dibêjin heta ku Ocalan di nav de nebe ew nikarin banga "çekan deynin, vegerin" li ti hevalên xwe bikin. Her kesê ku pêwendiya di navbera PKK û Ocalan de dizane, dizane ku ev yek ji bo gotinê nayê gotin.


Pirs ev e: Birêz Ocalan îro di şert û mercên gelekî sînordar de hewl dide vê rolê bilîze. Ji bo vê yekê pêşniyara me zelal e: Komîteya Aştî û Siyasîbûnê ya ku Birêz Ocalan bikaribe rola xwe tê de bilîze divê demildest were avakirin. Rêya ku Birêz Ocalan bikaribe bi wateyeke rasteqîn di nav de be ev e. Gava ku ev komîte hat avakirin, em dikarin bi rehetî bibêjin ku dê hatinên hem ji çiyê û hem jî ji Ewropayê dest pê bikin.


“Hiqûqa li ser kaxezê, dişibe fêrbûna avjeniyê ya ji pirtûkê”


Bakirhan da zanîn ku pêşî divê were diyarkirin ku daxuyanî heta astekê tên fêmkirin û weha got:


Lê em vê jî dizanin: Daxuyanî wekî nan in. Dema teze bin digirin, heke werin rawestandin avahiya wan xera dibe û kes naxwe. Ez difikirim ku me qonaxên daxuyaniyan qismen derbas kirine. Yasaya ku li Parlamentoyê bi dengekî mezin hat qebûlkirin ji vî aliyî ve gelekî girîng e. Êdî ez ji bo derbasbûna ji niyetê ber bi pratîkê ve biqîmet dibînim.


Piraniya gavên şênber ên ku dê werin avêtin li qadên siyasî, hiqûqî, civakî û psîkolojîk belav dibin û ji bo beşeke girîng a wan pêwîstî bi nivîsandina bêhnokekê jî nîne. title: Eğitim Sen’den MEB genelgesine tepki: Eğitim tek tipleştiriliyor
content:
Milli Eğitim Bakanlığı'nın (MEB) 19 Ağustos'ta yayımladığı 2026/70 sayılı "2026-2027 Eğitim ve Öğretim Yılına İlişkin İş ve İşlemler" Genelgesi'ne Eğitim ve Bilim Emekçileri Sendikası'ndan (Eğitim Sen) tepki geldi.


Eğitim Sen, genelgenin "eğitimin kamusal, bilimsel, laik, çoğulcu ve demokratik niteliğini güçlendirmekten uzak" olduğunu belirterek, düzenlemelerin eğitim süreçlerini daha fazla merkezileştirdiğini ve öğretmenlerin mesleki özerkliğini sınırlandırdığını savundu.


Maarif Modeli eleştirisi


Açıklamada, Türkiye Yüzyılı Maarif Modeli'nin yalnızca öğretim programlarıyla sınırlı tutulmadığı; öğretmenlerin mesleki eğitiminden sosyal etkinliklere, okul dışı öğrenmeden dijital platformlara ve seçmeli derslere kadar okul yaşamının farklı alanlarına yayıldığı belirtildi.


Öğretmenlerin Öğretmen Bilişim Ağı (ÖBA) üzerinden hazırlanan Maarif Modeli eğitim paketlerinin tüm modüllerini tamamlamalarının istenmesine de tepki gösteren sendika, mesleki gelişimin Bakanlık politikalarının "tek yönlü aktarımı" şeklinde değil, öğretmenlerin ihtiyaçları ve bilimsel gelişmeler doğrultusunda, eğitim emekçilerinin katılımıyla planlanması gerektiğini söyledi.


MEB’den Ermeni okullarına “misafir öğrenci” denetimi


14 Ağustos 2026


"Çoğulculuk eğitim sisteminde yer almalı"


Genelgedeki "Köklerden Geleceğe" yaklaşımına da değinen Eğitim Sen, Türk dünyası ve "gönül coğrafyası" üzerinden ortak tarih, kültür ve medeniyet birikiminin öğrencilere benimsetilmesinin istendiğini aktardı.


Sendika, çocukların farklı tarih ve kültürleri öğrenmesinin değerli olduğunu ancak bunların belirli bir kültürel kimlik ve siyasal perspektifle sunulmasına itiraz etti.


Türkiye'nin çok dilli, çok kültürlü ve çok kimlikli toplumsal yapısına dikkat çeken Eğitim Sen; Kürtçe, Arapça, Ermenice, Rumca, Gürcüce, Lazca, Çerkes dilleri ve diğer halkların dil, kültür ve tarihlerinin çoğulcu bir eğitim anlayışı içinde yer almasını ve çocukların anadilinde eğitim hakkının güvence altına alınmasını istedi.


Bakanlığın haber platformuna eleştiri


Eğitim Sen'in eleştirdiği başlıklardan biri de medya okuryazarlığı oldu.


Sendika, genelgede öğrencilerin eleştirel düşünme ve medya okuryazarlığı becerilerinin geliştirilmesinden söz edilirken Bakanlığın hazırladığı "Haberimiz Olsun" platformundaki içeriklerin derslerde kullanılmasının öngörülmesini çelişkili buldu.


Medya okuryazarlığının Bakanlığın belirlediği haberlerin öğrencilere aktarılması anlamına gelmediğini belirten sendika, öğrencilerin farklı haber kaynaklarını karşılaştırabilmesi, kaynakları sorgulayabilmesi ve propaganda ile manipülasyon yöntemlerini tanıyabilmesi gerektiğini ifade etti.


MEB yönetmeliği değişti: Okul yönetimlerine arama yetkisi verildi


29 Temmuz 2026


Önlük uygulaması: "Mesleğin saygınlığı kıyafetle sağlanmaz"


Açıklamada öğretmenlerin önlük giymesinin istenmesi ve uygulamanın milli eğitim müdürlükleri tarafından takip edilecek olması da eleştirildi.


Eğitim Sen, öğretmenlik mesleğinin saygınlığının kıyafetle değil; öğretmene verilen toplumsal değer, ekonomik ve özlük hakları, mesleki özerklik ve demokratik çalışma koşullarıyla sağlanabileceğini belirtti.


Norm fazlası öğretmenler


Genelgede norm kadro fazlası öğretmenlerin herhangi bir takvime bağlı olmadan ihtiyaç bulunan eğitim kurumlarına atanması, kendisine ders görevi verilemeyen öğretmenlerin ise Milli Eğitim Akademisi'nde eğitime alınarak öğretmen ihtiyacı bulunan "diğer alanlarda" görevlendirilmesi öngörülüyor.


Eğitim Sen, bu düzenlemenin öğretmenlerin eğitim aldıkları branşların dışında görevlendirilmelerinin önünü açabileceğini savundu. Öğretmen açığının farklı branşlarda görevlendirmelerle değil, ihtiyaç bulunan alanlara yeterli sayıda kadrolu öğretmen atanarak giderilmesi gerektiğini belirtti.


Sendika ayrıca norm fazlası sorununun yanlış norm planlaması, değiştirilen ders çizelgeleri, okul dönüşümleri ve Bakanlığın istihdam politikalarıyla bağlantılı olduğunu ifade etti. 


Dijital platformlar ve öğrenci verileri


Açıklamada Yeni EBA, MEBİ, OGM Materyal, HEMBA, Velivizyon ve yapay zekâ destekli DİLİM gibi Bakanlık platformlarının yaygınlaştırılması da değerlendirildi.


Eğitim Sen, dijital teknolojilerin eğitimde kullanılmasına karşı olmadığını ancak öğrenci ve öğretmen verilerinin hangi amaçlarla kullanılacağı, ne kadar süre saklanacağı, kimlerle paylaşılacağı ve yapay zekâ sistemlerinde nasıl değerlendirileceğinin açık ve denetlenebilir olması gerektiğini belirtti.

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: International humanitarian law violated in Toboso massacre, fact-finding concludes
content:
Sitio Plaringding, barangay Salamanca, Toboso, Negros Occidental. (Photo by Anne Marxze D. Umil/Bulatlat)

MANILA – After four months, the National Fact-Finding and Solidarity Mission (NFFSM) released the findings of its investigation on the killing of 19 people in Toboso, Negros Occidental last April 19 which revealed serious violations of international humanitarian law.

“It was clear: the path of retreating civilians and revolutionaries is a dead end,” said Matty Miguel, convenor of Defend Negros, in a press conference on Wednesday, August 19. “The military can distinguish who among the individuals are combatants, civilians, and those incapacitated, but they killed them all.”

At least nine of the 19 people killed were civilians, including minors. Ten, on the other hand, are revolutionaries.

The report of the fact-finding team was based on the interviews of the residents of sitio Sinugmawan and sitio Plaringding and series of visits to the communities in Toboso and actual observations of the members of the fact-finding mission. The groups involved in the fact-finding also participated in the public inquiry organized by the Commission on Human Rights, which concluded on August 12.

Cristina Palabay, secretary general of human rights group Karapatan, said, “Negros 19 is the biggest single mass casualty involving international humanitarian law violations that we have documented and looked into in the recent years. This merits not only continuing attention but also continuing push for justice.”

The fact-finding report concluded that the Philippine Army violated Articles 48 and 57 of the Protocol I to the Geneva Conventions, which refer to the principle of distinction and proportionality. The Philippines ratified the Geneva Conventions, which refers to the set of international treaties that establish the rules of war through IHL.

Article 48 reads, “The Parties to the conflict shall at all times distinguish between the civilian population and combatants and between civilian objects and military objectives and accordingly shall direct their operations only against military objectives.”

Meanwhile, Article 57 of the Conventions, states that those who plan or decide upon an attack shall do everything feasible to ensure that the objectives to be attacked are neither civilians nor civilian objects are not subject to special protection. The only valid attack is targeted at military objectives – capacitated revolutionaries. The minor casualties in Toboso 19 massacre are considered specially protected persons of the rules of war.

Another violation is the targeting of armed combatants who were no longer in a position to fight back or hors de combat, the fact-finding report noted. The safeguards of hors de combat are outlined in the Article 41 of Additional Protocol I (1977) to the 1949 Geneva Conventions.

“A person who is recognized or who, in the circumstances, should be recognized to be ‘hors de combat’ shall not be made the object of attack,” the provision reads.

The report highlighted that the government soldiers were strategically positioned uphill in such a way that they had an unobstructed view of the fleeing individuals. The NPA revolutionaries could be identified within the range of soldiers’ high velocity firearms.

The mission report added that the site where civilians and revolutionaries were shot is a fishpond, with waist-deep muddy waters. It stated: “They were not in a position to inflict any harm on the soldiers, who were well protected by their strategic positions.By reason of their condition, the armed NPA members had transitioned into hors de combat and could have been easily captured. But the intention was obvious.”

Palabay said that this practice of “no quarters given” is prohibited not only under the Geneva Conventions, but also with the domestic IHL policy of the Philippines. It is considered a war crime under Section 4 of Republic Act 9851.

“Those incapacitated, both hors de combat and civilians, should be given temporary aid instead of being strafed with bullets,” Palabay added. “This is proof of the take no prisoners policy of this administration.”

A drone footage also captured Roger Fabiliar, one of the NPA revolutionary casualties, was submerged in a fishpond, unarmed, and as the report noted “clearly posing no imminent threat.”

A woman’s body had four gunshot wounds, including a gunshot wound to the leg that caused fatal bleeding, based on the autopsy of forensic pathologist Raquel Fortun …

author: Act for freedom now!
title: Sabotage Against the CEA in Cadarache (France)
content:
Bouches-du-Rhône: Sabotage Against the CEA in Cadarache

On the night of Sunday, May 17, 2026, we sawed through a pylon on the 400,000-volt power line supplying the CEA [French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission] in Cadarache. Unfortunately, there was no short circuit.

A significant chapter in the history of French nuclear power was written in Cadarache. It was there that the nuclear propulsion systems for nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarines — the flagship of France’s nuclear deterrent — were developed. Today, the site is home to the ITER project, a nuclear fusion research initiative that hopes to make us swallow the myth of clean, renewable, and infinite energy.

We’ll be told that this action is dangerous, but it is the day-to-day normality of nuclear power that poses the real danger. To avoid any risk of an accident, we have left the other power line supplying the site intact; the site also has its own hydroelectric dam.

The media has kept silent on our action. We would like to take this opportunity to greet all those who are fighting against nuclear power. We are taking advantage of the last days of spring to join the campaign “Hotter Than Nuclear – For a Black Spring in 2026” and greet the other groups that have answered the call. Our thoughts go out to the evicted Gare collective and all those fighting against Cigéo. From basic research to waste disposal — down with the nuclear industry!

In memory of Sara and Sandro, who live on in the struggle!

title: Ephéméride des luttes : 21 août
content:
Le 21 août, l'éphéméride des luttes cherche à détruire les chaînes de l'esclavage et de l'exploitation pour que tous et toutes soient libres. Par le feu et par la poudre, pour faire tomber les murs.


1680 :

 Dans ce qui est aujourd'hui le Nouveau Mexique, le peuple Pueblo s'empare de la ville de Santa Fe et en chassent les colons espagnols, lors de la révolte des Pueblo.


1791 :

 Début de la révolte des esclaves Noirs de Saint-Domingue.


1852 :

 En Amérique du Nord, les Indien-ne-s Tlingit détruisent le Fort Selkirk, sur le territoire du Yukon.


1967 :

 A Londres, le Mouvement de Solidarité Révolutionnaire International mitraille l'ambassade américaine.


1968 :

 Les chars soviétiques pénètrent en Tchécoslovaquie pour y réimposer l'ordre.


1971 :

 Prison de San Quentin, aux États-Unis, George Jackson (du Black Panther Party, auteur des 'Frères de Soledad') est abattu par des gardes. Ceux-ci l'accusent d'avoir été en train d'essayer de s'évader de la prison.


1976 :

 Aux Etats-Unis, début d'une occupation de deux jours de la centrale nucléaire de Seabrook.


1981 :

 Dans le Tarn-et-Garonne, à Goudourville, le groupe Colt 45 (Coordination Ouvrière pour la Liquidation des Travaux) revendique le fait d'avoir tiré plusieurs balles contre le domicile du chef de chantier du projet de centrale nucléaire de Golfech, alors que la maison était vide.


« Pourquoi un attentat chez M. Silberstein ? C'est la confusion général à Golfech : le gel de la centrale est décidé à Paris mais les travaux continuent sur le site ; les entrepreneurs risquent de perdre quelques contrats mais ce sont les ouvriers qui manifestent et assurent la défense des intérêts patronaux. Dans cette incroyable pagaille, M. Silberstein reste lucide, il arrive même à distinguer “une dizaine d'ouvriers excités par une éventuelle perte d'emploi”. Il comprend, il vient même à justifier leurs exactions contre les antinucléaires : menace contre les occupants de la Rotonde ; cassage de gueules, voitures saccagées et brûlées, tracteur incendié le 16 août. Mais les responsables d'EDF se trompent s'ils croient que nous allons nous préoccuper de quelques castagneurs et les oublier, eux, qui tirent les ficelles… Erreur… Erreur qui pourrait devenir fatale… »


2009 :

 A Rovolon, près de Padoue en Italie, l'ALF (Front de Libération Animale) incendie une villa, la remise à outils, la fourgonnette, le tracteur et plusieurs véhicules de propriétaires d'un élevage de visons, faisant plus de 100.000 euros de dégâts.


Voir

 du 21 août.

title: Berlin (Germany): Vehicles Belonging to a War Profiteer Set on Fire
content:
A Fiery Disarmament Measure at Telekom!

“Arms manufacturing is a new business sector that Deutsche Telekom intends to develop, and in which it sees strong growth potential.”

What Deutsche Telekom CEO Tim Höttges refers to here as “growth potential” means nothing other than: war is a lucrative business, and the company wants its share of the pie. With the development of IT services for defense and security agencies, this semi-public company has long embodied the intertwining of civilian and military technologies.

But this new push into the arms market takes on a distinctly new dimension, and Deutsche Telekom thus finds itself in excellent company. Germany wants to prepare for war, and in this context, its struggling industrial sector is indeed shifting its focus toward defense. For example, tanks are expected to roll off the production lines soon at the Volkswagen plant in Osnabrück and at the Alstom rail manufacturer in Görlitz, while Rheinmetall plans to begin production of corresponding artillery ammunition as early as July at the former Pierburg plant in Wedding. For its part, Telekom plans to develop, in collaboration with Rheinmetall, a defense shield against drones. Through its 2-billion-euro technology fund, the company is also acquiring a stake in the defense technology startup Quantum Systems, which builds autonomous combat and surveillance drones.

We cannot let all this go unanswered: that’s why, last night, we reduced Deutsche Telekom’s vehicle fleet by six cars in Berlin’s Alt-Hohenschönhausen neighborhood. They didn’t count on us. We refuse to give up our neighborhoods for their weapons production, nor do we want to die on the front lines as cannon fodder for the rulers.

Solidarity greetings to the Ulm 5 and to all the other anti-militarists whom the cops have been harassing lately! Against all war—Against all genocide! Fuck military service—Fuck the Bundeswehr [German army]! Let’s attack militarization and the dystopia of AI surveillance! And as always: Let’s defend Rigaer94!

You have the power, we have the night!

title: Carl Ahlteen - Gruvarbetarsträjken i norra Minnesota
content:
Författare

: Carl Ahlteen

Titel

: Gruvarbetarsträjken i norra Minnesota

Källa

: Allarm augusti, oktober 1916


 För några år sedan gick den beryktade sträjken i Colorado av stapeln.


 En oändlig massa oskyldiga slavande män, kvinnor och barn fingo släppa till livet på grund av kapitalets blodtörst. Här i de norra staterna skakade man på huvudet och uttryckte sin dom, att det är endast i södern sådant kan försiggå. Nu är samma brottsligheter upprepade häruppe. Samma blodtörstiga kapital som ej skydde några medel att krossa de förtryckta gruvarbetarna i Colorado äro här nu och använda samma sätt som å den förut nämnda platsen.


 Det meddelas nämligen att över 2000 "gunmen" äro däruppe med orders att kväva varje försök till frigörelse. Gruvarbetarna äro så långt som kan ses till datum fast beslutna att vinna sträjken.


 Från "Strikers News", en tillfällig tidning utgiven och spridd av gruvarbetarna för att få den rätta situationen fram för publiken, meddelar huru beklagliga förhållanden äro däruppe. Det mest utvecklade slag av svindleri som kan tänkas har försiggått där.


 Unga ogifta män ha genom att bjuda basen på sprit o. dy. kunnat erhålla rätt goda shackt under det att de gifta männen ha måst nöja sig med de allra sämsta. Ja, det har gått t. o. m. så långt att basarna ha haft gifta män att arbeta upp ett schackt och när det kommit i sådant skick att där har varit möjlighet att förvärva ett lite bättre daglön än förut, så har basen sålt shacktet till någon som givit honom så högt som till 60 dollars för densamma. Tänk över en dylik situation.


 En man med hustru och barn att försörga har att gå till verket och arbeta upp ett shackt på vilket han ej tjänat mera än $1.50-$1.75, ja många ha fått gå till och med så långt som under en dollar per dag. En vacker dag när han fått shackten upparbetad går basen och säljer hans arbetsplats till någon annan. Dubbel stöld! Först bestjäl ståltrusten dessa tusentals arbetare på hundradetals miljoner varje år, så komma efter detta stora rövareband (basar) f. d. eller rättare arbetare och bestjäl dem ånyo.


 Ja flera av dessa basar ha t. o. m. gått så långt i sina oförskämdheter att de tvingat sig till "samlag" med de gifta kvinnorna så att mannen haft vetskap därom och basarna ha förstått att få dem att tiga genom hotelser att bliva avskedade.


 Av det ovannämnda kan varje sansad människa förstå att sträjken är till sitt yttersta berättigad.


 Sent, ja alldeles försent räta slavarna på sina krökta ryggar och skaka av sig ohyran - kapitalisterna och dess hejdukar.


 Ståltrusten - det allkontrollerande vidundret, har givetvis presat de privata affärsmännen däruppe så, att dessa ej skola lämna ut matvaror på kredit till de sträjkande för att på detta sätt få bukt på dem.


 Fäster o. dy. har arrangerats runt här till förmån för de stridande kamraterna men mera är av behovet påkallat. Kommen ihåg kamrater att det är mot ståltrusten dessa kamrater strida. Det fordras att vi alla göra vårt till för att i den mån möjligheterna tillåta såra "besten". Många och täta sår skall nog förkorta livet. Samtidigt som en uppmaning göres till att hjälpa dessa stridande däruppe, bör vi ej känna oss försvarade just med att vi hjälpt dem, utan tvärtom känna en skyldighet mot oss som människor, att gripa verket an och i organiserad grupp storma och slutligen tillintetgöra detta odjur, vars makt och blodtörst tilltager för varje dag under det att vi försvagas.


 I forna tider drogo de svärd mot sina förtryckare och höllo dem på vederbörligt avstånd, nu kyssa slavarna under en ödmjuk suck förtryckarnas sparkande fot.


 En blygsamhetens känsla borde spåras i edra anleten ni slavar i det 20 århundradet som fördraga att stå oorganiserade eller just bärande ett medlemskort i fickan och ej verka för den gemensamma saken: arbetarklassens befrielse. Ni må nu kalla det utvecklad intelligent individualism, eller kristen slaviskhet, det är

opassande fegt och uselt.


Fram

 för handling om den revolutionära arbetarklassens vackra mening

lika rätt och frihet åt alla

 skall

bliva en verklighet.


 Ståltrustens blodiga tand är ännu i verksamhet i gruvdistriktet. Kapitalisttidningar, präster, politiker m. m. sålda åt kapitalet, göra allt för sprida missmod bland massorna. Lögner spridas sådana som att sträjken är över och arbetet i full gång m. m.


 Trots allt detta stå arbetarna orubbligt eniga tillsammans och fast beslutna att strida till sista man. Sträjken däruppe är ingen barnlek utan en strid …

author: Unknown
title: Walfrid Engdahl - Medel i klasskampen
content:
Författare

: Walfrid Engdahl

Titel

: Medel i klasskampen

Källa

: Allarm oktober 1916


 En fråga uppstår ofta för mig vilka medel vi böra använda i klasskampen. Då jag ju är arbetare, tillhör jag underklassen och känner med en arbetares känslor och tänker från arbetarens synpunkt.


 Som vanligt då man försöker tänka mötas motsägelser och hinder, dessa andliga gärdesgårdar som ofta äro så hårda att överkomma. Det första hindret är mig då själva ordet: klasskamp. Vi kämpa för vår klass, arbetarklassen. Men det är ju en klass, som vi vill ha bort? Vi vill ju göra en ända på alla klasser, båda, klasserna, rika och fattiga? Är det meningen, som så många tänkare synes fatta det, att vi vilja dra ned de rike till fattigdomens nivå, göra alla fattiga? Knappast! Vi vilja allas rikedom och lycka, nej, arbete, det valda arbetet, som är den högsta lyckan. Ordet klasskamp har endast en halv betydelse, vilken äger logisk bärkraft i nuets och dagens strider. Men det är ju dock i nuet vi leva och röra oss och så tvingas vi ta det sådant det är.


 Ta vi så av oss framtidsdrömmarnas kåpa och stiga in i nuet, se vi verkligen en väldig kamp försiggå, och hur den föres med ojämna vapen. Det är striden om en klass bevarande och om dess fall, som klass sedd; det är arbetets kamp mot lättjan, lyxan och det oförskämda överflödet. Det är arbetet som vill bana sig väg upp till samhällets höjd, dess självskrivna och naturliga plats, det är nyttan som vill trampa onyttan under sina fötter och inta dess, sedan långa tider, kvarhållna previlegierade ställning. Naturligtvis kastar jag på mig rustning, griper mina vapen och inregistrerar mig i arbetets och nyttans här.


 Om mitt vapen bär en rostfläck kan det hugga lika bra, och om mina medel äro civiliserade, därpå har jag ingen tid att grunda. Jag ser fienden stå med högt hugg, som måttats mot mitt huvud; jag skyndar mig parera och ge ett dödshugg i stället. Om min rörelse ej är så graciös, så sitter vapnet säkert i grov och hårdnad hand och det är ändamålet jag är efter.


 "Men ändamålet hälgar väl inte medlet?" Visst gör det dä'! Det är mig absolut likgiltigt vad medel jag griper, endast jag hinner till makt och seger med mina intressen. Hjälper mig ett knytnävslag ger jag bort det; hjälper mig en lögn, så ljuger jag, och hjälper mig en ärlig strid eller ett lagbrott, så gör jag användning av dem.


 Jag vill ingen ängel vara, utan en krigare. Jag bär uniform och är soldat i det nyttiga arbetets här. Min uniform är lik de andras klädedräkter; men jag är ej uniform med deras sinnen.


 Till min egen klass, inom min egen här får jag ingen lögn spridas, och till fiendens här får ingen sanning spridas. Med fiender talar man ej, med dem slåss man, och man har vanligen ingen skonsamhet heller. Angripas de under det de såva eller anfallas de bakifrån; det är kanske ej så hederligt, men vad gör det, då vi äro säkrare om segern!


 Våra fiender förgiftade maten och kloroformerade oss till ständig sömn, och så ha de gått an att anfalla oss tills vi lågo besegrade under deras fötter. Det kunde endast ske genom gift och sömn, att en blev herre och nittionio slogos till hans fötter.


 Innan arbetarna frågar sig huruvida deras medel äro civiliserade eller ej, borde de undersöka överklassens. En sådan undersökning toge ej lång tid, och borde redan vara känd, de ha ju sårats av dessa varenda stund. Vi skola välja medlen, och välja dem som är bäst för oss och gör fienden den största skadan. Ibland är en undervattensbåt bättre än det största och stoltaste slagskepp.


 Varför skall jag så respekterae överklassen att jag förnekar mig själv, under det de förneka sig själva ingenting, men mig allt.


 Här i denna lilla stad på högst 2,000 invånare ha vi 3 olika banker. Bankörerna gå i snygga gångkläder - jag i trasiga "overalls". Deras arbete är fint och valkar ej deras händer - mitt gör mig smutsig och grov. De ha 2 a tre automobiler; ja de köper en ny och dyrbarare varenda vår - jag får gå och tjänar knappast nog till ett par skor, då de behövas. De ha vackra hem, vackra välklädda barn och hustrur - jag får hyra mig in i ett litet rum, äger ej medel till ett hem, äger ej pängar nog att försörja hustru och barn. De äta utsökt mat och härliga delikatesser - jag får vara nöjd, betala dyrt och äta vad som de rata. De ta emot andra människors besparingar, för vilka de betala 3 a 4 proc. ränta, och låna deras pängar sedan ut till de fattiga behövande från 10 till över 60 proc. ränta - jag får gå till dem och …

author: Alexandra Bradbury
title: New Voices Gain Ground at Letter Carriers Convention
content:
“The number one takeaway is that the times in the NALC, they are a-changing,” said Margo O’Neill of Branch 352 in Des Moines, Iowa, who attended her first Letter Carriers convention August 3-7 in Los Angeles.


“It was quite different than any convention that I’ve been to,” said retiree activist Jamie Partridge of Branch 82 in Portland, Oregon, who has been attending since 1988. “There were many competing factions and five times as many constitutional amendments as have been offered in the past, and many more resolutions, which I attribute to the uprising against the current leadership.”


President Brian Renfroe was already in hot water at the last convention. He had been negotiating in such secrecy that even the rest of the executive council was kept in the dark; when he took a months-long leave for alcoholism treatment, he left no bargaining notes.


But discontent really boiled over afterwards, when Renfroe came out with a tentative deal. Members were furious at the

low raises

 and continued two-tier, and voted it down; Renfroe agreed to most of it anyway and rushed the economic parts into arbitration, citing Trump’s attacks. A

near-identical contract

 was imposed.


The union will elect a new president this fall, from a field of four candidates. After months of speculation, Renfroe announced at the convention that he isn’t running again. Delegates cheered.


“I think that eased a lot of people’s minds, and also helped sharpen the dialogue about how this isn’t just about Renfroe,” said John Murphy of Branch 4716 in Naples, Florida. “We’ve gotta move forward, get some checks and balances. The younger members want their voices to be heard. They want more transparency, they want more democracy, they want more say.”


“We’re clearly rapidly expanding what democracy looks like in our union,” said Derek Liemohn of Branch 34 in Boston. “It would be a stretch to call this a winning convention for the reformers. But this was, I think, the strongest that independent reform politics has ever looked” in the NALC.


HOMELESS IN SEATTLE


The latest contract expired in May, and the union and management went through a required mediation period this summer. Interest arbitration is expected next, but delegates didn’t get any update on the proposals or timeline.


In the week’s biggest surprise, convention delegates bucked the executive council’s recommendation and approved (1,909 to 1,781) a resolution committing the union to lobbying for a wage boost in areas with a higher cost of living, like federal workers get.


“We had old guys coming up to us and saying they had been trying to get this passed since the 1980s,” said C Moline of Branch 79 in Seattle. “This was a huge win that none of us expected this go-round.”


Letter carrier pay is tiered by hire date and job type, but not by location. The union’s longstanding position is that bargaining a local differential would pit the interests of some carriers against others.


However, carriers in Alaska, Hawaii, and Puerto Rico already get a “Territorial COLA” allocated by Congress. The resolution calls for locality pay within the continental U.S. to be accomplished the same way.


“Some of our carriers have ended up homeless because they can’t afford rent in Seattle,” Moline said in an impassioned

speech

 on the convention floor, drawing applause. “This is the way we can do it and not use any of our bargaining power. This is legislative.”


PARTICIPATION OVERLOAD


Some proposed constitutional amendments were clearly inspired by the recent contract debacle, such as requiring the president to keep the executive council briefed on bargaining progress, and preventing the union from making a deal without a member vote.


Resolutions ran the gamut from contract demands, like $30-an-hour starting pay and an end to two-tier, to political positions, like opposing the war with Iran.


Most of these efforts failed, but some modest reforms did pass. Future union conventions will be livestreamed, as this one was. The president will be required to keep written records of bargaining proposals.


Under NALC rules, any resolution or constitutional amendment submitted in time by a branch (the union’s equivalent of a local) or state association was heard by the 5,000 delegates.


Proposals where the executive council recommended a “yes” were batched together. Those the council opposed were taken one by one, in a confusing process where delegates would have to vote “no” on the council …

author: Dennis Ward
title: Treaty #3 says parole board must address ‘systemic failures’ after granting full parole to man who killed Barbara Kentner
content:
The

Grand Council of Treaty #3

 in Ontario is the latest organization to come out and condemn the Parole Board of Canada for granting Brayden Bushby full parole.


Bushby was convicted of manslaughter for throwing a trailer hitch that killed Barbara Kentner, 34, of Wabigoon Lake Ojibway Nation. Kentner was walking down a Thunder Bay street with her sister when Bushby threw the hitch from a moving vehicle.


Four years later, Bushby was convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to seven years and 11 months. It included 10-year weapons prohibition.


“Grand Council Treaty #3 fully supports Wabigoon Lake Ojibway Nation Chief and Council in their call for justice and accountability,” said a statement released on Thursday. “The decision to grant full parole to the person responsible for Barbara’s death is a miscarriage of justice and sends an unacceptable message to our people,” said Ogichidaa Francis Kavanaugh in the statement.


The Treaty #3 statement comes a day after Wabigoon Lake Ojibway Nation said that Kentner’s death “was not an isolated tragedy” but a reflection of the “racism and violence that Indigenous people endure daily.”


“The granting of full parole to her attacker,” the statement continued, “sends a devastating message that Indigenous lives are treated as expendable.”


Barbara Kentner was struck with a trailer hitch while out walking with her sister in 2017. Photo: APTN file


The Assembly of First Nations (AFN), a lobby group that represents more than 600 First Nations in Canada, said that Bushby’s history while on parole should have been taken into account.


“Bushby committed a horrific act of targeted brutality and has a history of parole breaches and a pattern of high-risk behaviour,” said a statement from National Chief Cindy Woodhouse Nepinak on Thursday. “I am heartbroken for the friends and family of Barbara Kentner and the people of Wabigoon Lake Ojibway First Nation. This decision sends the wrong message about the value the criminal justice system places on the lives of First Nations women in Canada.”


On the Truth and Politics panel on APTN National News, Niigaan Sinclair said, “If this is a non-Indigenous woman or male, this is a much different story. If this is a killing in Toronto, it’s a much different story.”


“Because it’s in Thunder Bay, because it’s an Indigenous victim, this gets a scant amount of attention,” said Sinclair who added “when it comes to the murder of Indigenous peoples, as we know within the situations in Saskatchewan and Manitoba, no one is held to account.”


Panelist Jennifer Laewetz said the granting of full parole to Bushby sets a dangerous precedent.


“I’m just really concerned about this and at what point we’re going to start valuing not just human life but Indigenous lives as well because that’s part of the layered problem here is that people will maybe not view this as serious as it should be because there is already a crisis in our country on people not valuing our lives,” said Laewetz.


Watch the Truth and Politics Panel with host Dennis Ward 


According to the parole board documents on its decision, “the Board determines a release on full parole now will not pose undue risk and the release will contribute to the protection of society by facilitating your reintegration back into society as a law-abiding citizen…”


Bushby had previously been granted day parole in 2023. In 2024, it was revoked due to Bushby being in breach of several conditions. He was found in possession of contraband including a vape pen and juice and a knife fashioned into a screwdriver during a search in April 2023. He had also consumed alcohol and associated with a woman known to police and involved in the drug subculture.


Perhaps more concerning were his “attitude and use of symbols,” the board noted. Bushby obtained a tattoo of a Confederate flag, which the parole board said is “widely considered a racist symbol. His explanation for the tattoo was not found credible by staff.”


Bushby was also “identified as an instigator” in cutting a swastika into the lawn where he was residing, leading to a temporary transfer back to medium security.


“To add insult to injury, while in custody and in the community, you continued to demonstrate attitudes indicative of being racist and [of]arrogance,” the board said.

author: Veridiana Alimonti
title: Intermediary Liability in Brazil: The Intricate Path Ahead
content:
Brazil's new internet intermediary liability regime is underway. The implementation of

changes

 established by the Supreme Court includes notice and takedown mechanisms and duty of care obligations. Caution is crucial as these measures can create problematic incentives for

enforcement overreach

 and

over censorship

 of protected speech.

 


The court in June issued a new decision

clarifying elements

 of its 2025 finding that the previous liability regime was partially unconstitutional. The government also published in late May two presidential decrees that detail how the new rules apply.

 


Under the new regime, social media platforms and other internet applications that curate or interfere with posts can be held liable for third-party content if they don’t remove it after being notified by the user seeking take down unless there's a reasonable doubt that the content is unlawful. For certain specific cases, like crimes against honor (e.g. defamation), platform liability still depends on failing to comply with a judicial order.

 


For some serious crimes, like human trafficking and crimes against women, applications have a

duty of care

 to remove related content immediately and can be held liable when systemically failing to do so. The precise limits of what constitutes a systemic failure are still unclear. There are also stricter rules for paid ads, boosted content, and bots.

 


The previous regime, set by Article 19 of the

law

 known as the Brazilian Civil Rights Framework for the Internet (“Marco Civil da Internet” in Portuguese), sought to protect freedom of expression online by holding internet application providers liable for user content if they failed to comply with a judicial order to remove it. There were specific, limited exceptions to this rule, like the unauthorized disclosure of nude or private sexual images. This was meant to prevent providers from over-removal of user content to avoid legal action. Yet, the court found that this provision failed to sufficiently safeguard democracy and fundamental rights.

 


We

outlined

 the thorny context leading to this shift in Brazil’s intermediary liability rules, including Big Tech’s alignment with the far right and hurdles to approve platform regulation in Congress, through a proper legislative process.

 


Brazil’s shift is part of broader

discussions

 and

changes

 in response to growing concerns over online harms and digital platforms’ abuses. However, responses focused on platforms’ liability of user-generated content carry

important traps and risks

—from entrenching dominant platforms’ power over the information flow to escalating arbitrary online surveillance and censorship. The path ahead must prevent this to the extent possible, and the new presidential decrees provide a mixed contribution towards this task.

 


New Decrees: Strengths and Flaws

 


The government published two decrees regulating the new regime set by the Supreme Court.

One

introduces changes

 to its

previous regulation, the

Decree 8.771/2016

, detailing elements of the decision, including additional duties that the court only briefly addressed (Decree 12.975). The other regulates measures to

tackle violence against women online

 (Decree 12.976).

 


The Supreme Court's decision didn't establish guidelines to protect users' due process rights when facing content take down and removal demands. Instead, it relies on providers to self regulate, which could lead to over censorship.

 


The decrees’ provisions on user notification systems are helpful in this sense. They stipulate that providers must inform users (both the notifier and the content author) about the decision to remove or keep the content up, why, and the means to appeal. The guidance makes explicit that a platform may reconsider and reinstate content after an appeal and must explain its reasons to the party requesting removal and content author. The decrees also address concerns with the weaponization of notification systems, establishing that internet applications must adopt measures to prevent abuses.

 


Decree 12.795 reinforces that applications can keep content up after notification when there’s reasonable doubt that the post is unlawful, stating that the analysis should consider the context of the publications, freedom of religion and belief, and any informational, educational, or critical, satirical, or parodic purpose with the aim of ensuring freedom of expression.
